translation: 彼女は以前、そこへよく行くのだと彼に話したことがあった。それで彼は、空いた時間を、ひょっとするとつい先ほどまで彼女がいたかもしれないと思える場所で過ごしてみたくなったのだった。
point: 後半の a place where … の where は関係副詞、a fancy to spend は形容詞的用法の不定詞。判定するのは前半の主節。
explanation: tell 人 that節 で、him と that節が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン
workJa: エイジ・オブ・イノセンス

text: A formidable array of bottles and test-tubes, with the pungent cleanly smell of hydrochloric acid, told me that he had spent his day in the chemical work which was so dear to him.
translation: ずらりと並んだ瓶と試験管、それに塩酸の鼻をつく清潔なにおいから、彼がその日一日を大好きな化学の実験に費やしていたことがわかった。
parts: A formidable array of bottles and test-tubes
with the pungent cleanly smell of hydrochloric acid
that he had spent his day in the chemical work which was so dear to him
point: 無生物主語の文。「瓶と試験管の列が私に告げた」は「～から私にはわかった」と訳すと自然。
explanation: tell 人 that節 で、me と that節が2つの目的語なので SVOO。that節の中の spent his day は SVO、which was so dear to him は SVC。
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorJa: アーサー・コナン・ドイル
workJa: シャーロック・ホームズの冒険

text: The official detective was attired in a pea-jacket and cravat, which gave him a decidedly nautical appearance, and he carried a black canvas bag in his hand.
target: which gave him a decidedly nautical appearance
translation: その警察の刑事はピージャケットにクラヴァットという出で立ちで、そのせいでいかにも船乗りらしく見えた。手には黒い帆布の鞄を提げていた。
point: 非制限用法の which（＝ピージャケットとクラヴァット）が関係詞節の主語。
explanation: give 人 物 で、him と a decidedly nautical appearance が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorJa: アーサー・コナン・ドイル
workJa: シャーロック・ホームズの冒険

text: Stryver sucked the end of a ruler for a little while, and then stood hitting a tune out of his teeth with it, which probably gave him the toothache.
target: which probably gave him the toothache
translation: ストライヴァーはしばらく定規の端をしゃぶっていたが、やがて立ったまま、それで歯をたたいて調子をとりはじめた。おそらくそのせいで歯が痛くなったことだろう。
point: この which の先行詞は名詞ではなく、前の「定規で歯をたたいたこと」という内容全体。
explanation: give 人 the toothache（人に歯痛を与える）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: A man, dressed like a game-keeper, came up at the moment, and he handed him a basket which lay ready on the pavement.
target: he handed him a basket which lay ready on the pavement
translation: ちょうどそのとき猟場番のような身なりの男がやって来たので、彼は歩道に用意して置いてあった籠をその男に手渡した。
parts: which lay ready on the pavement
point: 関係詞節の lay ready（用意された状態で置かれていた）は lie＋形容詞の SVC。主節と関係詞節で文型が違う。
explanation: hand 人 物（人に物を手渡す）で、him と a basket が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: I had a single little pearl ornament which Miss Temple gave me as a parting keepsake: I put it on, and then we went downstairs.
target: which Miss Temple gave me as a parting keepsake
translation: 私はテンプル先生が別れの記念にくださった小さな真珠の飾りを一つだけ持っていた。それを身につけてから、私たちは階下へ下りた。
point: 目的格の関係代名詞 which は gave の2つ目の目的語（物）。語順を戻すと Miss Temple gave me which（＝the ornament）。
explanation: 関係代名詞が目的語の位置から前に出ているだけで、give 人 物 の SVOO。主節 I had a single little pearl ornament は SVO。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Iron gates between granite pillars showed me where to enter, and passing through them, I found myself at once in the twilight of close-ranked trees.
target: Iron gates between granite pillars showed me where to enter
translation: 花崗岩の門柱のあいだの鉄の門が入り口を教えてくれた。そこを通り抜けると、私はたちまち、びっしりと並んだ木々の薄暗がりの中にいた。
point: 疑問詞＋to不定詞 where to enter は名詞句で、2つ目の目的語になる。
explanation: show 人 物 で、me と where to enter が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Zillah has told me something of the way they go on, otherwise I should hardly know who was dead and who living.
target: Zillah has told me something of the way they go on
translation: ジラがあちらの暮らしぶりを少し話してくれたからいいものの、そうでなければ誰が死んで誰が生きているのかもろくにわからないところだ。
parts: of the way they go on
point: the way they go on は関係副詞 how が表に出ない形。the way how とは言わず、the way か how のどちらか一方だけを使う。
explanation: tell 人 物 で、me と something が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Emily Brontë
authorJa: エミリー・ブロンテ

text: She gave him credit for stationing himself where he might gaze and gaze again without offence; but was really obliged to put an end to it, and request him to place himself elsewhere.
target: She gave him credit for stationing himself where he might gaze and gaze again without offence
translation: 彼が失礼にならずに何度でも見とれていられる位置に陣取ったことは、うまいものだと彼女も認めた。だが、本当にもうやめさせなければならず、どこか別の場所に移ってくれるよう頼んだ。
parts: for stationing himself where he might gaze and gaze again without offence
point: give 人 credit for ～（～について人を評価する）。where he might gaze は先行詞を含む関係副詞（＝in the place where）。後半の request him to place は SVOC 型。
explanation: him と credit が2つの目的語なので SVOO。for 以下は理由を示す修飾語。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: The change which a few hours had wrought in the minds and the happiness of the Dashwoods, was such—so great—as promised them all, the satisfaction of a sleepless night.
target: as promised them all, the satisfaction of a sleepless night
translation: わずか数時間がダッシュウッド家の人々の心と幸福にもたらした変化はあまりに大きく、皆に眠れぬ一夜の満足を約束するほどだった。
parts: the satisfaction of a sleepless night
point: such … as の as は関係代名詞で、ここでは promised の主語。主節は The change … was such（SVC）。
explanation: promise 人 物（人に物を約束する）で、them all と the satisfaction が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Her mother stepped forwards, embraced her, and welcomed her with rapture; gave her hand with an affectionate smile to Wickham, who followed his lady; and wished them both joy, with an alacrity which showed no doubt of their happiness.
target: wished them both joy, with an alacrity which showed no doubt of their happiness
translation: 母親は進み出て娘を抱きしめ、大喜びで迎え入れた。妻の後に続いたウィッカムには愛想よく笑って手を差し出し、二人の幸せを少しも疑っていない勢いで、二人にお祝いを述べた。
parts: with an alacrity which showed no doubt of their happiness
point: 同じ文の gave her hand … to Wickham は give 物 to 人 の SVO。wish 人 物 と形が違うので見比べる。主語は文頭の Her mother。
explanation: wish 人 joy（人の幸福を祈る、祝う）で、them both と joy が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: While Tom was eating his supper, and stealing sugar as opportunity offered, Aunt Polly asked him questions that were full of guile, and very deep—for she wanted to trap him into damaging revealments.
translation: トムが夕食を食べ、隙を見ては砂糖をくすねているあいだ、ポリーおばさんは悪だくみたっぷりの、実に奥の深い質問をした。うっかり不利なことを白状させてやろうと思ったのだ。
parts: While Tom was eating his supper, and stealing sugar as opportunity offered
that were full of guile, and very deep
for she wanted to trap him into damaging revealments
point: ask 人 物 の SVOO。for 以下（for は接続詞で「というのは」）の中は wanted to trap him（不定詞が目的語、trap O into ～）。
explanation: him と questions が2つの目的語で SVOO。that 以下は questions を修飾する関係代名詞節。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: トム・ソーヤーの冒険

text: I snatched a cutlass from the pile, and someone, at the same time snatching another, gave me a cut across the knuckles which I hardly felt.
target: someone, at the same time snatching another, gave me a cut across the knuckles which I hardly felt
translation: 私は山の中から短剣を一本ひっつかんだ。同時に誰かがもう一本をつかみ、私の指の関節をさっと切りつけたが、ほとんど痛みも感じなかった。
parts: at the same time snatching another
point: which の先行詞は直前の the knuckles ではなく a cut（切り傷）。I hardly felt which（＝the cut）の関係。
explanation: give 人 a cut（人に切りつける）で、me と a cut が2つの目的語。SVOO。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン

text: When she came to herself, or when Miss Betsey had restored her, whichever it was, she found the latter standing at the window.
translation: 自分で正気に戻ったのか、ミス・ベッツィに介抱されて我に返ったのか、ともかく気がつくと、ミス・ベッツィが窓辺に立っていた。
parts: When she came to herself, or when Miss Betsey had restored her, whichever it was
point: whichever it was は「どちらであったにせよ」という複合関係代名詞の譲歩の挿入句。the latter（後者）は Miss Betsey を指す。
explanation: find O doing（Oが～しているのに気づく）で、the latter＝standing の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: I want you to explain to me why you won’t exhibit Dorian Gray’s picture.
translation: どうしてドリアン・グレイの肖像画を展示しないのか、説明してほしいね。
parts: to explain to me why you won’t exhibit Dorian Gray’s picture
point: want O to do は、you が explain する（O と不定詞の間に主語・述語の関係がある）形。why節は explain の目的語になる名詞節。
explanation: 本アプリでは allow O to do と同様、want O to do を SVOC として扱う。
note: want O to do を「SVO＋不定詞」と説明する文法書もあるが、学校文法では O と to do の主述関係から SVOC とするのが一般的。
author: Oscar Wilde
authorJa: オスカー・ワイルド
workJa: ドリアン・グレイの肖像

text: My hour of favour was over; I found myself lumped along with Kurtz as a partisan of methods for which the time was not ripe: I was unsound!
target: I found myself lumped along with Kurtz as a partisan of methods for which the time was not ripe
translation: 私の寵愛の時は終わった。気がつけば私はクルツと一緒くたにされ、時機尚早のやり方の支持者と見なされていたのだ。私は「不健全」だというわけだ。
parts: as a partisan of methods for which the time was not ripe
point: 前置詞＋関係代名詞 for which（the time was ripe for the methods）の節は SVC だが、methods を修飾する部分。
explanation: find oneself＋過去分詞（気づくと～されていた）で、myself＝lumped の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: There are counterpoises and compensations in life; and the event which had made of her a social warning had also for the moment made her the most interesting personage in the village to many.
target: the event which had made of her a social warning had also for the moment made her the most interesting personage in the village to many
translation: 人生には釣り合いや埋め合わせというものがある。彼女を世間への戒めにしてしまった出来事が、同時にさしあたり、多くの人にとって彼女を村でいちばん興味を引く人物にもしていたのである。
parts: which had made of her a social warning
had also for the moment made
the most interesting personage in the village
point: 関係詞節の made of her a social warning は make A of B（BをAにする）の A と of B が入れ替わった形で、make O C とは形が違う。同じ make でも主節は make O C。
explanation: 主節は the event had made her the most interesting personage。her＝personage の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: Her eyes, which were grey with a shade of green through them, had a habit of glancing upwards when she spoke with anyone, which made her look like a little perverse madonna.
target: which made her look like a little perverse madonna
translation: 彼女の目は緑がかった灰色で、誰かと話すときには上目づかいにちらりと見る癖があり、そのせいで小さなひねくれ者の聖母マリアのように見えた。
parts: look like a little perverse madonna
point: 主節 Her eyes … had a habit は SVO、最初の which were grey は SVC。1つの文の中の3つの節の文型がすべて違う。
explanation: 使役の make O 原形で、her が look する関係。make O do は SVOC。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス

text: His first care was given to the child, whose cries, indeed, as she lay writhing on the trundle-bed, made it of peremptory necessity to postpone all other business to the task of soothing her.
target: whose cries, indeed, as she lay writhing on the trundle-bed, made it of peremptory necessity to postpone all other business to the task of soothing her
translation: 彼はまず赤ん坊の手当てにかかった。実際、低い寝台の上で身もだえする赤ん坊の泣き声を聞けば、ほかのことはすべて後回しにして、なだめることを優先するほかなかった。
parts: as she lay writhing on the trundle-bed
to postpone all other business to the task of soothing her
point: it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to postpone 以下。of＋抽象名詞（of necessity＝necessary）が補語。
explanation: make it C to do（～することをCにする）の SVOC。it（＝to postpone …）＝of peremptory necessity（絶対に必要）の関係。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン

text: It had been represented to them that the disarray into which society had been thrown by this deplorable affair made their presence in town more necessary than ever.
target: the disarray into which society had been thrown by this deplorable affair made their presence in town more necessary than ever
translation: この嘆かわしい事件で社交界が陥った混乱のために、自分たちが街にいることがこれまで以上に必要になっている、と彼らは説き伏せられていたのだった。
parts: into which society had been thrown by this deplorable affair
point: into which の節は throw O into ～ の受動態（society had been thrown into the disarray）。主語 the disarray と動詞 made が遠く離れている。
explanation: make O C で、their presence＝more necessary の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン
workJa: エイジ・オブ・イノセンス

text: As he entered the box his eyes met Miss Welland's, and he saw that she had instantly understood his motive, though the family dignity which both considered so high a virtue would not permit her to tell him so.
target: the family dignity which both considered so high a virtue would not permit her to tell him so
translation: ボックス席に入ると彼の目はウェランド嬢の目と合い、彼女が彼の意図をすぐに理解したのがわかった。もっとも、二人がこの上ない美徳と考える一家の体面が、それを口に出すことを彼女に許さなかったが。
parts: which both considered so high a virtue
point: 関係詞節 which both considered so high a virtue も consider O C（which＝O、so high a virtue＝C）の SVOC。さらに to tell him so の中は SVOO。三層の入れ子。
explanation: permit O to do（Oが～するのを許す）は allow O to do と同じく SVOC として扱う。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン
workJa: エイジ・オブ・イノセンス

text: He felt himself flung back on all the ugly uncertainties from which he thought he had cast loose forever.
translation: 彼は、永遠に縁を切ったと思っていたあの醜い迷いのすべてに、自分がまた投げ戻されたように感じた。
parts: on all the ugly uncertainties from which he thought he had cast loose forever
point: from which he thought he had cast loose は、he thought が挟まった連鎖関係詞節（he had cast loose from the uncertainties）。
explanation: feel O＋過去分詞（Oが～されるのを感じる）で、himself＝flung back（投げ戻された）の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: I found it simple, in my ignorance, my confusion, and perhaps my conceit, to assume that I could deal with a boy whose education for the world was all on the point of beginning.
translation: 無知と混乱と、たぶんうぬぼれのせいで、世間に出るための教育がまさに始まろうとしている少年くらい自分で扱えるだろうと思い込むのは、私にはたやすいことだった。
parts: in my ignorance, my confusion, and perhaps my conceit
to assume that I could deal with a boy whose education for the world was all on the point of beginning
point: it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to assume 以下。間に長い修飾語が挟まっているので、it と to assume を結びつけにくい。
explanation: find it C to do（～することをCだと思う）で、it（＝to assume …）＝simple の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: I knew myself, at the first breath of this new life, to be more wicked, tenfold more wicked, sold a slave to my original evil; and the thought, in that moment, braced and delighted me like wine.
target: I knew myself, at the first breath of this new life, to be more wicked, tenfold more wicked, sold a slave to my original evil
translation: この新しい生命の最初のひと息で、私は自分がより邪悪な、十倍も邪悪な者となり、生来の悪に奴隷として売り渡されたのを知った。そしてその瞬間、その思いは酒のように私を奮い立たせ、喜ばせた。
parts: at the first breath of this new life
to be more wicked, tenfold more wicked, sold a slave to my original evil
point: know O to be C の O（myself）と to be のあいだに長い修飾語が挟まっている。sold a slave は「奴隷として売られた」。
explanation: myself＝more wicked の関係が成り立つ SVOC（know / believe / think O to be C）。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
work: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
workJa: ジキル博士とハイド氏

text: Hareton allowed Zillah to give him her aid; and she flattered him into a good humour; so, when Catherine came, half forgetting her former insults, he tried to make himself agreeable, by the housekeeper’s account.
target: Hareton allowed Zillah to give him her aid
translation: ヘアトンはジラに手当てをさせてやった。彼女がおだてて機嫌を直させたので、家政婦の話によれば、キャサリンが来たとき、彼は以前の侮辱を半ば忘れて、感じよくふるまおうとしたという。
point: 不定詞の中 give him her aid は SVOO。文全体の動詞 allowed で判定する。
explanation: allow O to do（Oが～するのを許す）は SVOC。Zillah が give する関係。
author: Emily Brontë
authorJa: エミリー・ブロンテ

text: Anne could just acknowledge within herself such a possibility of having been induced to marry him, as made her shudder at the idea of the misery which must have followed.
target: as made her shudder at the idea of the misery which must have followed
translation: アンは、説き伏せられて彼と結婚していたかもしれないという可能性を心の中で認めることはできたが、それは、そうなれば続いたにちがいない不幸を思うと身震いするような可能性だった。
parts: at the idea of the misery which must have followed
point: such … as の as は関係代名詞で、made の主語。先行詞は such a possibility。
explanation: make O 原形（Oに～させる）で、her が shudder する関係。SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: And as to my father, I really should not have thought that he, who has kept himself single so long for our sakes, need be suspected now.
target: who has kept himself single so long for our sakes
translation: それに父のことなら、私たちのためにこんなに長く独り身を通してきた人が、今さら疑われる必要があるなんて、本当に思いもしなかったわ。
point: 主節は I should not have thought that …（SVO）。that節の中の he と need be suspected のあいだに who節が挿入されている。
explanation: keep O C（OをCに保つ）で、himself＝single の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Angry as she was, the thought of the moment made her resolve to restrain herself when she did speak.
translation: 腹は立っていたが、その場の思いが、口を開くときには自制しようと彼女に決心させた。
parts: resolve to restrain herself when she did speak
point: Angry as she was は「形容詞＋as＋S＋V」で「～だったけれども」という譲歩。resolve to do は不定詞が resolve の目的語。
explanation: 使役の make O 原形で、her が resolve する関係なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: As soon as they had driven from the door, Elizabeth was called on by her cousin to give her opinion of all that she had seen at Rosings, which, for Charlotte’s sake, she made more favourable than it really was.
target: which, for Charlotte’s sake, she made more favourable than it really was
translation: 馬車が玄関を離れるとすぐ、エリザベスはいとこからロジングズで見たものすべてについて感想を求められた。彼女はシャーロットのために、その感想を実際よりも好意的なものにした。
point: which は made の目的語で、先行詞は her opinion。語順を戻すと she made her opinion more favourable。
explanation: make O C で、which（＝her opinion）＝more favourable の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: A little thing like that don’t cost nothing, and it’s just the little things that makes a man to be looked up to and liked.
target: it’s just the little things that makes a man to be looked up to and liked
translation: そういうちょっとしたことは一文もかからねえ。人から一目置かれて好かれるようになるのは、まさにそういうちょっとしたことなんだ。
parts: to be looked up to and liked
point: it is … that の強調構文。方言なので、主語が複数なのに makes、さらに標準英語では make O 原形のところに to be が入っている。
explanation: 強調構文を戻すと the little things make a man (to) be looked up to and liked。a man が look up to される関係なので SVOC。
note: 標準英語なら make a man be looked up to となる。強調構文の it is と that は文型判定から外して考える。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: ハックルベリー・フィンの冒険

text: I told him I did not know his mate Bill, and this was for a person who stayed in our house whom we called the captain.
target: whom we called the captain
translation: 私は、相棒のビルなんて人は知らないし、これはうちに泊まっていて、私たちが「船長」と呼んでいる人のためのものだと言った。
point: 1つの先行詞 a person に who stayed in our house と whom we called the captain の2つの関係詞節がかかっている（二重限定）。
explanation: call O C で、whom（＝a person）＝the captain の関係が成り立つ SVOC。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン

text: In reality he was annoyed at having old Monsieur Farival, who considered himself the better sailor of the two.
target: who considered himself the better sailor of the two
translation: 実のところ彼は、老ファリヴァル氏が一緒なのが気に入らなかった。老人は二人のうち自分のほうが船乗りとして上だと思っていたのだ。
parts: the better sailor of the two
point: consider O (to be) C の to be が省略された形。主節の was annoyed at ～ は感情を表す受動態。
explanation: himself＝the better sailor の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Kate Chopin
authorJa: ケイト・ショパン

text: A very chill and vault-like air pervaded the stairs and gallery, suggesting cheerless ideas of space and solitude; and I was glad, when finally ushered into my chamber, to find it of small dimensions, and furnished in ordinary, modern style.
target: to find it of small dimensions, and furnished in ordinary, modern style
translation: 階段と回廊にはひどく冷たい納骨堂のような空気が漂い、がらんとした広さと孤独という陰気な思いを誘った。だから、ようやく自分の部屋に通されて、そこが小ぢんまりとして、ふつうの現代風にしつらえてあるのを知ったときはうれしかった。
parts: of small dimensions, and furnished in ordinary, modern style
point: 主節 I was glad は SVC で、to find 以下は glad の理由を表す副詞的用法の不定詞。判定するのは不定詞句の中。
explanation: find O C で、it（部屋）＝of small dimensions（小さい）、furnished in … style（～風にしつらえられた）の関係が成り立つ SVOC。of＋名詞が形容詞の働きをしている。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: In easy state upon this couch, there sat a jolly Giant, glorious to see; who bore a glowing torch, in shape not unlike Plenty's horn, and held it up, high up, to shed its light on Scrooge, as he came peeping round the door.
target: In easy state upon this couch, there sat a jolly Giant, glorious to see
translation: この寝椅子の上にゆったりと構えて、見るも見事な陽気な巨人が座っていた。巨人は豊穣の角にどこか似た形の、燃え立つたいまつを手にしていて、スクルージがドアの陰からのぞきこむと、その光を彼に注ごうと、高く、さらに高く掲げた。
point: there sat ~ は There is 構文と同じく、主語が動詞の後ろに回った倒置。セミコロン以下の who 節には bore a glowing torch（SVO）や held it up などがあり、そちらに引っぱられやすい。
explanation: 主語は a jolly Giant、動詞は自動詞の sat。glorious to see は巨人を説明する形容詞句（to see は形容詞を限定する副詞的用法の不定詞）。骨格は A jolly Giant sat＝SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: クリスマス・キャロル

text: About on a level with his eyes, there sat, in that corner of the Judge’s bench, two persons upon whom his look immediately rested; so immediately, and so much to the changing of his aspect, that all the eyes that were turned upon him, turned to them.
target: About on a level with his eyes, there sat, in that corner of the Judge’s bench, two persons upon whom his look immediately rested
translation: ちょうど彼の目の高さ、判事席のその片隅に二人の人物が座っていて、彼の視線はすぐさまその二人にとまった。あまりにすぐに、そしてあまりに彼の顔色を変えさせたので、彼に向けられていたすべての目が、その二人のほうへ向いた。
parts: About on a level with his eyes
in that corner of the Judge’s bench
upon whom his look immediately rested
point: 主語 two persons が動詞 sat のずっと後ろにある倒置文。upon whom は「前置詞＋関係代名詞」で、rest upon（~にとまる）の upon が前に出たもの。
explanation: there sat ... two persons は「二人が座っていた」で、sat は自動詞。位置を表す句と関係詞節はすべて修飾語なので、骨格は two persons sat＝SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: The steps came creaking up the stairs—the intolerable distress of the situation woke the stricken resolution of the lads—they were about to spring for the closet, when there was a crash of rotten timbers and Injun Joe landed on the ground amid the debris of the ruined stairway.
target: Injun Joe landed on the ground amid the debris of the ruined stairway
translation: 足音がきしみながら階段を上ってきた――耐えがたい窮地が、すくみ上がっていた少年たちの決心を呼び覚ました――二人が戸棚へ飛びこもうとしたそのとき、腐った材木が崩れる轟音がして、インジャン・ジョーは壊れた階段の残骸のなか、地面に落ちた。
parts: amid the debris of the ruined stairway
point: 長い文の中に woke the stricken resolution（SVO）や there was a crash（SV）など複数の節がある。問われているのは最後の and 以下の節。
explanation: land はここでは「着地する、落ちる」の自動詞。on the ground も amid ~ も場所を表す修飾語で、骨格は Injun Joe landed＝SV。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: トム・ソーヤーの冒険

text: After breakfast they went whooping and prancing out on the bar, and chased each other round and round, shedding clothes as they went, until they were naked, and then continued the frolic far away up the shoal water of the bar, against the stiff current, which latter tripped their legs from under them from time to time and greatly increased the fun.
target: After breakfast they went whooping and prancing out on the bar
translation: 朝食のあと、彼らは歓声をあげ跳ねまわりながら砂州へ出ていき、ぐるぐると追いかけっこをした。走りながら服を脱ぎ捨てて素っ裸になると、今度は強い流れに逆らって、砂州の浅瀬をずっと上のほうまではしゃぎ続けた。その流れがときどき彼らの足をすくい、おかげで面白さはいっそう増した。
point: 後ろには chased each other（SVO）、continued the frolic（SVO）、tripped their legs（SVO）が続く。判定するのは最初の went の節だけ。
explanation: go ~ing は「~しながら行く」。whooping and prancing は様子を表す分詞で、went は自動詞。骨格は they went＝SV。
note: go ~ing の ~ing を主語の状態を表す補語とみて SVC と説明する立場もある。ここでは様子を表す修飾語と考えて SV とした。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: トム・ソーヤーの冒険

text: I went up and set down on a log at the head of the island, and looked out on the big river and the black driftwood and away over to the town, three mile away, where there was three or four lights twinkling.
target: I went up and set down on a log at the head of the island
translation: おいらは上に行って、島の先っぽの丸太に腰をおろし、大きな川や黒い流木や、三マイル向こうの町のほうをずっと眺めた。町では明かりが三つ四つまたたいていた。
parts: at the head of the island
point: set は本来「置く」の他動詞だが、ハックの方言では sat（座った）の代わりに使われている。後ろに目的語はない。
explanation: went も set down も自動詞で、後ろはすべて場所を表す修飾語。骨格は I went ... and set down＝SV。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: ハックルベリー・フィンの冒険

text: I was there to protect and defend the little creatures in the world the most bereaved and the most lovable, the appeal of whose helplessness had suddenly become only too explicit, a deep, constant ache of one’s own committed heart.
translation: 私がそこにいたのは、この世でいちばん身寄りがなく、いちばん愛らしい小さな者たちを守り抜くためだった。その子たちの無力さの訴えは、にわかに痛いほどはっきりしてきた――身を捧げた自分の心の、深く絶え間ない疼きとなって。
parts: to protect and defend the little creatures in the world the most bereaved and the most lovable, the appeal of whose helplessness had suddenly become only too explicit, a deep, constant ache of one’s own committed heart
point: 関係代名詞の所有格 whose が the appeal of whose helplessness という形で使われ、その中に had become only too explicit（SVC）がある。
explanation: be＋場所（there）は「いる」の意味で SV と判定する。to protect and defend ~ は目的を表す副詞的用法の不定詞。骨格は I was (there)＝SV。
note: be 動詞の後ろに場所を表す語句が来るときは「存在」を表す SV とするのが学校文法の約束。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: Instantly, in the emptiness of the landscape, a cry arose whose shrillness pierced the still air like a sharp arrow flying straight to the very heart of the land; and, as if by enchantment, streams of human beings—of naked human beings—with spears in their hands, with bows, with shields, with wild glances and savage movements, were poured into the clearing by the dark-faced and pensive forest.
target: Instantly, in the emptiness of the landscape, a cry arose whose shrillness pierced the still air like a sharp arrow flying straight to the very heart of the land
translation: たちまち、がらんとした風景のなかに叫び声が上がった。その甲高さは、大地のまさに心臓へまっすぐ飛ぶ鋭い矢のように、静まりかえった空気を貫いた。そして魔法のように、人間の群れが――裸の人間の群れが――手に槍を、弓を、盾を持ち、荒々しい目つきと野蛮な動きで、黒い顔をした物思わしげな森から空き地へと吐き出された。
parts: in the emptiness of the landscape
whose shrillness pierced the still air like a sharp arrow flying straight to the very heart of the land
point: 関係代名詞 whose の先行詞 a cry が、動詞 arose をはさんで離れている。whose 節の中の pierced the still air（SVO）につられやすい。
explanation: arise（起こる、上がる）は自動詞。whose 以下は a cry を説明する修飾語なので、骨格は a cry arose＝SV。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: No fear can stand up to hunger, no patience can wear it out, disgust simply does not exist where hunger is; and as to superstition, beliefs, and what you may call principles, they are less than chaff in a breeze.
target: disgust simply does not exist where hunger is
translation: どんな恐怖も飢えには立ち向かえず、どんな忍耐も飢えをすり減らせない。飢えのあるところには、嫌悪などまるで存在しないのだ。迷信や信仰や、主義とでも呼べるものに至っては、風に舞うもみ殻ほどの重みもない。
point: 前の節の wear it out（SVO）や、後ろの they are less than chaff（SVC）と並んでいる。where hunger is は場所を表す修飾語の節。
explanation: exist は自動詞で、目的語も補語もとらない。where hunger is の is も「存在する」の意味の自動詞。骨格は disgust does not exist＝SV。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: They went out, locking the door of the theatre behind them; and Utterson, once more leaving the servants gathered about the fire in the hall, trudged back to his office to read the two narratives in which this mystery was now to be explained.
target: Utterson, once more leaving the servants gathered about the fire in the hall, trudged back to his office to read the two narratives in which this mystery was now to be explained
translation: 二人は階段教室の扉に鍵をかけて外へ出た。そしてアタスンは、ふたたび召使いたちを広間の暖炉のまわりに集まらせたまま、この謎がいよいよ解き明かされるはずの二通の手記を読むために、とぼとぼと事務所へ戻った。
parts: once more leaving the servants gathered about the fire in the hall
to read the two narratives in which this mystery was now to be explained
point: 挿入された分詞構文 leaving the servants gathered ~ は leave O C（O を C のままにしておく）の形。だがこれは主語を説明する修飾語にすぎない。
explanation: 主節の動詞 trudged（とぼとぼ歩く）は自動詞。back と to his office は方向、to read ~ は目的を表す副詞的用法の不定詞。骨格は Utterson trudged＝SV。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
work: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
workJa: ジキル博士とハイド氏

text: Thus speaking, and sobbing aloud, the unhappy creature turned away; while Rose Maylie, overpowered by this extraordinary interview, which had more the semblance of a rapid dream than an actual occurrence, sank into a chair, and endeavoured to collect her wandering thoughts.
target: Rose Maylie, overpowered by this extraordinary interview, which had more the semblance of a rapid dream than an actual occurrence, sank into a chair
translation: そう言うと、その不幸な女は声をあげて泣きながら背を向けた。一方ローズ・メイリーは、現実の出来事というより、つかの間の夢のようなこの異様な会見に圧倒されて椅子に崩れるように座りこみ、乱れた思いをまとめようと努めた。
parts: which had more the semblance of a rapid dream than an actual occurrence
point: 主語 Rose Maylie と動詞 sank のあいだに、過去分詞の句と関係詞節（had the semblance＝SVO）が挟まっている。
explanation: sink（沈む、くずおれる）は自動詞。into a chair は方向を表す修飾語。骨格は Rose Maylie sank＝SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: He was walking along, thinking how happy and contented he ought to feel; and how much he would give for only one look at poor little Dick, who, starved and beaten, might be weeping bitterly at that very moment; when he was startled by a young woman screaming out very loud.
target: He was walking along, thinking how happy and contented he ought to feel; and how much he would give for only one look at poor little Dick, who, starved and beaten, might be weeping bitterly at that very moment
translation: 彼は歩きながら、自分はどんなに幸せで満ち足りた気持ちでいるべきか、そして、飢えと殴打に苦しみ、ちょうど今ごろ激しく泣いているかもしれないかわいそうなディックを一目見るためなら、どれほどのものを差し出すだろうかと考えていた。そのとき、若い女の大きな叫び声に彼はぎょっとした。
parts: thinking how happy and contented he ought to feel; and how much he would give for only one look at poor little Dick, who, starved and beaten, might be weeping bitterly at that very moment
point: thinking 以下には how happy he ought to feel（SVC）や how much he would give（SVO）が詰まっているが、すべて分詞構文の中身。
explanation: was walking は進行形の自動詞で、along は副詞。thinking 以下は「~と考えながら」という付帯状況の修飾語。骨格は He was walking＝SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: But thoughts like these troubled very few of the reckless crew; and when, after steadily dropping and dropping the pirates astern, the Pequod at last shot by the vivid green Cockatoo Point on the Sumatra side, emerging at last upon the broad waters beyond; then, the harpooneers seemed more to grieve that the swift whales had been gaining upon the ship, than to rejoice that the ship had so victoriously gained upon the Malays.
target: the Pequod at last shot by the vivid green Cockatoo Point on the Sumatra side, emerging at last upon the broad waters beyond
translation: だがこうした考えに悩まされた者は、向こう見ずな乗組員のなかにほとんどいなかった。海賊船をじりじりと船尾のかなたへ引き離したのち、ピークォド号がついにスマトラ側の鮮やかな緑のコカトゥー岬のそばを矢のように通り過ぎ、その先の広い海へ出たとき、銛打ちたちは、船が見事にマレー人を引き離したことを喜ぶよりも、足の速い鯨たちに差を広げられていたことを嘆いているように見えた。
parts: by the vivid green Cockatoo Point
emerging at last upon the broad waters beyond
point: when 節の中を判定する。shot by の by は「~のそばを」という場所の前置詞で、受動態の by ではない。
explanation: shoot はここでは「疾走する」の自動詞。by ~ は場所、emerging ~ は付帯状況の修飾語。骨格は the Pequod shot＝SV。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: When I got up I shook like a leaf with excitement, and when I opened these beautiful wings and made sure what a rare and so extraordinary perfect specimen I had, my head went round and my legs became so weak with emotion that I had to sit on the ground.
target: When I got up I shook like a leaf with excitement
translation: 起き上がったとき、私は興奮で木の葉のように震えていた。そしてその美しい羽を広げ、自分が手にしたのがどれほど珍しく、どれほど並外れて完全な標本かを確かめたとき、頭がくらくらし、感激で脚の力が抜けて、地面に座りこまずにはいられなかった。
point: 後半には made sure what ... I had（SVO）や my legs became so weak（SVC）がある。問われているのは最初の主節。
explanation: shake（震える）はここでは自動詞。like a leaf は様態、with excitement は原因を表す修飾語。骨格は I shook＝SV。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: After dinner the squire and the doctor sat by the captain’s side awhile in consultation; and when they had talked to their hearts’ content, it being then a little past noon, the doctor took up his hat and pistols, girt on a cutlass, put the chart in his pocket, and with a musket over his shoulder crossed the palisade on the north side and set off briskly through the trees.
target: After dinner the squire and the doctor sat by the captain’s side awhile in consultation
translation: 食事のあと、郷士と医者はしばらく船長のそばに座って相談していた。心ゆくまで話し合ったころには正午を少し過ぎていたので、医者は帽子と拳銃を手に取り、短剣を腰に帯び、地図をポケットに入れ、マスケット銃を肩にかけて北側の柵を越え、木立のなかを足早に出発した。
point: 後半には took up his hat（SVO）、put the chart in his pocket（SVO）、crossed the palisade（SVO）など他動詞が並ぶ。判定するのは最初の節。
explanation: sat は自動詞。by ~ は場所、awhile は時間、in consultation は様子を表す修飾語。骨格は the squire and the doctor sat＝SV。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン

text: During the whole of this time, and during the whole search, my companion, wrapped up on the box, never relaxed in his vigilance a single moment; but when we crossed the bridge he seemed, if possible, to be more on the alert than before.
target: my companion, wrapped up on the box, never relaxed in his vigilance a single moment
translation: そのあいだずっと、捜索のあいだじゅう、御者台で身をくるんだ連れの男は一瞬たりとも警戒をゆるめなかった。だが橋を渡ると、彼はできることならこれまで以上に油断なく構えているように見えた。
point: a single moment は名詞の形をしているが、「一瞬も」という時間を表す副詞的な名詞句で、relaxed の目的語ではない。後半の he seemed to be more on the alert は SVC。
explanation: relax はここでは「ゆるむ」の自動詞で、in his vigilance は「警戒において」という修飾語。骨格は my companion never relaxed＝SV。
note: relax を他動詞として relax his vigilance と書けば SVO になる。ここでは in があるので自動詞。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I had so worked upon my imagination as really to believe that about the whole mansion and domain there hung an atmosphere peculiar to themselves and their immediate vicinity--an atmosphere which had no affinity with the air of heaven, but which had reeked up from the decayed trees, and the grey wall, and the silent tarn--a pestilent and mystic vapour, dull, sluggish, faintly discernible, and leaden-hued.
target: I had so worked upon my imagination as really to believe that about the whole mansion and domain there hung an atmosphere peculiar to themselves and their immediate vicinity
translation: 私は自分の想像力にあまりに働きかけたために、本気でこう信じるまでになっていた――屋敷と地所の全体のまわりには、それ自体とそのすぐ周辺にだけ特有の空気が垂れこめている、と。それは天の空気とはなんの縁もなく、朽ちた木々や灰色の壁や静まりかえった沼から立ちのぼった空気――有毒で神秘的な、どんよりと重く、かすかにしか見えない鉛色の靄なのだと。
parts: as really to believe that about the whole mansion and domain there hung an atmosphere peculiar to themselves and their immediate vicinity
point: so ~ as to do（…するほど~）の構文。as to believe 以下の that 節には there hung an atmosphere（倒置の SV）が含まれている。
explanation: work は「働きかける」の自動詞で、upon my imagination は前置詞句の修飾語。as really to believe ~ は程度・結果を表す副詞的用法の不定詞。骨格は I had worked＝SV。
note: work upon を「~に働きかける」という一つの他動詞（群動詞）とみれば、my imagination を目的語として SVO とする立場もある。
author: Edgar Allan Poe
authorJa: エドガー・アラン・ポー
work: The Fall of the House of Usher

text: He had the offer of Count Cassel and Anhalt, and at first did not know which to chuse, and wanted Miss Bertram to direct him; but upon being made to understand the different style of the characters, and which was which, and recollecting that he had once seen the play in London, and had thought Anhalt a very stupid fellow, he soon decided for the Count.
target: upon being made to understand the different style of the characters, and which was which, and recollecting that he had once seen the play in London, and had thought Anhalt a very stupid fellow, he soon decided for the Count
translation: 彼にはカッセル伯爵とアンハルトの役が提示されたが、はじめはどちらを選んでいいかわからず、ミス・バートラムに決めてもらいたがった。だが役柄の違いや、どちらがどちらかを説明されて理解し、かつてロンドンでその芝居を見てアンハルトをひどく愚かな男だと思ったことを思い出すと、すぐに伯爵に決めた。
parts: upon being made to understand the different style of the characters, and which was which, and recollecting that he had once seen the play in London, and had thought Anhalt a very stupid fellow
point: 前半には wanted Miss Bertram to direct him（SVOC）、主節の前の前置き部分には had thought Anhalt a very stupid fellow（SVOC）がある。どちらも判定する主節ではない。
explanation: decide for ~ は「~に決める」。decide はここでは自動詞で、for the Count は前置詞句の修飾語。骨格は he decided＝SV。
note: decide for を一つの他動詞的なまとまりとみて SVO と説明する参考書もある。学校文法では「自動詞＋前置詞句」として SV に分類するのが一般的。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: The regiment was standing at order arms at the side of a lane, waiting for the command to march, when suddenly the youth remembered the little packet enwrapped in a faded yellow envelope which the loud young soldier with lugubrious words had intrusted to him.
target: The regiment was standing at order arms at the side of a lane, waiting for the command to march
translation: 連隊は小道のわきで立て銃の姿勢をとり、進軍の命令を待っていた。そのとき突然、若者は、あの声の大きな若い兵士が陰気な言葉とともに自分に預けていった、色あせた黄色い封筒に包まれた小さな包みのことを思い出した。
parts: at the side of a lane
waiting for the command to march
point: when 以下には remembered the little packet（SVO）があり、その中の関係詞節 which ... had intrusted to him も SVO。判定するのは前半の主節。
explanation: stand は自動詞。at order arms（立て銃の姿勢で）、at the side of a lane（場所）、waiting ~（付帯状況）はすべて修飾語。骨格は The regiment was standing＝SV。
author: Stephen Crane
authorJa: スティーヴン・クレイン

text: How Joe got out of the room, I have never been able to determine; but I know that when he did get out he was steadily proceeding upstairs instead of coming down, and was deaf to all remonstrances until I went after him and laid hold of him.
target: he was steadily proceeding upstairs instead of coming down
translation: ジョーがどうやって部屋から出たのか、私にはいまだにわからない。だが、ようやく出たときには、下りてくるどころか着実に階段を上っていき、私が追いかけてつかまえるまで、どんな忠告にも耳を貸さなかったことは知っている。
point: 文頭の How Joe got out of the room は determine の目的語が前に出たもの。後ろの was deaf to all remonstrances は SVC。判定するのは that 節の中の、when 節に続く部分。
explanation: proceed（進む）は自動詞。upstairs は方向を表す副詞、instead of ~ も修飾語。骨格は he was proceeding＝SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Next to her sat, on her right, Sir Thomas Burdon, a Radical member of Parliament, who followed his leader in public life and in private life followed the best cooks, dining with the Tories and thinking with the Liberals, in accordance with a wise and well-known rule.
translation: 彼女の隣、右側には、急進派の下院議員サー・トマス・バードンが座っていた。彼は公の生活では党首に従い、私生活では最高の料理人に従って、賢明でよく知られた処世訓どおり、トーリー党員と食事をし、自由党員と考えを共にしていた。
parts: who followed his leader in public life and in private life followed the best cooks, dining with the Tories and thinking with the Liberals, in accordance with a wise and well-known rule
point: Next to her sat ... Sir Thomas Burdon は、場所の句が文頭に出て主語と動詞が入れ替わった倒置文。関係詞節の followed his leader（SVO）に引っぱられやすい。
explanation: 主語は Sir Thomas Burdon、動詞は自動詞の sat。a Radical member of Parliament は主語の同格語で、who 以下も主語を説明する修飾語。骨格は Sir Thomas Burdon sat＝SV。
author: Oscar Wilde
authorJa: オスカー・ワイルド
workJa: ドリアン・グレイの肖像

text: Bingley, from this time, was of course a daily visitor at Longbourn; coming frequently before breakfast, and always remaining till after supper; unless when some barbarous neighbour, who could not be enough detested, had given him an invitation to dinner, which he thought himself obliged to accept.
target: Bingley, from this time, was of course a daily visitor at Longbourn
translation: このときからビングリー氏は、当然のように毎日ロングボーンを訪れるようになった。たびたび朝食前にやって来ては、いつも夕食のあとまで居残った。ただし、いくら憎んでも憎み足りないどこかの野蛮な隣人が彼を夕食に招き、断るわけにはいかないと彼が思った場合は別だった。
point: 後半には had given him an invitation（SVOO）や thought himself obliged to accept（SVOC）が出てくるが、どちらも unless 以下の従属節の中。
explanation: a daily visitor は主語 Bingley とイコールの関係にある補語。from this time、of course、at Longbourn は修飾語。骨格は Bingley was a visitor＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Her Ladyship received them civilly, but it was plain that their company was by no means so acceptable as when she could get nobody else; and she was, in fact, almost engrossed by her nephews, speaking to them, especially to Darcy, much more than to any other person in the room.
target: their company was by no means so acceptable as when she could get nobody else
translation: 令夫人は一行を礼儀正しく迎えはしたが、ほかに誰も呼べなかったころほど彼らの同席を歓迎していないのは明らかだった。実際、夫人は甥たちにほとんどかかりきりで、部屋のほかの誰よりも彼らに、とりわけダーシーに話しかけていた。
parts: as when she could get nobody else
point: it was plain that ~ の that 節の中を判定する。as when ~ は「~だったときほど」という比較の相手で、修飾語。
explanation: acceptable は主語 their company の性質を述べる形容詞で補語。by no means は否定の修飾語。骨格は their company was acceptable＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Her own attachment had really subsided into a mere nothing; it was not worth thinking of;—but if he, who had undoubtedly been always so much the most in love of the two, were to be returning with the same warmth of sentiment which he had taken away, it would be very distressing.
target: if he, who had undoubtedly been always so much the most in love of the two, were to be returning with the same warmth of sentiment which he had taken away, it would be very distressing
translation: 彼女自身の恋心は、もうすっかりしぼんで無に等しくなっていた。考えるにも値しなかった。――だが、二人のうちで間違いなくずっと深く恋していた彼が、去ったときと同じ熱い気持ちのまま戻ってくるのだとしたら、それはひどく困ったことになるだろう。
parts: if he, who had undoubtedly been always so much the most in love of the two, were to be returning with the same warmth of sentiment which he had taken away
point: if 節の中に who 節（been the most in love＝SVC）が挟まり、were to be returning という仮定の形もある。主節は最後の it would be very distressing だけ。
explanation: it は「その状況」を指す主語で、distressing（困った、悩ましい）は主語の状態を表す補語。骨格は it would be distressing＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: The conclusion of the whole was, that if the woman who had been sensible of Captain Wentworth’s merits could be allowed to prefer another man, there was nothing in the engagement to excite lasting wonder; and if Captain Wentworth lost no friend by it, certainly nothing to be regretted.
target: The conclusion of the whole was, that if the woman who had been sensible of Captain Wentworth’s merits could be allowed to prefer another man, there was nothing in the engagement to excite lasting wonder
translation: 全体の結論はこうだった――ウェントワース大佐の美点がわかっていた女性が別の男性を選ぶことが許されるのなら、この婚約にいつまでも驚くべきことは何もない。そしてウェントワース大佐がそれで友人を一人も失わないのなら、悔やむべきことも確かに何もない。
parts: that if the woman who had been sensible of Captain Wentworth’s merits could be allowed to prefer another man, there was nothing in the engagement to excite lasting wonder
point: that 節の中に、if 節（be allowed to prefer＝受動態）や there was nothing（SV）がある。だが問われているのは主節 The conclusion was ~ の形。
explanation: be 動詞の後ろの that 節は「結論＝その内容」というイコールの関係を表す名詞節で、補語になる。骨格は The conclusion was that ~＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: He was steady, observant, moderate, candid; never run away with by spirits or by selfishness, which fancied itself strong feeling; and yet, with a sensibility to what was amiable and lovely, and a value for all the felicities of domestic life, which characters of fancied enthusiasm and violent agitation seldom really possess.
target: He was steady, observant, moderate, candid
translation: 彼は落ち着いていて、観察が鋭く、節度があり、率直だった。気分の高ぶりにも、強い感情だと思いこんだ身勝手さにも決して振り回されなかった。それでいて、愛すべきもの、美しいものを感じとる心と、家庭生活のあらゆる幸せを大切にする気持ちを持っていた。それは、熱狂ぶったり激しく取り乱したりする人がめったに持ちあわせないものである。
point: 後半には fancied itself strong feeling（SVOC）や、関係詞節の中の characters ... seldom possess（SVO）がある。判定するのは最初の節。
explanation: steady, observant, moderate, candid の四つの形容詞は、すべて主語 He の性質を述べる補語。骨格は He was steady＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Elinor placed all that was astonishing in this way of acting to his mother’s account; and it was happy for her that he had a mother whose character was so imperfectly known to her, as to be the general excuse for every thing strange on the part of her son.
target: it was happy for her that he had a mother whose character was so imperfectly known to her, as to be the general excuse for every thing strange on the part of her son
translation: エリナーは、彼のこうしたふるまいの驚くべき点はすべて母親のせいだと考えた。そして彼女にとって幸いなことに、彼の母親はその性格を彼女がよく知らない人だったので、息子の妙なところはなんでもその母親のせいにしておけたのである。
parts: that he had a mother whose character was so imperfectly known to her, as to be the general excuse for every thing strange on the part of her son
point: it は仮主語で、真主語は that 節。that 節の中に whose 節や so ~ as to do（…するほど~）が入り組んでいる。前の節 Elinor placed ~ は SVO。
explanation: 本当の主語は that he had a mother ~ の名詞節で、happy はその内容を評価する補語。for her は修飾語。骨格は It was happy (that ~)＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: My affection for Marianne, my thorough conviction of her attachment to me—it was all insufficient to outweigh that dread of poverty, or get the better of those false ideas of the necessity of riches, which I was naturally inclined to feel, and expensive society had increased.
target: it was all insufficient to outweigh that dread of poverty, or get the better of those false ideas of the necessity of riches, which I was naturally inclined to feel, and expensive society had increased
translation: マリアンへの愛情も、彼女が僕を愛しているという確信も――それだけではすべて、貧乏への恐れに打ち勝つにも、富が必要だというあの誤った考えを抑えるにも足りなかった。その恐れや考えは、もともと僕が抱きがちなもので、贅沢な交際がそれをさらに強めていたのだ。
parts: to outweigh that dread of poverty, or get the better of those false ideas of the necessity of riches, which I was naturally inclined to feel, and expensive society had increased
point: ダッシュの前の二つの名詞句を it で受け直している。which 節の which は feel と increased の両方の目的語。
explanation: insufficient（不十分な）は主語 it の状態を表す補語。to outweigh ~ は形容詞を限定する副詞的用法の不定詞。骨格は it was insufficient＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: In a by-yard, there was a wilderness of empty casks, which had a certain sour remembrance of better days lingering about them; but it was too sour to be accepted as a sample of the beer that was gone,—and in this respect I remember those recluses as being like most others.
target: it was too sour to be accepted as a sample of the beer that was gone
translation: 裏庭には空き樽が雑然と転がっていて、それらにはよかった昔をしのばせる酸っぱい名残がどこか漂っていた。だがそれは酸っぱすぎて、もう失われたビールの見本としては通用しなかった。――そしてこの点で、あの隠遁者たちもたいていの者と同じだったと思う。
parts: to be accepted as a sample of the beer that was gone
point: 前半の which had a certain sour remembrance ... lingering about them は have O ~ing の形。最後の remember those recluses as being ~ も O と説明語句が続く形。判定するのは but の後の節。
explanation: too ~ to do で「~すぎて…できない」。sour は主語 it（樽に残る名残）の性質を表す補語で、to be accepted ~ は too を受ける副詞的用法の不定詞。骨格は it was sour＝SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Still, as we drive along in an open carriage, this fairy marriage is real enough to fill me with a sort of wondering pity for the unfortunate people who have no part in it, but are sweeping out the shops, and going to their daily occupations.
translation: それでも、無蓋の馬車に乗って走っていくと、このおとぎ話のような結婚は十分に現実のもので、それにまったく関わりなく、店の掃除をしたり日々の仕事に出かけたりしている不運な人たちに、不思議な哀れみさえ覚えるほどだ。
parts: as we drive along in an open carriage
to fill me with a sort of wondering pity for the unfortunate people who have no part in it, but are sweeping out the shops, and going to their daily occupations
point: ~ enough to do（…するほど~）の構文。to fill me with ~ は fill O with（O を~で満たす）の形で、その中に関係詞節 who have no part in it もある。
explanation: real は主語 this fairy marriage の性質を表す補語。enough to fill ~ はその程度を表す修飾語。骨格は this fairy marriage is real＝SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: The only great occasions for Volumnia in this changed aspect of the place in Lincolnshire are those occasions, rare and widely separated, when something is to be done for the county or the country in the way of gracing a public ball.
translation: リンカンシャーのあの屋敷がこうして様変わりしたなかで、ヴォラムニアにとって唯一の晴れ舞台となるのは、公の舞踏会に花を添えるなど、州や国のために何かをすることになる、まれでたまにしかない機会である。
parts: for Volumnia in this changed aspect of the place in Lincolnshire
when something is to be done for the county or the country in the way of gracing a public ball
point: 関係副詞 when の先行詞は those occasions で、rare and widely separated という挿入をはさんで離れている。when 節の中は is to be done（be to 不定詞＋受動態）。
explanation: 主語 The only great occasions と補語 those occasions がイコールの関係で結ばれている。骨格は The occasions are those occasions＝SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Nothing is more painful to the human mind than, after the feelings have been worked up by a quick succession of events, the dead calmness of inaction and certainty which follows and deprives the soul both of hope and fear.
translation: 立て続けに起こる出来事で感情が高ぶったあと、それに続いてやって来て、魂から希望も恐れも奪い去ってしまう、行動もなく何もかも決まってしまった死んだような静けさほど、人の心にとってつらいものはない。
parts: than, after the feelings have been worked up by a quick succession of events, the dead calmness of inaction and certainty which follows and deprives the soul both of hope and fear
point: 「否定語＋比較級＋than」で最上級の意味を表す形。than の後ろに after 節が割りこみ、さらに関係詞節 which follows and deprives the soul of ~ が続く。
explanation: Nothing が主語、more painful が補語。than 以下は比較の相手を表す修飾語。骨格は Nothing is more painful＝SVC。
author: Mary Shelley
authorJa: メアリー・シェリー
workJa: フランケンシュタイン

text: His father had been our ambassador at Madrid when Isabella was young and Prim unthought of, but had retired from the diplomatic service in a capricious moment of annoyance on not being offered the Embassy at Paris, a post to which he considered that he was fully entitled by reason of his birth, his indolence, the good English of his dispatches, and his inordinate passion for pleasure.
target: His father had been our ambassador at Madrid when Isabella was young and Prim unthought of
translation: 彼の父親は、イサベル女王がまだ若く、プリムのことなど誰も考えてもいなかったころ、マドリード駐在の英国大使を務めていた。だがパリ大使のポストを与えられなかったことに腹を立て、気まぐれに外交官を辞めてしまった。そのポストは、自分の家柄、怠惰、報告書の見事な英語、そして並はずれた快楽への情熱からして、当然自分に与えられるべきだと考えていたのである。
parts: when Isabella was young and Prim unthought of
point: 後半には not being offered the Embassy（SVOO の受動態）や、to which he considered that ~ という入り組んだ関係詞節がある。判定するのは前半の節。
explanation: our ambassador は主語 His father とイコールの関係にある補語。at Madrid と when 節は修飾語。骨格は His father had been our ambassador＝SVC。
author: Oscar Wilde
authorJa: オスカー・ワイルド
workJa: ドリアン・グレイの肖像

text: There was nothing within sight to compare him with, as though he had been one of those exceptional men who can be only measured by the greatness of their fame; and his fame, remember, was the greatest thing around for many a day’s journey.
target: his fame, remember, was the greatest thing around for many a day’s journey
translation: 見わたすかぎり、彼と比べられるものは何もなかった。まるで彼が、名声の大きさでしか測れない並はずれた人間の一人であるかのように。そして彼の名声は――いいかね――何日旅しても、そのあたりでいちばん大きなものだったのだ。
point: remember は命令文が挿入されたもので、この節の動詞ではない。前半には to compare him with（with の目的語が前にある不定詞）や can be measured（受動態）がある。
explanation: the greatest thing は主語 his fame とイコールの関係にある補語。around と for many a day’s journey は修飾語。骨格は his fame was the greatest thing＝SVC。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: True, from the unmarred dead body of the whale, you may scrape off with your hand an infinitely thin, transparent substance, somewhat resembling the thinnest shreds of isinglass, only it is almost as flexible and soft as satin; that is, previous to being dried, when it not only contracts and thickens, but becomes rather hard and brittle.
target: only it is almost as flexible and soft as satin
translation: たしかに、傷のない鯨の死体からは、手でごく薄い透明な物質をこそげとることができる。それはいちばん薄いにかわの切れ端に少し似ているが、ほとんどサテンのようにしなやかでやわらかい。ただしそれは乾かす前のことで、乾くと縮んで厚くなるばかりか、かなり硬くもろくなる。
parts: as flexible and soft as satin
point: 前の you may scrape off ... a substance は目的語が後ろに回った SVO、最後の becomes rather hard and brittle も SVC。only は「ただし」という接続詞的な使い方。
explanation: as flexible and soft as satin は「サテンと同じくらいしなやかでやわらかい」で、主語 it（その物質）の性質を表す補語。骨格は it is flexible and soft＝SVC。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: You see we knew right where to put our hands on them, by your description; so we crept along on tiptoe till we got within fifteen feet of them—dark as a cellar that sumach path was—and just then I found I was going to sneeze.
target: dark as a cellar that sumach path was
translation: ほら、あんたの説明で、やつらがどこにいるかちゃんとわかってたからさ。それで忍び足でそっと進んで、十五フィートのところまで近づいたんだ――あのウルシの小道は地下室みたいに真っ暗だったよ――そしたらちょうどそのとき、くしゃみが出そうになっちゃって。
point: 補語 dark as a cellar が文頭に出た倒置文。that は関係代名詞ではなく「あの」という指示語で、that sumach path が主語。
explanation: 元の語順に戻すと That sumach path was dark as a cellar. dark は主語の状態を表す補語なので SVC。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: トム・ソーヤーの冒険

text: Monsieur the Marquis cast his eyes over the submissive faces that drooped before him, as the like of himself had drooped before Monseigneur of the Court--only the difference was, that these faces drooped merely to suffer and not to propitiate--when a grizzled mender of the roads joined the group.
target: the difference was, that these faces drooped merely to suffer and not to propitiate
translation: 侯爵閣下は、自分の前にうなだれる従順な顔の数々を見わたした。それは、彼と同類の者たちが宮廷で大殿の前にうなだれたのと同じだった――ただ違うのは、これらの顔は機嫌をとるためではなく、ただ苦しむためにうなだれていることだった――そのとき、白髪まじりの道路工夫が一団に加わった。
parts: that these faces drooped merely to suffer and not to propitiate
point: ダッシュで挟まれた挿入部分を判定する。外側の主節 cast his eyes over the faces（SVO）や、最後の joined the group（SVO）に惑わされないこと。
explanation: that 節は「違い＝その内容」を表す名詞節で、was の補語。that 節の中の drooped は自動詞、to suffer は目的を表す不定詞。骨格は the difference was that ~＝SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: She was too sprightly to allow of their walking at a slow pace on her account, but she was very grateful to be talked to, and very willing to talk to any extent: so, when they came to their part of the town, she was more brisk and vivacious than ever.
target: when they came to their part of the town, she was more brisk and vivacious than ever
translation: 彼女は元気がよすぎて、自分のためにみんながゆっくり歩くのを許さなかった。だが話しかけてもらえるのはとてもありがたがり、いくらでもしゃべりたがった。だから、町の自分たちの住む界隈に来るころには、いつにも増して快活で生き生きしていた。
parts: when they came to their part of the town
point: 前半の too sprightly to allow of ~、grateful to be talked to、willing to talk もすべて SVC で、不定詞が形容詞を限定している。判定するのは so 以下の主節。
explanation: more brisk and vivacious は主語 she の状態を表す補語（比較級）。when 節と than ever は修飾語。骨格は she was brisk and vivacious＝SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Death, a cause of terror to the sinner, is a blessed moment for him who has walked in the right path, fulfilling the duties of his station in life, attending to his morning and evening prayers, approaching the holy sacrament frequently and performing good and merciful works.
translation: 罪人にとっては恐怖の種である死も、正しい道を歩み、身分に応じた務めを果たし、朝夕の祈りを欠かさず、たびたび聖体を拝領し、善い慈悲深い行いをしてきた者にとっては、祝福された瞬間なのである。
parts: a cause of terror to the sinner

for him who has walked in the right path, fulfilling the duties of his station in life, attending to his morning and evening prayers, approaching the holy sacrament frequently and performing good and merciful works
point: him who は「~する人」を表す古風な言い方（he who）。who 節の中には walked（SV）に続いて、fulfilling the duties（他動詞＋目的語）などの分詞がずらりと並ぶ。
explanation: 主語 Death と補語 a blessed moment がイコールで結ばれている。a cause of terror ~ は主語の同格語。骨格は Death is a blessed moment＝SVC。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス
work: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

text: Our clothing was insufficient to protect us from the severe cold: we had no boots, the snow got into our shoes and melted there: our ungloved hands became numbed and covered with chilblains, as were our feet: I remember well the distracting irritation I endured from this cause every evening, when my feet inflamed; and the torture of thrusting the swelled, raw, and stiff toes into my shoes in the morning.
target: Our clothing was insufficient to protect us from the severe cold
translation: 私たちの衣服は厳しい寒さから身を守るには足りなかった。長靴はなく、雪が靴の中に入りこんでそこで溶けた。手袋のない手は、足と同じようにかじかんでしもやけだらけになった。毎晩足が炎症を起こすたびに味わった気も狂いそうなかゆみと、朝、腫れてただれてこわばった足指を靴に押しこむ苦しみを、私はよく覚えている。
parts: to protect us from the severe cold
point: この文には had no boots（SVO）、became numbed（SVC）、remember the irritation（SVO）など多くの節がコロンでつながれている。判定するのは最初の節だけ。
explanation: insufficient（不十分な）は主語 Our clothing の状態を表す補語。to protect us ~ は形容詞を限定する副詞的用法の不定詞。骨格は Our clothing was insufficient＝SVC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Not unfrequently, through Emma’s persuasion, he had some of the chosen and the best to dine with him: but evening parties were what he preferred; and, unless he fancied himself at any time unequal to company, there was scarcely an evening in the week in which Emma could not make up a card-table for him.
target: evening parties were what he preferred
translation: エマに説得されて、彼が選りすぐりの人たちを何人か夕食に招くこともたびたびあった。だが彼が好んだのは夜の集まりのほうだった。そして、自分は人の相手ができないと思いこむときでもないかぎり、エマが彼のためにカードのテーブルを用意できない夜は、一週間にほとんどなかった。
point: 前の節の had some ... to dine with him は have O to do、後ろの fancied himself unequal to company は SVOC。判定するのは but の後の節。
explanation: what he preferred（彼が好んだもの）は関係代名詞 what が作る名詞節で、主語 evening parties とイコールの補語。骨格は evening parties were what ~＝SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Anne had a moment’s astonishment on the subject herself; but it was soon lost in the pleasanter feelings which sprang from the sight of all the ingenious contrivances and nice arrangements of Captain Harville, to turn the actual space to the best account, to supply the deficiencies of lodging-house furniture, and defend the windows and doors against the winter storms to be expected.
target: Anne had a moment’s astonishment on the subject herself
translation: アンもこの件には一瞬驚いた。だがその驚きは、すぐにもっと心地よい気持ちにかき消された。ハーヴィル大佐が、実際の空間を最大限に生かし、貸家の家具の足りないところを補い、予想される冬の嵐から窓や扉を守るために施した、数々の巧みな工夫と行き届いた配置を目にしたからである。
point: 後半の it was soon lost（受動態で SV）や、関係詞節 which sprang from ~（SV）、to turn / to supply / defend と続く不定詞の列に引っぱられないこと。
explanation: had の目的語は a moment’s astonishment（一瞬の驚き）。herself は「自分も」と主語を強める再帰代名詞の強調用法で、目的語ではない。骨格は Anne had astonishment＝SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: She played over every favourite song that she had been used to play to Willoughby, every air in which their voices had been oftenest joined, and sat at the instrument gazing on every line of music that he had written out for her, till her heart was so heavy that no farther sadness could be gained; and this nourishment of grief was every day applied.
target: She played over every favourite song that she had been used to play to Willoughby, every air in which their voices had been oftenest joined
translation: 彼女は、ウィロビーに弾いて聞かせるのが常だったお気に入りの歌を、二人の声がいちばんよく重なりあった調べを、ひとつ残らず弾いた。それから楽器の前に座ったまま、彼が書き写してくれた楽譜を一行一行見つめ、もうこれ以上悲しくなりようがないほど心が重くなるまでそうしていた。そしてこの悲しみの糧は毎日与えられた。
parts: every favourite song that she had been used to play to Willoughby, every air in which their voices had been oftenest joined
point: 二つの名詞句がコンマで並び、どちらも played over の目的語。目的語が二つあるように見えて SVOO と迷いやすい。
explanation: every favourite song と every air は同じものを言い換えた同格の目的語で、「人に物を」の関係ではない。骨格は She played over every song＝SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: About a mile and a half from the cottage, along the narrow winding valley of Allenham, which issued from that of Barton, as formerly described, the girls had, in one of their earliest walks, discovered an ancient respectable looking mansion which, by reminding them a little of Norland, interested their imagination and made them wish to be better acquainted with it.
target: About a mile and a half from the cottage, along the narrow winding valley of Allenham, which issued from that of Barton, as formerly described, the girls had, in one of their earliest walks, discovered an ancient respectable looking mansion
translation: 前に述べたとおり、バートンの谷から分かれて伸びるアレナムの細く曲がりくねった谷沿い、コテージから一マイル半ほどのところで、姉妹はごく初めのころの散歩の折に、古風で立派な構えの屋敷を見つけていた。それはノーランドを少し思い出させたので、彼女たちの想像力をかき立て、もっとよく知りたいという気持ちにさせた。
parts: About a mile and a half from the cottage
along the narrow winding valley of Allenham
which issued from that of Barton
in one of their earliest walks
point: 主語 the girls が出てくるまでに場所の句が四つも続く。屋敷を説明する which 節の中には made them wish to ~（SVOC）があるが、そちらは修飾語。
explanation: had ... discovered の目的語は an ancient respectable looking mansion。骨格は the girls had discovered a mansion＝SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: As soon as I arrived I made an attempt to find my host, but the two or three people of whom I asked his whereabouts stared at me in such an amazed way, and denied so vehemently any knowledge of his movements, that I slunk off in the direction of the cocktail table—the only place in the garden where a single man could linger without looking purposeless and alone.
target: As soon as I arrived I made an attempt to find my host
translation: 着くとすぐ、ぼくは主人役を探そうとした。ところが居場所を尋ねた二、三人がひどく呆れた様子でぼくをじろじろ見て、彼の動向など知らないと猛然と否定したので、ぼくはカクテルのテーブルのほうへこそこそ逃げ出した――庭のなかで、ひとりの男が手持ちぶさたにも孤独にも見えずにぶらぶらしていられる唯一の場所へ。
point: make an attempt は「試みる」。to find my host は an attempt を説明する形容詞的用法の不定詞。後半の but 以下には denied any knowledge（目的語が後ろに回った SVO）や slunk off（SV）がある。
explanation: made の目的語は an attempt。make は「作る」以外にも、名詞と組んで行為を表す。骨格は I made an attempt＝SVO。
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
authorJa: F・スコット・フィッツジェラルド
workJa: グレート・ギャツビー

text: She had loved, she did love still, and she had all the suffering which a warm temper and a high spirit were likely to endure under the disappointment of a dear, though irrational hope, with a strong sense of ill-usage.
target: she had all the suffering which a warm temper and a high spirit were likely to endure under the disappointment of a dear, though irrational hope, with a strong sense of ill-usage
translation: 彼女は愛していたし、今もなお愛していた。そして、熱い気性と強い気位の持ち主が、理屈に合わないとはいえ大切な望みを裏切られ、ひどい仕打ちを受けたという思いを強く抱いて味わいそうな苦しみを、すべて味わっていた。
parts: which a warm temper and a high spirit were likely to endure under the disappointment of a dear, though irrational hope, with a strong sense of ill-usage
point: 前の She had loved, she did love still は目的語のない love で SV。関係代名詞 which は endure の目的語で、節の先頭に出ている。
explanation: had の目的語は all the suffering。which 以下はその suffering を説明する修飾語。骨格は she had the suffering＝SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: As for any society in Portsmouth, that could at all make amends for deficiencies at home, there were none within the circle of her father’s and mother’s acquaintance to afford her the smallest satisfaction: she saw nobody in whose favour she could wish to overcome her own shyness and reserve.
target: she saw nobody in whose favour she could wish to overcome her own shyness and reserve
translation: 家庭の物足りなさを少しでも埋め合わせてくれるようなポーツマスの社交についていえば、両親の知り合いの範囲には、彼女にほんのわずかな満足でも与えてくれる人は一人もいなかった。この人のためなら自分の内気さや遠慮を乗り越えたいと思えるような相手は、誰ひとり見当たらなかった。
parts: in whose favour she could wish to overcome her own shyness and reserve
point: コロンの前の there were none ... to afford her the smallest satisfaction の中に afford O O（SVOO）がある。in whose favour は「前置詞＋関係代名詞の所有格」。
explanation: saw の目的語は nobody。in whose favour 以下は nobody を説明する修飾語。骨格は she saw nobody＝SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: I wrote it as fervently and pathetically as I could; and when I had finished it and sent it in, I wrote out other petitions to such men in authority as I hoped were the most merciful, and drew up one to the Crown itself.
target: I wrote out other petitions to such men in authority as I hoped were the most merciful, and drew up one to the Crown itself
translation: 私はできるかぎり熱をこめ、哀切に書いた。そしてそれを書き終えて提出すると、いちばん慈悲深いと思われる権力者たちにあてて別の嘆願書を何通も書き、国王その人にあてても一通したためた。
parts: to such men in authority as I hoped were the most merciful
point: such ~ as は「~のような」。as は関係代名詞のはたらきをし、as I hoped were the most merciful では I hoped が挿入されている。
explanation: wrote out の目的語は other petitions、drew up の目的語は one（＝a petition）。to ~ はあて先を表す修飾語。骨格は I wrote out petitions＝SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: She recalled faintly an ecstasy of pain, the heavy odor of chloroform, a stupor which had deadened sensation, and an awakening to find a little new life to which she had given being, added to the great unnumbered multitude of souls that come and go.
translation: 彼女はかすかに思い出した。苦痛の恍惚、クロロホルムの重いにおい、感覚を麻痺させた昏睡、そして目覚めると、自分が命を与えた小さな新しい命が、生まれては去っていく無数の魂の群れに加わっていたことを。
parts: an ecstasy of pain, the heavy odor of chloroform, a stupor which had deadened sensation, and an awakening to find a little new life to which she had given being, added to the great unnumbered multitude of souls that come and go
point: 目的語が四つの名詞句の並列で、とても長い。最後の an awakening to find a life added to ~ の中には find O C の形がひそんでいる。
explanation: recalled の目的語は an ecstasy of pain から始まる名詞句の列全体。faintly は副詞。骨格は She recalled an ecstasy ...＝SVO。
author: Kate Chopin
authorJa: ケイト・ショパン

text: That, the lofty example of this immaculate and unimpeachable witness for the Crown, to refer to whom however unworthily was an honour, had communicated itself to the prisoner’s servant, and had engendered in him a holy determination to examine his master’s table-drawers and pockets, and secrete his papers.
target: the lofty example of this immaculate and unimpeachable witness for the Crown, to refer to whom however unworthily was an honour, had communicated itself to the prisoner’s servant
translation: すなわち、この汚れなき非の打ちどころのない国王側証人――たとえ不肖の身であれ、その名を口にすることさえ名誉であるような人物――の気高い模範が、被告の召使いにも伝わり、主人の机の引き出しやポケットを調べて書類をこっそり隠そうという神聖な決意を、その心に生じさせたのだ、と。
parts: of this immaculate and unimpeachable witness for the Crown
to refer to whom however unworthily was an honour
point: to refer to whom however unworthily was an honour は、関係代名詞 whom を含む不定詞句が主語になった関係詞節（その人に言及することが名誉だ）。後半の engendered in him a holy determination は目的語が後ろに回った SVO。
explanation: communicate itself to ~ は「（自分自身を）~に伝える」→「~に伝わる」。itself は再帰代名詞の目的語。骨格は the example had communicated itself＝SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I had often admired, as I have elsewhere described, his benignant manner towards his youthful wife; but the respectful tenderness he manifested in every reference to her on this occasion, and the almost reverential manner in which he put away from him the lightest doubt of her integrity, exalted him, in my eyes, beyond description.
target: the respectful tenderness he manifested in every reference to her on this occasion, and the almost reverential manner in which he put away from him the lightest doubt of her integrity, exalted him, in my eyes, beyond description
translation: 若い妻に対する彼の慈愛に満ちた態度には、ほかでも書いたとおり、私はたびたび感心していた。だがこのとき、彼女に触れるたびに彼が見せた敬意あふれる優しさと、彼女の誠実さへのほんのわずかな疑いさえ、ほとんど敬虔なまでの態度で退けるそのさまは、私の目には言葉に尽くせないほど彼を高めた。
parts: he manifested in every reference to her on this occasion
in which he put away from him the lightest doubt of her integrity
point: 主語が「the tenderness＋関係詞節」と「the manner＋関係詞節」の二つで、とても長い。he manifested は関係代名詞の省略（接触節）、in which ~ の中の put away the doubt も目的語が後ろに回った SVO。
explanation: 動詞 exalted（高める）の目的語は him。in my eyes と beyond description は修飾語。骨格は the tenderness and the manner exalted him＝SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: As Oliver was told that he might do what he liked with the old clothes, he gave them to a servant who had been very kind to him, and asked her to sell them to a Jew, and keep the money for herself.
target: he gave them to a servant who had been very kind to him
translation: オリヴァーは古い服を好きにしてよいと言われたので、とても親切にしてくれた女中にそれをあげ、ユダヤ人の古着屋に売って、お金は自分のものにしてほしいと頼んだ。
parts: to a servant who had been very kind to him
point: give は SVOO をとる代表的な動詞だが、give A to B の形では「人」が前置詞句になる。前の was told that ~ は SVOO の受動態、後ろの asked her to sell は SVOC。
explanation: gave の目的語は them（＝the old clothes）だけで、to a servant 以下は修飾語。骨格は he gave them＝SVO。
note: give A to B は SVOO（give B A）の書きかえとして扱われることもあるが、文型としては前置詞句を修飾語とみて SVO と判定する。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: She came and shook hands with me when she heard that I was her governess; and as I led her in to breakfast, I addressed some phrases to her in her own tongue: she replied briefly at first, but after we were seated at the table, and she had examined me some ten minutes with her large hazel eyes, she suddenly commenced chattering fluently.
target: as I led her in to breakfast, I addressed some phrases to her in her own tongue
translation: 私が自分の家庭教師だと聞くと、彼女はやって来て握手した。朝食の席へ連れていきながら、私は彼女の国の言葉でいくつか話しかけた。はじめ彼女は短く答えるだけだったが、食卓について、大きなはしばみ色の目で十分ほど私をじろじろ見ると、急に流暢にしゃべり始めた。
parts: as I led her in to breakfast
point: address は「~に話しかける」の意味では address her だが、ここでは address A to B（A を B に向ける）の形。to her は修飾語。
explanation: addressed の目的語は some phrases。to her と in her own tongue は修飾語。骨格は I addressed some phrases＝SVO。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: As in general shape the noble Sperm Whale’s head may be compared to a Roman war-chariot (especially in front, where it is so broadly rounded); so, at a broad view, the Right Whale’s head bears a rather inelegant resemblance to a gigantic galliot-toed shoe.
target: at a broad view, the Right Whale’s head bears a rather inelegant resemblance to a gigantic galliot-toed shoe
translation: 全体の形でいえば、気高いマッコウクジラの頭がローマの戦車に（とくに、ひどく幅広く丸みを帯びた前の部分は）たとえられるように、大まかに見れば、セミクジラの頭は、つま先がガリオット船のような巨大な靴にいささか不格好に似ている。
point: bear a resemblance to ~（~に似ている）は熟語。前半の As 節は may be compared to ~ という受動態で SV。
explanation: bears の目的語は a rather inelegant resemblance（似ているところ）。to ~ は似ている相手を示す修飾語。骨格は the head bears a resemblance＝SVO。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: Edgar’s coldness depressed me exceedingly; and all the way from the Grange I puzzled my brains how to put more heart into what he said, when I repeated it; and how to soften his refusal of even a few lines to console Isabella.
target: all the way from the Grange I puzzled my brains how to put more heart into what he said, when I repeated it; and how to soften his refusal of even a few lines to console Isabella
translation: エドガーさまの冷たさに、私はひどく気が沈みました。そして屋敷からずっと道々、旦那さまの言葉を伝えるときにどうやってもっと温かみを持たせたらいいか、イザベラさまを慰める数行の手紙さえ拒んだことをどうやってやわらげたらいいかと、頭をひねりつづけました。
parts: all the way from the Grange
how to put more heart into what he said, when I repeated it; and how to soften his refusal of even a few lines to console Isabella
point: puzzle one’s brains は「頭をひねる」。後ろの how to ~ が二つ目の目的語に見えて SVOO と迷いやすい。
explanation: puzzled の目的語は my brains。how to ~ は「~について」の about が省略された修飾語と考える。骨格は I puzzled my brains＝SVO。
note: how to ~ を二つ目の目的語とみる余地もあるが、「頭に方法を与える」という関係ではないので SVOO にはならない。前置詞 about の省略と考えて修飾語とする。
author: Emily Brontë
authorJa: エミリー・ブロンテ

text: He neither spoke nor loosed his hold for some five minutes, during which period he bestowed more kisses than ever he gave in his life before, I daresay: but then my mistress had kissed him first, and I plainly saw that he could hardly bear, for downright agony, to look into her face!
target: during which period he bestowed more kisses than ever he gave in his life before
translation: 五分ほどのあいだ、あの人は口もきかず腕もゆるめませんでした。そのあいだに、それまでの一生で与えたよりも多くの口づけをしたにちがいありません。でもそもそも奥さまのほうが先に口づけしたのですし、あの人が本当につらくて奥さまの顔をまともに見ることもできないでいるのが、私にははっきりわかりました。
parts: than ever he gave in his life before
point: during which period は「その期間のあいだに」という、関係形容詞 which を使った言い方。最後の could hardly bear to look は不定詞が目的語の SVO。
explanation: bestowed（与える）の目的語は more kisses。than 以下は比較の相手を表す修飾語。骨格は he bestowed more kisses＝SVO。
author: Emily Brontë
authorJa: エミリー・ブロンテ

text: I shall ere long paint to you as well as one can without canvas, something like the true form of the whale as he actually appears to the eye of the whaleman when in his own absolute body the whale is moored alongside the whale-ship so that he can be fairly stepped upon there.
target: I shall ere long paint to you as well as one can without canvas, something like the true form of the whale
translation: やがてきみたちに、画布なしでできるかぎりうまく、鯨の本当の姿に近いものを描いてみせよう。捕鯨船の男の目に実際に映る姿――鯨がそのまま丸ごとの体で捕鯨船の舷側につながれ、その上をしっかり歩けるほどになっているときの姿を。
parts: as well as one can without canvas
something like the true form of the whale
point: paint の目的語 something like ~ が、to you や as well as ~ の後ろまで遠く離れている。to you があるので SVOO と迷いやすい。
explanation: paint の目的語は something like the true form of the whale。to you は相手を表す修飾語。骨格は I shall paint something＝SVO。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: After a few words touching his qualifications, I engaged him, glad to have among my corps of copyists a man of so singularly sedate an aspect, which I thought might operate beneficially upon the flighty temper of Turkey, and the fiery one of Nippers.
target: After a few words touching his qualifications, I engaged him, glad to have among my corps of copyists a man of so singularly sedate an aspect
translation: 彼の資格について二言三言話したあと、私は彼を雇い入れた。これほど妙に落ち着いた風采の男を写字係の一団に加えられるのがうれしかったのだ。その落ち着きが、ターキーの移り気やニッパーズの短気によい影響を与えるかもしれないと思ったのである。
parts: After a few words touching his qualifications
glad to have among my corps of copyists a man of so singularly sedate an aspect
point: glad は him ではなく主語 I の気持ちを表す（being glad の分詞構文）。him glad で SVOC と読まないこと。which I thought might operate ~ は I thought が挿入された関係詞節。
explanation: engaged（雇う）の目的語は him。glad to have ~ は主語の気持ちを表す修飾語。骨格は I engaged him＝SVO。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: In that direction my windows commanded an unobstructed view of a lofty brick wall, black by age and everlasting shade; which wall required no spy-glass to bring out its lurking beauties, but for the benefit of all near-sighted spectators, was pushed up to within ten feet of my window panes.
target: In that direction my windows commanded an unobstructed view of a lofty brick wall, black by age and everlasting shade
translation: その方角では、私の窓から、年月と絶えることのない日陰で黒ずんだ高いれんが壁が、何にもさえぎられずに見わたせた。その壁は、ひそんだ美しさを引き出すのに望遠鏡など要らなかった。それどころか、近眼の見物人すべてのために、窓ガラスから十フィート以内のところまで迫り出していたのである。
parts: an unobstructed view of a lofty brick wall
black by age and everlasting shade
point: command はここでは「命令する」ではなく「（景色を）見わたす」。which wall は「その壁は」という関係形容詞の用法。
explanation: commanded の目的語は an unobstructed view of a lofty brick wall。black by ~ は wall を説明する修飾語。骨格は my windows commanded a view＝SVO。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: Every boy he encountered added another ton to his depression; and when, in desperation, he flew for refuge at last to the bosom of Huckleberry Finn and was received with a Scriptural quotation, his heart broke and he crept home and to bed realizing that he alone of all the town was lost, forever and forever.
target: Every boy he encountered added another ton to his depression
translation: 出会う少年の一人ひとりが、彼の落ちこみにさらに一トンずつ重みを加えた。そして思いあまって、とうとうハックルベリー・フィンのふところに逃げこんだものの、聖書の一節で迎えられると、彼の心は砕け、町じゅうで自分ひとりが永遠に救われないのだと悟りながら、こっそり家に帰って寝床にもぐりこんだ。
point: Every boy he encountered は関係代名詞 whom の省略（接触節）。he encountered を文の主語・動詞と読み違えないこと。
explanation: 主語は Every boy、動詞は added、目的語は another ton。to his depression は修飾語。骨格は Every boy added another ton＝SVO。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: トム・ソーヤーの冒険

text: He had a wild, lost manner of occasionally clasping his head in his hands, that had not been seen in him before; yet, he had some pleasure in the mere sound of his daughter’s voice, and invariably turned to it when she spoke.
target: He had a wild, lost manner of occasionally clasping his head in his hands, that had not been seen in him before
translation: 彼にはときおり両手で頭を抱えこむという、取り乱した途方に暮れたようなしぐさがあった。それはそれまでの彼には見られなかったものだった。それでも娘の声の響きを聞くだけで、いくらかは喜びを感じるらしく、娘が話すといつもそちらを向いた。
parts: a wild, lost manner of occasionally clasping his head in his hands
that had not been seen in him before
point: that had not been seen ~ は関係代名詞節だが、先行詞 a manner から離れている（his hands を先行詞と読まないこと）。clasping his head は前置詞 of の後の動名詞。
explanation: had の目的語は a wild, lost manner。of 以下と that 節はその manner を説明する修飾語。骨格は He had a manner＝SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: The nights were too dark for the ladies to meet again till the morrow, but Captain Harville had promised them a visit in the evening; and he came, bringing his friend also, which was more than had been expected, it having been agreed that Captain Benwick had all the appearance of being oppressed by the presence of so many strangers.
target: Captain Harville had promised them a visit in the evening
translation: 夜は暗すぎて、婦人たちは翌日まで会えなかった。だがハーヴィル大佐が晩に訪ねてくると約束していた。そして彼はやって来たが、友人まで連れてきたのは予想以上のことだった。ベンウィック大佐は大勢の見知らぬ人がいると気詰まりな様子だと、みなの意見が一致していたからである。
point: 前の節 too dark for the ladies to meet は SVC（for ~ は不定詞の意味上の主語）。promise は SVOO をとる動詞。
explanation: promised them（彼女たちに）a visit（訪問を）で「人に物を約束する」。them と a visit はイコールではない。SVOO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: She had yet another reason for wishing her children to remain where they were; a letter from her son-in-law had told her that he and his wife were to be in town before the middle of February, and she judged it right that they should sometimes see their brother.
target: a letter from her son-in-law had told her that he and his wife were to be in town before the middle of February
translation: 彼女には、子どもたちを今いる場所にとどまらせておきたい理由がもう一つあった。義理の息子からの手紙で、彼と妻が二月の半ばまでにロンドンに来ることになっていると知らされていたので、娘たちがときには兄に会うのが正しいと判断したのである。
parts: that he and his wife were to be in town before the middle of February
point: 前の wishing her children to remain（O＋to 不定詞）や、後ろの judged it right that ~（仮目的語の SVOC）に惑わされないこと。主語は人ではなく a letter。
explanation: told her（彼女に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。that 節が二つ目の目的語。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: She felt that the carriage was for herself, and herself alone: and her uncle’s consideration of her, coming immediately after such representations from her aunt, cost her some tears of gratitude when she was alone.
target: her uncle’s consideration of her, coming immediately after such representations from her aunt, cost her some tears of gratitude when she was alone
translation: 馬車は自分のため、自分ひとりのためのものなのだと彼女は感じた。伯母からあんなことを言われたすぐあとだっただけに、伯父の心づかいに、彼女はひとりになると感謝の涙をいくらか流した。
parts: coming immediately after such representations from her aunt
point: cost は「（人に）~を費やさせる」の意味で SVOO をとる。過去形も cost なので、動詞だと気づきにくい。
explanation: cost her（彼女に）some tears of gratitude（感謝の涙を）で SVOO。直訳は「伯父の心づかいは彼女に感謝の涙を費やさせた」。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: It was the sole resource; for he told me that the case must be over in five minutes when the witness was there, and that no power on earth could prevent its going against us.
target: he told me that the case must be over in five minutes when the witness was there, and that no power on earth could prevent its going against us
translation: それが唯一の手だった。というのも、証人がそこに出てくれば裁判は五分で片がつき、こちらに不利になるのはどんな力でも防げない、と彼が言ったからだ。
parts: that the case must be over in five minutes when the witness was there, and that no power on earth could prevent its going against us
point: that 節が and でつながれて二つあるが、どちらも told の二つ目の目的語。that 節の中には must be over（SVC）や could prevent its going（SVO）がある。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~ and that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: When we had had our laugh quite out, which was after some time, he told me that Miss Mowcher had quite an extensive connexion, and made herself useful to a variety of people in a variety of ways.
target: he told me that Miss Mowcher had quite an extensive connexion, and made herself useful to a variety of people in a variety of ways
translation: ひとしきり笑い終えると（それはしばらくしてからのことだったが）、彼は、ミス・モウチャーはなかなか顔が広くて、いろいろな人にいろいろなやり方で役に立っているのだと話してくれた。
parts: that Miss Mowcher had quite an extensive connexion, and made herself useful to a variety of people in a variety of ways
point: that 節の中の made herself useful（自分を役に立つものにする）は SVOC。中身の文型につられないこと。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。前の which was after some time は挿入。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: He soon fell into a gentle doze, from which he was awakened by the light of a candle: which, being brought near the bed, showed him a gentleman with a very large and loud-ticking gold watch in his hand, who felt his pulse, and said he was a great deal better.
target: which, being brought near the bed, showed him a gentleman with a very large and loud-ticking gold watch in his hand
translation: 彼はほどなく心地よくまどろんだが、ろうそくの光で目を覚まされた。ろうそくがベッドのそばに近づけられると、その光に、大きくてカチカチとうるさい金時計を手にした紳士の姿が浮かび上がった。紳士は彼の脈をとり、ずいぶんよくなったと言った。
parts: a gentleman with a very large and loud-ticking gold watch in his hand
point: コロンの後の which は前の a candle を受ける継続用法の関係代名詞で、この節の主語。
explanation: showed him（彼に）a gentleman（紳士を）で SVOO。直訳は「ろうそくは彼に紳士を見せた」。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: And Charley told me that when her father died she had kneeled down and prayed in her first sorrow that he likewise might be raised up and given back to his poor children, and that if she should never get better and should die too, she thought it likely that it might come into Tom’s mind to offer the same prayer for her.
translation: そしてチャーリーは私に話してくれた。父親が死んだとき、最初の悲しみのなかでひざまずき、父も同じように生き返らせてもらい、かわいそうな子どもたちのもとへ返してもらえますようにと祈ったこと、そしてもし自分がよくならずに死んでしまったら、トムも自分のために同じ祈りを捧げようと思いつくかもしれない、と思ったことを。
parts: that when her father died she had kneeled down and prayed in her first sorrow that he likewise might be raised up and given back to his poor children, and that if she should never get better and should die too, she thought it likely that it might come into Tom’s mind to offer the same prayer for her
point: that 節の中に、prayed that ~、thought it likely that ~（仮目的語の SVOC）、it might come into Tom’s mind to ~（仮主語）と、さらに節が入れ子になっている。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~ and that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。文の骨格だけを見れば Charley told me that ~。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Besides, there were fewer to feed; the sick could eat little; our breakfast-basins were better filled; when there was no time to prepare a regular dinner, which often happened, she would give us a large piece of cold pie, or a thick slice of bread and cheese, and this we carried away with us to the wood, where we each chose the spot we liked best, and dined sumptuously.
target: when there was no time to prepare a regular dinner, which often happened, she would give us a large piece of cold pie, or a thick slice of bread and cheese
translation: それに、食べさせる口も減っていた。病人はほとんど食べられなかったし、朝食の鉢はたっぷり満たされた。ちゃんとした昼食を用意する時間がないときは――それはよくあったが――先生は冷たいパイの大きな一切れや、パンとチーズの厚切りをくれた。私たちはそれを森へ持っていき、めいめい好きな場所を選んで、ぜいたくな食事をした。
