parts: when there was no time to prepare a regular dinner, which often happened
a large piece of cold pie, or a thick slice of bread and cheese
point: which often happened は前の節の内容全体を受ける継続用法の関係代名詞。後ろの this we carried away は目的語 this が前に出た SVO。
explanation: give us（私たちに）a large piece of cold pie（パイを）で SVOO。would は過去の習慣「よく~したものだ」。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: She brought me some warm wine and gingerbread, and appeared exceedingly good-natured; and Linton sat in the arm-chair, and I in the little rocking chair on the hearth-stone, and we laughed and talked so merrily, and found so much to say: we planned where we would go, and what we would do in summer.
target: She brought me some warm wine and gingerbread
translation: その人は温かいワインとしょうがパンを持ってきてくれて、とても機嫌がよさそうだったわ。リントンは肘かけ椅子に、私は炉石の上の小さな揺り椅子に座って、とても楽しく笑ったりしゃべったりして、話すことがいくらでもあったの。夏にはどこへ行こう、何をしようと計画したのよ。
point: 後ろには appeared good-natured（SVC）、found so much to say（SVO）、planned where we would go（SVO）など別の文型が並ぶ。判定するのは最初の節。
explanation: brought me（私に）some warm wine and gingerbread（ワインとしょうがパンを）で SVOO。
author: Emily Brontë
authorJa: エミリー・ブロンテ

text: The communication was necessarily a slow and difficult process, for Silas’s meagre power of explanation was not aided by any readiness of interpretation in Dolly, whose narrow outward experience gave her no key to strange customs, and made every novelty a source of wonder that arrested them at every step of the narrative.
target: whose narrow outward experience gave her no key to strange customs
translation: この伝え合いは、どうしても時間がかかる難しいものになった。サイラスの乏しい説明力を、ドリーの側の飲みこみの早さが助けてくれるわけでもなかったからだ。彼女は外の世界をほとんど知らなかったので、見慣れない習慣を理解する手がかりがなく、目新しいことはどれも驚きの種になって、話の一歩ごとに二人を立ち止まらせた。
point: and の後ろの made every novelty a source of wonder（目新しいものを驚きの種にした）は SVOC。同じ主語に二つの動詞が続くが、問われているのは gave の部分。
explanation: gave her（彼女に）no key（手がかりを）で SVOO。to strange customs は key を説明する修飾語。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: He had seen her who was to him simultaneously a delight and a torture, sitting in the room he had shared with her as a peculiarly privileged guest only a little earlier in the summer, and she had denied him an entrance there now.
target: she had denied him an entrance there now
translation: 彼にとって喜びであると同時に責め苦でもある彼女が、夏のほんの少し前には特別に許された客として彼と一緒に過ごしたその部屋に座っているのを、彼は見たのだった。それなのに今、彼女は彼がそこに入ることを拒んだのである。
point: 前半の had seen her ... sitting は「知覚動詞＋O＋~ing」の SVOC。deny は「人に物を与えない」という意味で SVOO をとる。
explanation: denied him（彼に）an entrance（立ち入りを）で SVOO。him と an entrance はイコールではない。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: She made a very grand appearance, having on a high head-dress, a rich gown of velvet, and a ruff done up with the famous yellow starch, of which Anne Turner, her especial friend, had taught her the secret, before this last good lady had been hanged for Sir Thomas Overbury’s murder.
target: of which Anne Turner, her especial friend, had taught her the secret
translation: 彼女はとても堂々とした姿で現れた。高い頭飾りをつけ、豪華なビロードのガウンをまとい、あの有名な黄色い糊で仕立てたひだ襟をつけていた。その糊の秘伝は、彼女の特別な友人アン・ターナーが、サー・トマス・オーヴァベリー殺しで絞首刑になる前に教えたものだった。
point: of which は the secret of the starch（糊の秘伝）の of the starch が関係代名詞になって前に出たもの。前の made a very grand appearance は SVO。
explanation: taught her（彼女に）the secret（秘伝を）で SVOO。her especial friend は Anne Turner の同格語。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン

text: As this ancient lady had the renown (which subsequently cost her no less a price than her life) of being a principal actor in all the works of necromancy that were continually going forward, the crowd gave way before her, and seemed to fear the touch of her garment, as if it carried the plague among its gorgeous folds.
target: which subsequently cost her no less a price than her life
translation: この老婦人は、絶えず行われている魔術のあらゆるわざで主役を演じているという評判を得ていたので（その評判はのちに、ほかならぬ命という代償を彼女に払わせた）、群衆は彼女の前で道をあけ、まるでその豪奢なひだの間に疫病がひそんでいるかのように、衣に触れるのを恐れている様子だった。
parts: no less a price than her life
point: 関係代名詞 which の先行詞は the renown（評判）。the renown ... of being ~ と、先行詞とそれを説明する of 句のあいだに関係詞節が割りこんでいる。
explanation: cost her（彼女に）no less a price than her life（命にほかならない代償を）で SVOO。no less ~ than … は「…にほかならない」。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン

text: It was fairly clear that Madame Olenska had not known that he was coming, though her words to Archer had hinted at the possibility; at any rate, she had evidently not told him where she was going when she left New York, and her unexplained departure had exasperated him.
target: she had evidently not told him where she was going when she left New York
translation: オレンスカ夫人が彼の来ることを知らなかったのは、かなり明らかだった。もっとも、アーチャーへの彼女の言葉はその可能性をほのめかしてはいたが。いずれにせよ、彼女はニューヨークを発つときに行き先を彼に告げていなかったのは明らかで、そのわけを言わない出発に彼はいらだっていた。
point: where she was going は間接疑問の名詞節で、told の二つ目の目的語。when she left New York は時を表す修飾語。似た形の wh- 節の役割を見分ける問題。
explanation: told him（彼に）where she was going（どこへ行くかを）で SVOO。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン
workJa: エイジ・オブ・イノセンス

text: That lady’s dread of a scene gave her an inexorableness which the greatest strength of character could not have produced, since it was independent of all considerations of right or wrong; and knowing this, Lily seldom ventured to assail it.
target: That lady’s dread of a scene gave her an inexorableness which the greatest strength of character could not have produced
translation: あの婦人は騒ぎを起こされるのをひどく恐れていて、そのせいで、どれほど強い性格でも生み出せなかったほどの頑固さを身につけていた。それは正しいか間違っているかとはまったく関係のないものだったからだ。それがわかっているので、リリーはめったにそこを突こうとはしなかった。
parts: which the greatest strength of character could not have produced
point: which 節の中の could not have produced は「~できなかっただろう」という仮定法過去完了。which は produced の目的語。
explanation: gave her（彼女に）an inexorableness（頑として動かない態度を）で SVOO。主語は人ではなく dread（恐れ）という無生物。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: We called at the door, when the maid, at Holmes’ request, showed us the boots which her master wore at the time of his death, and also a pair of the son’s, though not the pair which he had then had.
target: the maid, at Holmes’ request, showed us the boots which her master wore at the time of his death, and also a pair of the son’s
translation: 私たちが戸口を訪ねると、メイドはホームズの頼みで、主人が亡くなったときに履いていた長靴と、息子の長靴を一足見せてくれた。ただし息子のほうは、そのとき彼が履いていた一足ではなかった。
parts: the boots which her master wore at the time of his death, and also a pair of the son’s
point: when はここでは「するとそのとき」という継続用法の関係副詞。二つ目の目的語の中に、関係詞節 which her master wore が入っている。
explanation: showed us（私たちに）the boots ... and also a pair of the son’s（長靴を）で SVOO。
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorJa: アーサー・コナン・ドイル
workJa: シャーロック・ホームズの冒険

text: Having lived three years in this country, the reader, I suppose, will expect that I should, like other travellers, give him some account of the manners and customs of its inhabitants, which it was indeed my principal study to learn.
target: I should, like other travellers, give him some account of the manners and customs of its inhabitants, which it was indeed my principal study to learn
translation: この国に三年も暮らしたのだから、読者は、私がほかの旅行者たちと同じように、その住民の風俗や習慣について何か話してくれるものと期待されることだろう。それを学ぶことこそ、実際に私の主な研究だったのである。
parts: some account of the manners and customs of its inhabitants
which it was indeed my principal study to learn
point: 主節 the reader will expect that ~ は SVO で、問われているのは that 節の中。最後の which it was my principal study to learn は、which が to learn の目的語、it が仮主語という入り組んだ関係詞節。
explanation: give him（読者に）some account（話を）で SVOO。him は the reader を指す。
author: Jonathan Swift
authorJa: ジョナサン・スウィフト

text: I gave him a knife, which he was wonderfully delighted with; and I made him a belt, with a frog hanging to it, such as in England we wear hangers in; and in the frog, instead of a hanger, I gave him a hatchet, which was not only as good a weapon in some cases, but much more useful upon other occasions.
target: I gave him a knife, which he was wonderfully delighted with
translation: 私は彼にナイフを一本やった。彼はそれをたいそう喜んだ。それから剣帯を作ってやり、イングランドで短剣を下げるのに使うような剣吊りをそれにつけた。そして剣吊りには短剣のかわりに手斧を下げてやった。それは場合によっては短剣に劣らぬ武器になるだけでなく、ほかの場面ではずっと役に立った。
parts: which he was wonderfully delighted with
point: 後ろの I made him a belt も SVOO（彼にベルトを作ってやった）。which he was delighted with は前置詞 with が後ろに残った関係詞節。
explanation: gave him（彼に）a knife（ナイフを）で SVOO。which 以下は knife を説明する修飾語。
author: Daniel Defoe
authorJa: ダニエル・デフォー
workJa: ロビンソン・クルーソー

text: This household happiness did not come all at once, but John and Meg had found the key to it, and each year of married life taught them how to use it, unlocking the treasuries of real home love and mutual helpfulness, which the poorest may possess, and the richest cannot buy.
target: each year of married life taught them how to use it, unlocking the treasuries of real home love and mutual helpfulness, which the poorest may possess, and the richest cannot buy
translation: この家庭の幸せは一度にやって来たわけではなかった。だがジョンとメグはその鍵を見つけていたし、結婚生活の一年一年が、その使い方を二人に教えてくれた。そして、どんなに貧しい者でも持つことができ、どんなに金持ちでも買うことのできない、本当の家庭の愛と助け合いの宝庫を開けていったのである。
parts: unlocking the treasuries of real home love and mutual helpfulness, which the poorest may possess, and the richest cannot buy
point: how to use it は「疑問詞＋不定詞」の名詞句で、taught の二つ目の目的語。主語は人ではなく each year という無生物。
explanation: taught them（二人に）how to use it（その使い方を）で SVOO。unlocking 以下は結果を表す分詞構文の修飾語。
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorJa: ルイーザ・メイ・オルコット

text: The agony of my feelings allowed me no respite; no incident occurred from which my rage and misery could not extract its food; but a circumstance that happened when I arrived on the confines of Switzerland, when the sun had recovered its warmth and the earth again began to look green, confirmed in an especial manner the bitterness and horror of my feelings.
target: The agony of my feelings allowed me no respite
translation: 激しい苦悩は私に休む間を与えなかった。私の怒りと悲しみが糧を引き出さない出来事など、一つもなかった。だがスイスの国境に着いたとき――太陽がふたたび暖かさを取り戻し、大地がまた緑づきはじめたころ――に起きたある出来事が、私の気持ちの苦々しさと恐ろしさを、とりわけはっきりと決定的なものにした。
point: allow は allow O to do（SVOC）の形でよく出るが、ここでは後ろに不定詞がなく、名詞 no respite が続く。
explanation: allowed me（私に）no respite（休息を）で「人に物を与える」の意味の SVOO。me と no respite はイコールではない。
note: allow O to do の形なら SVOC、allow O O（人に物を許す・与える）の形なら SVOO と、後ろの形で判定が変わる。
author: Mary Shelley
authorJa: メアリー・シェリー
workJa: フランケンシュタイン

text: Jumping over forms, and creeping under tables, I made my way to one of the fire-places; there, kneeling by the high wire fender, I found Burns, absorbed, silent, abstracted from all round her by the companionship of a book, which she read by the dim glare of the embers.
target: there, kneeling by the high wire fender, I found Burns, absorbed, silent, abstracted from all round her by the companionship of a book, which she read by the dim glare of the embers
translation: 長椅子を飛び越え、テーブルの下をくぐって、私は暖炉の一つにたどりついた。そこで、高い金網の炉格子のそばにひざまずいているバーンズを見つけた。彼女は本に夢中で黙りこみ、本を友として周りのすべてから心を離して、燃えさしのほの暗い明かりでそれを読んでいた。
parts: kneeling by the high wire fender
absorbed, silent, abstracted from all round her by the companionship of a book
which she read by the dim glare of the embers
point: 前の節 I made my way to ~ は SVO。found Burns の後ろに absorbed, silent, abstracted と三つの語句が並び、どれも Burns の状態を表している。
explanation: found O C で「O が C の状態であるのを見つけた」。Burns＝absorbed, silent, abstracted の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: At the moment when Holmes struck the light I heard a low, clear whistle, but the sudden glare flashing into my weary eyes made it impossible for me to tell what it was at which my friend lashed so savagely.
target: the sudden glare flashing into my weary eyes made it impossible for me to tell what it was at which my friend lashed so savagely
translation: ホームズが明かりをつけたその瞬間、低く澄んだ口笛が聞こえた。だが、突然のまぶしい光が疲れた目に飛びこんできたので、友人があれほど激しく打ちすえているものが何なのか、私にはわからなかった。
parts: to tell what it was at which my friend lashed so savagely
point: it は仮目的語で、本当の目的語は to tell 以下。to tell の後ろには what it was（強調構文の間接疑問）と at which ~（関係詞節）が続く。
explanation: made it impossible で「それを不可能にした」。it（＝to tell ~）＝impossible の関係が成り立つので SVOC。for me は不定詞の意味上の主語。
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorJa: アーサー・コナン・ドイル
workJa: シャーロック・ホームズの冒険

text: Some people who had lost by him called him a vicious man; but he regarded horse-dealing as the finest of the arts, and might have argued plausibly that it had nothing to do with morality.
target: Some people who had lost by him called him a vicious man
translation: 彼のせいで損をした人のなかには、彼を悪人と呼ぶ者もいた。だが彼は馬の取引をあらゆる技芸のなかで最も見事なものとみなしていたし、それは道徳とはなんの関係もないと、もっともらしく論じることもできただろう。
point: 後半の regarded horse-dealing as the finest of the arts（regard A as B）も SVOC とする立場がある。who had lost by him の lose は「損をする」の自動詞。
explanation: called O C で「O を C と呼んだ」。him＝a vicious man の関係なので SVOC（SVOO ではない）。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: I found him a very patient, very forbearing, and yet an exacting master: he expected me to do a great deal; and when I fulfilled his expectations, he, in his own way, fully testified his approbation.
target: I found him a very patient, very forbearing, and yet an exacting master
translation: 彼はとても辛抱強く、とても寛容で、それでいて要求の厳しい先生だとわかった。私に多くのことを期待し、私がその期待に応えると、彼なりのやり方で十分に満足を示してくれた。
parts: a very patient, very forbearing, and yet an exacting master
point: found him a master は「彼に先生を見つけてやった」（SVOO）とも読める形。後ろの he expected me to do a great deal も SVOC。
explanation: ここでは「彼が先生である」という関係（him＝a master）が成り立ち、「彼に先生を見つけた」では意味が通らない。find O C（O が C だとわかる）の SVOC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Expansive persons found him a little dry, and very young girls thought him sarcastic; but this air of friendly aloofness, as far removed as possible from any assertion of personal advantage, was the quality which piqued Lily’s interest.
target: Expansive persons found him a little dry, and very young girls thought him sarcastic
translation: 開けっぴろげな人たちは彼をいささかそっけないと思い、ごく若い娘たちは彼を皮肉屋だと思った。だが、個人的な優位をひけらかすこととはできるかぎりかけ離れた、この親しげなよそよそしさこそが、リリーの興味をそそった資質だった。
point: 後半の this air ... was the quality（SVC）と、その中の which piqued Lily’s interest（SVO）に惑わされないこと。
explanation: found him a little dry、thought him sarcastic は、どちらも「O を C だと思う」。him＝dry、him＝sarcastic なので SVOC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: This was his system with his tenants: he allowed them to get into arrears, neglect their fences, reduce their stock, sell their straw, and otherwise go the wrong way,—and then, when he became short of money in consequence of this indulgence, he took the hardest measures and would listen to no appeal.
target: he allowed them to get into arrears, neglect their fences, reduce their stock, sell their straw, and otherwise go the wrong way
translation: これが小作人に対する彼のやり方だった。小作料を滞納させ、垣根の手入れを怠らせ、家畜を減らさせ、わらを売らせ、ほかにもいろいろと悪いほうへ向かうのを放っておく。――そして、この甘やかしのせいで自分の金が足りなくなると、このうえなく厳しい手段をとり、どんな訴えにも耳を貸さなかった。
parts: to get into arrears, neglect their fences, reduce their stock, sell their straw, and otherwise go the wrong way
point: to get の to が、neglect / reduce / sell / go にもかかっている。不定詞の中の neglect their fences などの「動詞＋目的語」に引っぱられないこと。
explanation: allow O to do（O が~するのを許す）は学校文法で SVOC。them が「滞納する」主体なので、O と C の間に主語・述語の関係がある。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: She saw them undressing in the orange light of the vanished sun, which flushed their forms with its colour; she dozed again, but she was reawakened by their voices, and quietly turned her eyes towards them.
target: She saw them undressing in the orange light of the vanished sun, which flushed their forms with its colour
translation: 沈んだ太陽の残したオレンジ色の光のなかで、彼女たちが服を脱いでいるのが見えた。その光は彼女たちの体をその色に染めていた。テスはまたまどろんだが、彼女たちの声でふたたび目を覚まし、静かにそちらへ目を向けた。
parts: in the orange light of the vanished sun
which flushed their forms with its colour
point: 知覚動詞 see＋O＋~ing の形。which flushed their forms with its colour は先行詞 light を説明する継続用法の関係詞節で SVO。
explanation: saw them undressing で「彼女たちが服を脱いでいるのを見た」。them が undressing の主体なので SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: There was a bright air and manner about her now, by which she seemed to imply that the desirability of her existence could not be questioned; and this rather saucy assumption failed in being offensive because a beholder felt it to be, upon the whole, true.
target: a beholder felt it to be, upon the whole, true
translation: いまの彼女には明るい雰囲気と物腰があり、それによって、自分という存在が望ましいものであることは疑いようがないとほのめかしているように見えた。そしてこのいささか生意気な思いこみが不快に感じられなかったのは、見る人が、それが大筋では本当だと感じたからだった。
point: to be と true のあいだに upon the whole（大筋では）が挿入されている。前半の by which she seemed to imply ~ は seem to do と imply that ~ の組み合わせ。
explanation: felt O to be C（O が C だと感じる）。it（＝その思いこみ）＝true の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: The Democrats take the offices, as a general rule, because they need them, and because the practice of many years has made it the law of political warfare, which unless a different system be proclaimed, it was weakness and cowardice to murmur at.
target: the practice of many years has made it the law of political warfare
translation: 民主党員が官職を手にするのは、たいていの場合、それが必要だからであり、また長年の慣行がそれを政争のおきてにしてしまったからである。別の制度が布告されないかぎり、そのおきてに不平を言うのは弱さであり臆病であった。
point: 最後の which ... it was weakness and cowardice to murmur at は、which が murmur at の目的語、it が仮主語という入り組んだ関係詞節。unless ~ be proclaimed は古い仮定法現在。
explanation: made it the law で「それをおきてにした」。it（官職を取ること）＝the law の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン

text: But her aunt made it a matter of high but easy irony, or comedy, and led her to ask herself if the common tone, which was all she had known, had ever been as interesting.
target: her aunt made it a matter of high but easy irony, or comedy, and led her to ask herself if the common tone, which was all she had known, had ever been as interesting
translation: だが伯母はそれを、高尚だが気楽な皮肉の、あるいは喜劇の種にしてしまい、自分がこれまで知っていた唯一のものである平凡な調子が、果たしてこれほど面白かったことがあっただろうかと、彼女に自問させた。
parts: a matter of high but easy irony, or comedy
to ask herself if the common tone, which was all she had known, had ever been as interesting
point: 二つの動詞 made と led が and で並ぶ。to ask herself if ~ の中には ask O if ~（SVOO）と、関係詞節 which was all she had known（SVC）がある。
explanation: made it a matter（それを種にした）は it＝a matter、led her to ask（彼女に自問させた）は her が ask の主体。どちらも SVOC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: Of course the circumspection of suspicious swains had never gone the length of making her a social proscript; for the number of those whose hearts, as they approached her, beat only just fast enough to remind them they had heads as well, had kept her unacquainted with the supreme disciplines of her sex and age.
target: the number of those whose hearts, as they approached her, beat only just fast enough to remind them they had heads as well, had kept her unacquainted with the supreme disciplines of her sex and age
translation: もちろん、疑り深い若者たちの用心が、彼女を社交界ののけ者にするほどまでに及んだことはなかった。というのも、彼女に近づいても、心臓はほんの少し速く打つだけで、自分には頭もあるのだと思い出させる程度にとどまる者たちが大勢いたおかげで、彼女は自分の性別と年齢にとっての最大の試練を知らずにすんでいたからである。
parts: of those whose hearts, as they approached her, beat only just fast enough to remind them they had heads as well
with the supreme disciplines of her sex and age
point: 主語 the number の後ろに、whose 節、その中の as 節、さらに remind them (that) they had heads（SVOO）と入れ子が続く。前の節 making her a social proscript も SVOC の形。
explanation: kept her unacquainted（彼女を知らないままにしておいた）。her＝unacquainted の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: Once or twice, however, while I lived at the pond, I found myself ranging the woods, like a half-starved hound, with a strange abandonment, seeking some kind of venison which I might devour, and no morsel could have been too savage for me.
target: Once or twice, however, while I lived at the pond, I found myself ranging the woods, like a half-starved hound, with a strange abandonment, seeking some kind of venison which I might devour
translation: しかし池のほとりに住んでいたあいだに一度か二度、気がつくと私は、飢えかけた猟犬のように、奇妙な捨て鉢な気分で、むさぼり食えるような何かの獣の肉を求めて森をうろついていた。どんなに野蛮なひと口でも、私にとって野蛮すぎることはなかっただろう。
parts: while I lived at the pond
seeking some kind of venison which I might devour
point: find oneself ~ing は「気がつくと~していた」。ranging the woods の中には range（歩き回る）＋the woods（目的語）がある。
explanation: found myself ranging で「自分が森をうろついているのに気づいた」。myself が ranging の主体なので SVOC。
author: Henry David Thoreau
authorJa: ヘンリー・デイヴィッド・ソロー
workJa: ウォールデン 森の生活

text: In these dialogues, my sister spoke to me as if she were morally wrenching one of my teeth out at every reference; while Pumblechook himself, self-constituted my patron, would sit supervising me with a depreciatory eye, like the architect of my fortunes who thought himself engaged on a very unremunerative job.
target: who thought himself engaged on a very unremunerative job
translation: こうしたやりとりのあいだ、姉は話題に触れるたびに、まるで私の歯を一本ずつ道義的に引き抜いているかのような口のきき方をした。一方パンブルチュックは、自分で私の後見人を気どって、さげすむような目で私を監督しながら座っていた。まるで、ひどく割に合わない仕事を請け負ってしまったと思っている、私の運命の設計者のように。
point: 関係代名詞 who の節の中を判定する。前の self-constituted my patron（自分で自分を後見人に任じた）も、O＋C の関係を含む過去分詞の句。
explanation: thought himself engaged で「自分が（仕事に）従事させられていると思った」。himself＝engaged の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I found it quite a delightful place—in front, the pretty avenue and drive by which we had approached (and where, by the by, we had cut up the gravel so terribly with our wheels that I asked the gardener to roll it); at the back, the flower-garden, with my darling at her window up there, throwing it open to smile out at me, as if she would have kissed me from that distance.
target: I found it quite a delightful place
translation: そこはとても気持ちのいい場所だった――前には、私たちがやって来た美しい並木道と車寄せ（ついでに言えば、私たちの車輪が砂利をひどく荒らしてしまったので、私は庭師にローラーをかけてくれるよう頼んだ）。裏には花園があり、上の窓辺には私の大切な人がいて、窓を開け放って私にほほえみかけ、まるでその距離から口づけしたいとでもいうようだった。
point: ダッシュの後ろは名詞句の羅列で、括弧の中の asked the gardener to roll it（ask O to do）も SVOC。where は関係副詞で、先行詞は the avenue and drive。
explanation: found it quite a delightful place で「そこがとても楽しい場所だとわかった」。it＝a delightful place の関係なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: We found him engaged with a not very hopeful pupil—a stubborn little girl with a sulky forehead, a deep voice, and an inanimate, dissatisfied mama—whose case was certainly not rendered more hopeful by the confusion into which we threw her preceptor.
target: We found him engaged with a not very hopeful pupil
translation: 行ってみると、彼はあまり見込みのなさそうな生徒の相手をしていた――ふくれっ面の額に低い声、それに気力のない不満げな母親のついた、強情な小さな女の子だった。私たちが先生をまごつかせたことで、彼女の見込みがよくならなかったのは確かである。
parts: with a not very hopeful pupil
point: ダッシュの後ろの whose case was not rendered more hopeful は render O C（O を C にする）の受動態で SVC。
explanation: found him engaged で「彼が（生徒の相手で）ふさがっているのを見つけた」。him＝engaged の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: We hustled it on to the raft in a pile, and I told Jim to float along down, and show a light when he judged he had gone about two mile, and keep it burning till I come; then I manned my oars and shoved for the light.
target: I told Jim to float along down, and show a light when he judged he had gone about two mile, and keep it burning till I come
translation: おいらたちはそれを山積みにして筏に急いで積みこんだ。そしてジムには、流れに乗って下っていって、二マイルくらい来たと思ったら明かりを見せ、おいらが行くまでずっと灯しておくように言った。それからおいらはオールを握って、明かりめざして漕ぎ出した。
parts: to float along down, and show a light when he judged he had gone about two mile, and keep it burning till I come
point: 前の We hustled it on to the raft は SVO。C の中にさらに keep it burning（O を燃やしつづける）という SVOC がある。
explanation: tell O to do（O に~するように言う）は O が不定詞の動作の主体になるので、学校文法では SVOC と考える。
note: tell O to do を「O に〈~すること〉を言う」とみて SVOO とする説明もある。このアプリでは allow / want O to do と同じく SVOC として扱う。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: ハックルベリー・フィンの冒険

text: When Buck earned sixteen hundred dollars in five minutes for John Thornton, he made it possible for his master to pay off certain debts and to journey with his partners into the East after a fabled lost mine, the history of which was as old as the history of the country.
target: he made it possible for his master to pay off certain debts and to journey with his partners into the East after a fabled lost mine, the history of which was as old as the history of the country
translation: バックがジョン・ソーントンのために五分で千六百ドルを稼いだことで、主人は借金をいくらか返し、仲間とともに、この国の歴史と同じくらい古い歴史を持つ伝説の失われた鉱山を求めて、東へ旅立つことができるようになった。
parts: to pay off certain debts and to journey with his partners into the East after a fabled lost mine, the history of which was as old as the history of the country
point: it は仮目的語で、本当の目的語は to pay off ~ and to journey ~。最後の the history of which ~ は「前置詞＋関係代名詞」が名詞の後ろに来た形。
explanation: made it possible（それを可能にした）。it（＝to pay off ~）＝possible の関係が成り立つので SVOC。for his master は不定詞の意味上の主語。
author: Jack London
authorJa: ジャック・ロンドン

text: The fact that he had money enough to do no work, and that he had left Cambridge after two terms owing to a difference with the authorities, and had then travelled and drifted, made his life strange at many points where his friends’ lives were much of a piece.
translation: 働かずにすむだけの金があること、そして当局ともめて二学期でケンブリッジを去り、それから旅をしてふらふらと過ごしたこと――その事実のせいで、友人たちの人生がほとんど似たり寄ったりになる多くの点で、彼の人生は風変わりなものになっていた。
parts: that he had money enough to do no work, and that he had left Cambridge after two terms owing to a difference with the authorities, and had then travelled and drifted
where his friends’ lives were much of a piece
point: 主語 The fact の後ろに同格の that 節が二つ続き、動詞 made が出てくるまでが長い。where 節は関係副詞で、先行詞は points。
explanation: made his life strange で「彼の人生を風変わりにした」。his life＝strange の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: In the midst of this distress, I observed them all to run away on a sudden as fast as they could; at which I ventured to leave the tree and pursue the road, wondering what it was that could put them into this fright.
target: In the midst of this distress, I observed them all to run away on a sudden as fast as they could
translation: この苦境のさなかに、私は彼らがみな突然、全速力で逃げていくのを見た。そこで思いきって木から下りて道をたどったが、いったい何が彼らをあれほどおびえさせたのだろうと不思議に思った。
parts: In the midst of this distress
point: 現代英語では知覚動詞の後ろは原形不定詞（observe them run）だが、18世紀のこの文では to がついている。後ろの what it was that could put them into this fright は強調構文の間接疑問。
explanation: observed them all to run away（彼らが逃げていくのを見た）。them が run away の主体なので SVOC。
author: Jonathan Swift
authorJa: ジョナサン・スウィフト

text: The master of the house heard with real sorrow that they were to go so soon, and repeatedly tried to persuade Miss Bennet that it would not be safe for her--that she was not enough recovered; but Jane was firm where she felt herself to be right.
target: she felt herself to be right
translation: 屋敷の主人は、二人がそんなに早く帰ることを心から残念がり、まだ十分よくなっていないのだから帰るのは危ないと、何度もミス・ベネットを説得しようとした。だがジェインは、自分が正しいと思うことについては頑として譲らなかった。
point: 主節 Jane was firm は SVC、前半の tried to persuade Miss Bennet that ~ は SVOO の形。問われているのは where 節の中。
explanation: felt herself to be right（自分が正しいと感じた）。herself＝right の関係が成り立つので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Nevertheless, so well did he succeed in that dissembling, that when with ivory leg he stepped ashore at last, no Nantucketer thought him otherwise than but naturally grieved, and that to the quick, with the terrible casualty which had overtaken him.
translation: それでも彼はその偽装にあまりにうまく成功したので、ついに象牙の義足で上陸したとき、ナンタケットの者は誰ひとり、彼が身に降りかかった恐ろしい災難を――それも骨身にしみて――ごく自然に嘆いているとしか思わなかった。
parts: that when with ivory leg he stepped ashore at last, no Nantucketer thought him otherwise than but naturally grieved, and that to the quick, with the terrible casualty which had overtaken him
point: so well が文頭に出たため did he succeed と疑問文の語順になった倒置文。that 節の中の thought him ... grieved（SVOC）に目を奪われやすい。
explanation: so ~ that …（とても~なので…）の構文。主節の動詞 succeed は自動詞で、in that dissembling は修飾語。元の語順は He succeeded so well in that dissembling that ~ で SV。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: Detailed instructions were added relative to the address of a reply, which, although they betrayed the intervention of several hands, and made it difficult to arrive at any very probable conclusion in reference to her place of concealment, made it at least not unlikely that she had written from that spot where she was stated to have been seen.
translation: 返信のあて先についても詳しい指示が書き添えられていた。その指示は、何人もの手を経ていることをうかがわせ、彼女の隠れ場所についてはっきりした結論を出すのを難しくしたものの、目撃されたと言われているあの場所から彼女が手紙を書いたということを、少なくともありえなくはないと思わせた。
parts: relative to the address of a reply

which, although they betrayed the intervention of several hands, and made it difficult to arrive at any very probable conclusion in reference to her place of concealment, made it at least not unlikely that she had written from that spot where she was stated to have been seen
point: which 節の中に made it difficult to ~ と made it not unlikely that ~ という仮目的語の SVOC が二つもある。だがどちらも関係詞節の中身。
explanation: 主節は Detailed instructions were added（受動態）。SVO の受動態は目的語が主語になるので SV と判定する。relative to ~（~に関して）は修飾語。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: They were relieved however, not by her own recollection, but by the good will of Lucy, who believed herself to be inflicting a severe disappointment when she told her that Edward certainly would not be in Harley Street on Tuesday, and even hoped to be carrying the pain still farther by persuading her that he was kept away by the extreme affection for herself, which he could not conceal when they were together.
translation: だが二人が窮地を救われたのは、彼女自身が思い出したからではなく、ルーシーの好意のおかげだった。ルーシーは、エドワードは火曜日にはハーリー街に絶対来ないと告げることで手ひどい失望を与えているつもりでいたし、さらに、彼が来ないのは、二人でいるときには隠しきれないほどの自分への強い愛情のせいだと思いこませて、その痛手をもっと深めてやろうとさえしていた。
parts: not by her own recollection, but by the good will of Lucy

who believed herself to be inflicting a severe disappointment when she told her that Edward certainly would not be in Harley Street on Tuesday, and even hoped to be carrying the pain still farther by persuading her that he was kept away by the extreme affection for herself, which he could not conceal when they were together
point: who 節の中に believed herself to be ~（SVOC）、told her that ~（SVOO）、persuading her that ~ が詰めこまれている。
explanation: 主節は They were relieved（受動態）で、by 以下は動作主を表す修飾語。受動態は SV と判定する。
note: relieved を「ほっとした」という形容詞とみれば SVC になる。ここでは by ~ で動作主が示されているので受動態として SV とした。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Here they came out into the hall, where once more the little band was greeted with curious respectful glances by the people who had not gone to church, although their clothing made it clear that they approved of Sunday to the very verge of going to church.
translation: ここで一行は広間に出た。そこでは、教会へ行かなかった人々が、またしても好奇心まじりの敬意をこめたまなざしで小さな一団を迎えた。もっともその人々の服装からは、教会へ行く一歩手前までは日曜日をよしとしていることが見てとれた。
parts: where once more the little band was greeted with curious respectful glances by the people who had not gone to church, although their clothing made it clear that they approved of Sunday to the very verge of going to church
point: 関係副詞 where の節の中に was greeted（受動態）があり、さらに although 節の中に made it clear that ~（仮目的語の SVOC）がある。
explanation: 主節は they came out into the hall。came は自動詞で、out と into the hall は方向を表す修飾語。SV。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: After they had examined the figure, and had walked on finishing their dispute, they had parted, Ladislaw lingering behind while Naumann had gone into the Hall of Statues where he again saw Dorothea, and saw her in that brooding abstraction which made her pose remarkable.
translation: 二人は像を見終え、言い争いに決着をつけながら歩きつづけたあと別れた。ラディスローはあとに残ってぐずぐずしていたが、ナウマンは彫像の間へ入っていき、そこでふたたびドロシアを見かけた。物思いに沈んだ放心のさまで、そのせいで彼女の姿はひときわ目を引いた。
parts: After they had examined the figure, and had walked on finishing their dispute
Ladislaw lingering behind while Naumann had gone into the Hall of Statues where he again saw Dorothea, and saw her in that brooding abstraction which made her pose remarkable
point: Ladislaw lingering behind は意味上の主語つきの分詞構文（独立分詞構文）。その中に saw Dorothea（SVO）や made her pose remarkable（SVOC）がある。
explanation: 主節は they had parted だけ。part（別れる）は自動詞なので SV。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: A certain mysterious feeling, consequent on the darkness, the secrecy of the revel, and the whisper in which everything was said, steals over me again, and I listen to all they tell me with a vague feeling of solemnity and awe, which makes me glad that they are all so near, and frightens me (though I feign to laugh) when Traddles pretends to see a ghost in the corner.
translation: 暗闇と、宴のひそやかさと、何もかもがささやき声で語られることから生まれる、ある不思議な感じが、またしても私を包む。そして私は、みんなが話してくれることすべてに、ぼんやりとした厳粛さと畏れを覚えながら耳を傾ける。その気持ちのせいで、みんながすぐそばにいてくれるのがうれしくなり、トラドルズが隅に幽霊が見えるふりをすると（笑うふりはするものの）怖くなる。
parts: consequent on the darkness, the secrecy of the revel, and the whisper in which everything was said
with a vague feeling of solemnity and awe
which makes me glad that they are all so near, and frightens me (though I feign to laugh) when Traddles pretends to see a ghost in the corner
point: which 節の中に makes me glad that ~（SVOC）と frightens me（SVO）がある。all they tell me は関係代名詞の省略で、tell me ~ が SVOO に見える。
explanation: steal over ~ は「（感情が）~にしのび寄る」で、steal は自動詞。listen to ~ も自動詞＋前置詞。二つの主節はどちらも SV。
note: steal over や listen to を一つの他動詞（群動詞）とみれば SVO と説明する立場もある。学校文法では「自動詞＋前置詞句」として SV とすることが多い。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: There were only a few lines, setting forth that he would leave the city that afternoon, that he had packed his trunk in good shape, that he was well, and sent her his love and begged to be affectionately remembered to all.
translation: 手紙はほんの数行だった。その午後に町を発つこと、トランクはきちんと荷造りしたこと、元気でいること、そして彼女に愛をこめて、皆によろしく伝えてほしいということが書いてあるだけだった。
parts: setting forth that he would leave the city that afternoon, that he had packed his trunk in good shape, that he was well, and sent her his love and begged to be affectionately remembered to all
point: setting forth 以下の that 節の並びの最後に sent her his love（SVOO）がある。主節は There were ~ の存在文。
explanation: There + be は「~がある」で SV。主語は only a few lines で、setting forth ~ はそれを説明する分詞句。
author: Kate Chopin
authorJa: ケイト・ショパン

text: I thought of my dead godmother, of the night when I read to her, of her frowning so fixedly and sternly in her bed, of the strange place I was going to, of the people I should find there, and what they would be like, and what they would say to me, when a voice in the coach gave me a terrible start.
translation: 私は亡くなった名づけ親のことを考えた。彼女に本を読んで聞かせたあの夜のこと、ベッドの中でじっと険しく眉をひそめていた姿のこと、これから行く見知らぬ場所のこと、そこで会う人たちのこと、その人たちがどんな人で、私に何と言うだろうかということを。そのとき、馬車の中で声がして、私はひどくびっくりした。
parts: of my dead godmother, of the night when I read to her, of her frowning so fixedly and sternly in her bed, of the strange place I was going to, of the people I should find there, and what they would be like, and what they would say to me
when a voice in the coach gave me a terrible start
point: 最後の when 節の gave me a terrible start（SVOO）に引っぱられやすい。when はここでは「するとそのとき」の意味。
explanation: think of ~ は「~のことを考える」で、think は自動詞。of ~ が何度も並んでいるが、すべて前置詞句の修飾語。骨格は I thought＝SV。
note: think of を一つの他動詞（群動詞）とみて SVO とする説明もある。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Nothing has happened to write about, except a call on Miss Norton, who has a room full of pretty things, and who was very charming, for she showed me all her treasures, and asked me if I would sometimes go with her to lectures and concerts, as her escort, if I enjoyed them.
translation: 書くほどのことは何も起きていません。ただ、ミス・ノートンを訪ねたことくらい。きれいなものでいっぱいの部屋をお持ちで、とても感じのいい方でした。宝物を全部見せてくださって、もしお好きなら、ときどきお供として一緒に講演会や音楽会に行かないかと誘ってくださったのです。
parts: except a call on Miss Norton, who has a room full of pretty things, and who was very charming, for she showed me all her treasures, and asked me if I would sometimes go with her to lectures and concerts, as her escort, if I enjoyed them
point: 後半の showed me all her treasures と asked me if ~ はどちらも SVOO だが、関係詞節に続く for 節の中にある。
explanation: 主節は Nothing has happened。happen は自動詞。to write about は Nothing を説明する形容詞的用法の不定詞で、動詞の後ろに離れて置かれている。SV。
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorJa: ルイーザ・メイ・オルコット

text: There was silence for a few moments, while Dorothea sat as if she had been turned to marble, though the life within her was so intense that her mind had never before swept in brief time over an equal range of scenes and motives.
translation: しばらく沈黙が続いた。そのあいだドロシアは大理石に変えられてしまったかのように座っていたが、内なる生命はあまりに激しく、彼女の心がこれほど短いあいだにこれほど多くの場面や動機を駆けめぐったことは、それまで一度もなかった。
parts: while Dorothea sat as if she had been turned to marble, though the life within her was so intense that her mind had never before swept in brief time over an equal range of scenes and motives
point: while 節の中に sat as if ~ had been turned（受動態）、though 節の中に was so intense that ~（SVC）がある。
explanation: There was silence は「沈黙があった」で SV。主語は silence。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: It was, that whether she was in town or out of town, whether he had been premature with her who was so hard to comprehend, or she had lost courage, or they were discovered, or some mischance or mistake, at present incomprehensible, had occurred, he must remain to confront his fortune, whatever it was.
translation: つまりこういうことだった。彼女が町にいようといまいと、あの理解しがたい女に対して自分が早まったのであれ、彼女が勇気を失ったのであれ、二人のことが露見したのであれ、今はわけのわからない何かの不運や手違いが起きたのであれ、自分はここに残って、どんなものであれ自分の運命に立ち向かわねばならない、と。
parts: that whether she was in town or out of town, whether he had been premature with her who was so hard to comprehend, or she had lost courage, or they were discovered, or some mischance or mistake, at present incomprehensible, had occurred, he must remain to confront his fortune, whatever it was
point: whether ~ or ~ が延々と続き、その中に was so hard to comprehend（SVC）や were discovered（受動態）がある。that 節の中の主節は he must remain。
explanation: It was, that ~ は「（彼の考えは）~ということだった」。that 節は It の内容を表す名詞節で補語。骨格は It was that ~＝SVC。
note: It を仮主語、that 節を真主語とみる読み方も考えられるが、was の後ろにほかの補語がないので、ここでは that 節を補語とした。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: The consequence was, that when the moon, which was full and bright (for the night was fine), came in her course to that space in the sky opposite my casement, and looked in at me through the unveiled panes, her glorious gaze roused me.
translation: その結果、満ちて明るく輝く月が（その夜は晴れていた）、軌道をたどって私の開き窓の向かいの空にさしかかり、覆いのない窓ガラス越しに私をのぞきこむと、その輝かしいまなざしに私は目を覚まされたのである。
parts: that when the moon, which was full and bright (for the night was fine), came in her course to that space in the sky opposite my casement, and looked in at me through the unveiled panes, her glorious gaze roused me
point: that 節の中に when 節があり、さらに which 節と括弧の挿入が入る。that 節の中の主節 her glorious gaze roused me は SVO。
explanation: The consequence was that ~ で「結果は~ということだった」。that 節は補語なので SVC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: It is impossible for any human being to do that which offends so deeply the divine Majesty, that which is punished by an eternity of agony, that which crucifies again the Son of God and makes a mockery of Him.
translation: 神の威厳をこれほど深く傷つけるもの、永遠の苦しみをもって罰せられるもの、神の御子をふたたび十字架にかけ、御子を嘲るもの――それを行うなど、いかなる人間にもありえないことだ。
parts: to do that which offends so deeply the divine Majesty, that which is punished by an eternity of agony, that which crucifies again the Son of God and makes a mockery of Him
point: that which ~（~するもの）が三回くり返され、offends so deeply the divine Majesty は目的語が後ろに回った SVO、makes a mockery of Him も SVO。
explanation: It は仮主語で、真主語は to do ~。impossible は補語。for any human being は不定詞の意味上の主語。骨格は It is impossible＝SVC。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス
work: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

text: The truth was, that she had objected to me as an expensive companion who did Herbert no good, and that, when Herbert had first proposed to present me to her, she had received the proposal with such very moderate warmth, that Herbert had felt himself obliged to confide the state of the case to me, with a view to the lapse of a little time before I made her acquaintance.
translation: 実のところ、彼女は私をハーバートのためにならない金のかかる仲間だとして嫌っていたのであり、ハーバートが最初に私を紹介しようと言い出したときも、その申し出をあまりに冷ややかに受けとめたので、ハーバートは、私が彼女と知り合うまでに少し時間をおこうと考えて、事情を私に打ち明けざるをえないと感じたのだった。
parts: that she had objected to me as an expensive companion who did Herbert no good, and that, when Herbert had first proposed to present me to her, she had received the proposal with such very moderate warmth, that Herbert had felt himself obliged to confide the state of the case to me, with a view to the lapse of a little time before I made her acquaintance
point: that 節の中に did Herbert no good（SVOO）や felt himself obliged to ~（SVOC）が入りこんでいる。
explanation: The truth was that ~ and that ~ で「実は~だった」。二つの that 節がそろって補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: It was really very wrong of me, because, though my chief mate was an excellent man all round, he was the victim of such black imaginings that if he did not get a letter from his wife at the expected time he would go quite distracted with rage and jealousy, lose all grip on the work, quarrel with all hands, and either weep in his cabin or develop such a ferocity of temper as all but drove the crew to the verge of mutiny.
translation: それは本当に私がいけなかった。というのも、一等航海士はどこから見ても立派な男だったが、ひどく暗い妄想に取りつかれていて、予定の時期に妻からの手紙が届かないと、怒りと嫉妬で気も狂わんばかりになり、仕事がまるで手につかなくなり、乗組員の誰かれとなく喧嘩をし、船室で泣くか、さもなければ乗組員を反乱寸前に追いこむほどの激しい癇癪を起こすかだったからだ。
parts: because, though my chief mate was an excellent man all round, he was the victim of such black imaginings that if he did not get a letter from his wife at the expected time he would go quite distracted with rage and jealousy, lose all grip on the work, quarrel with all hands, and either weep in his cabin or develop such a ferocity of temper as all but drove the crew to the verge of mutiny
point: because 節の中に though 節、such ~ that 構文、if 節、such ~ as と入れ子が続く。go quite distracted も「~になる」の SVC。
explanation: 主節は It was very wrong of me（それは私が悪かった）。wrong は主語 It の性質を表す補語で、of me は行為者を表す修飾語。SVC。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: She had been made awkward by her not wishing to receive the news in too cavalier a fashion or to seem to have connived and Polly had been made awkward not merely because allusions of that kind always made her awkward but also because she did not wish it to be thought that in her wise innocence she had divined the intention behind her mother’s tolerance.
translation: 母親のほうは、その知らせをあまりに軽々しく受けとめたくはなく、見て見ぬふりをしていたと思われたくもなかったので、ぎこちなくなっていた。ポリーのほうもぎこちなくなっていた。そういうほのめかしにはいつもぎこちなくなってしまうからというだけでなく、賢い無邪気さの陰で母親の寛大さの裏の意図を見抜いていたと思われたくなかったからでもあった。
parts: by her not wishing to receive the news in too cavalier a fashion or to seem to have connived

not merely because allusions of that kind always made her awkward but also because she did not wish it to be thought that in her wise innocence she had divined the intention behind her mother’s tolerance
point: made her awkward（SVOC）を受動態にすると She was made awkward となり、O だった her が主語になって、C の awkward だけが残る。because 節の中には wish it to be thought that ~（SVOC）もある。
explanation: SVOC の受動態は SVC と判定する。awkward は主語 She / Polly の状態を表す補語。二つの節はどちらも SVC。
note: 受動態の文型の扱いは参考書によって異なるが、このアプリでは SVOC の受動態を SVC としている。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス

text: It was so delicious to see the clouds about his bright face clearing, and to see him so heartily pleased, and to know, as it was impossible not to know, that the source of his pleasure was the goodness which was tortured by condemning, or mistrusting, or secretly accusing any one, that I saw the tears in Ada’s eyes, while she echoed his laugh, and felt them in my own.
translation: 彼の明るい顔から雲が晴れていくのを見るのも、彼が心から喜ぶのを見るのも、そして――知らずにいられるはずもないが――その喜びの源が、誰かを責めたり、疑ったり、ひそかに咎めたりすることに苦しむあの善良さなのだと知るのも、あまりにうれしくて、私は、彼の笑いに声を合わせるエイダの目に涙を見、自分の目にも涙を感じた。
parts: to see the clouds about his bright face clearing, and to see him so heartily pleased, and to know, as it was impossible not to know, that the source of his pleasure was the goodness which was tortured by condemning, or mistrusting, or secretly accusing any one
that I saw the tears in Ada’s eyes, while she echoed his laugh, and felt them in my own
point: 仮主語 It の真主語が to see ~, to see ~, to know ~ と三つも続き、so ~ that … の that がずっと後ろに来る。to see the clouds clearing、to see him pleased は知覚動詞の SVOC の形。
explanation: It は仮主語で、真主語は三つの to 不定詞。so delicious が補語。that 以下は結果を表す修飾語。骨格は It was delicious＝SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: This young girl was so handy, that after I had once or twice pulled off my clothes before her, she was able to dress and undress me, though I never gave her that trouble when she would let me do either myself.
translation: この少女はとても手先が器用で、私が彼女の前で一、二度服を脱いでみせると、もう私に服を着せたり脱がせたりできるようになった。もっとも、自分でやらせてもらえるときには、彼女にそんな手間をかけさせることは決してなかったが。
parts: that after I had once or twice pulled off my clothes before her, she was able to dress and undress me, though I never gave her that trouble when she would let me do either myself
point: that 節の中に gave her that trouble（SVOO）と let me do ~（SVOC）がある。so ~ that … の構文。
explanation: handy（器用な）は主語 This young girl の性質を表す補語。that 以下は結果を表す修飾語。SVC。
author: Jonathan Swift
authorJa: ジョナサン・スウィフト

text: When she did understand it, however, and found herself expected to believe that she had created sensations which his heart had never known before, and that everything he had done for William was to be placed to the account of his excessive and unequalled attachment to her, she was exceedingly distressed, and for some moments unable to speak.
translation: けれども、ようやくそれを理解し、自分が彼の心にかつてない感情を呼び起こしたのだと、そして彼がウィリアムのためにしてくれたことはすべて、自分へのこのうえない比類ない愛着によるものと考えるべきなのだと信じるよう求められているのに気づくと、彼女はひどく困惑し、しばらく口もきけなかった。
parts: When she did understand it, however, and found herself expected to believe that she had created sensations which his heart had never known before, and that everything he had done for William was to be placed to the account of his excessive and unequalled attachment to her
point: When 節の中の found herself expected to believe ~ は SVOC。主語 she が出てくるまでが非常に長い。
explanation: 主節は she was distressed, and unable to speak。distressed と unable はどちらも主語 she の状態を表す補語。SVC。
note: distressed を受動態の過去分詞とみれば SV と説明する立場もある。ここでは unable と並ぶ形容詞として補語とした。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: Simon Rosedale was a man who made it his business to know everything about every one, whose idea of showing himself to be at home in society was to display an inconvenient familiarity with the habits of those with whom he wished to be thought intimate.
translation: サイモン・ローズデイルは、誰のことでも何もかも知っておくのを自分の務めとしている男で、社交界で自分がくつろいでいるところを見せるには、親しいと思われたい相手の習慣について、迷惑なほどなれなれしく通じているところを見せればよいと考えていた。
parts: who made it his business to know everything about every one, whose idea of showing himself to be at home in society was to display an inconvenient familiarity with the habits of those with whom he wished to be thought intimate
point: 関係詞節が二つ続き、who 節の made it his business to know ~ は仮目的語の SVOC、whose 節の中は was to display ~（SVC）。
explanation: 主節は Simon Rosedale was a man。a man は主語とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: Poor Dorothea felt a pang at the thought that the labor of her husband’s life might be void, which left her no energy to spare for the question whether this young relative who was so much obliged to him ought not to have repressed his observation.
translation: かわいそうにドロシアは、夫の生涯の仕事が無に帰すかもしれないと思って胸が痛んだ。そのせいで、夫にこれほど恩を受けているこの若い親類が、あんなことは口に出さずにおくべきではなかったかという問題にまで気を回す余力は残っていなかった。
parts: at the thought that the labor of her husband’s life might be void
which left her no energy to spare for the question whether this young relative who was so much obliged to him ought not to have repressed his observation
point: which 節の left her no energy は「彼女に気力を残さなかった」の SVOO。主節の文型と取り違えないこと。
explanation: felt の目的語は a pang（心の痛み）。at the thought that ~ は原因を表す修飾語で、that 節は thought の同格節。SVO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: In these days before the funeral, I saw but little of Peggotty, except that, in passing up or down stairs, I always found her close to the room where my mother and her baby lay, and except that she came to me every night, and sat by my bed’s head while I went to sleep.
translation: 葬式までのその数日、私はペゴティーにほとんど会わなかった。ただ、階段を上り下りするときにはいつも、母と赤ん坊が横たわっている部屋のすぐそばに彼女がいたし、毎晩私のところへ来て、私が眠るまで枕もとに座っていてくれたけれども。
parts: In these days before the funeral

except that, in passing up or down stairs, I always found her close to the room where my mother and her baby lay, and except that she came to me every night, and sat by my bed’s head while I went to sleep
point: except that 節の中に found her close to the room（SVOC）がある。but little は「ほんの少ししか~ない」。
explanation: see little of ~ で「~にほとんど会わない」。saw の目的語は little（わずかなもの）で、but は「ほんの」。of Peggotty は修飾語。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: He had not discovered that it was necessary for him to make it worth the other’s while to buy them, or at least make him think that it was so, or to make something else which it would be worth his while to buy.
translation: 彼はまだ気づいていなかった。相手にそれを買う値打ちがあるようにしてやること、少なくともそうだと相手に思わせること、あるいは相手が買う値打ちのある別の何かを作ることが必要なのだということに。
parts: that it was necessary for him to make it worth the other’s while to buy them, or at least make him think that it was so, or to make something else which it would be worth his while to buy
point: that 節の中に、仮主語の it was necessary、make it worth ~ while to buy（仮目的語の SVOC）、make him think（SVOC）、worth his while to buy と、it を使った構文がいくつも重なる。
explanation: discovered の目的語は that 以下の名詞節全体。骨格は He had not discovered that ~＝SVO。
author: Henry David Thoreau
authorJa: ヘンリー・デイヴィッド・ソロー
workJa: ウォールデン 森の生活

text: He watched it with that strange interest in trivial things that we try to develop when things of high import make us afraid, or when we are stirred by some new emotion for which we cannot find expression, or when some thought that terrifies us lays sudden siege to the brain and calls on us to yield.
translation: 彼はそれを、あの奇妙な関心をもって見つめた。重大なことに怯えるとき、言い表しようのない新しい感情に揺さぶられるとき、あるいは恐ろしい考えが突然頭を包囲して降伏を迫るときに、私たちがつまらないものに向けようとする、あの関心である。
parts: with that strange interest in trivial things

that we try to develop when things of high import make us afraid, or when we are stirred by some new emotion for which we cannot find expression, or when some thought that terrifies us lays sudden siege to the brain and calls on us to yield
point: 関係代名詞 that の節の中に when 節が三つあり、make us afraid（SVOC）、calls on us to yield などが入っている。
explanation: watched の目的語は it。with ~ は様子を表す修飾語。SVO。
author: Oscar Wilde
authorJa: オスカー・ワイルド
workJa: ドリアン・グレイの肖像

text: The place owed much of its mysterious melancholy to the fact that it was properly entered from the second door of the house, the door that had been condemned, and that it was secured by bolts which a particularly slender little girl found it impossible to slide.
translation: その部屋の神秘的なもの悲しさの多くは、本来は家の二つめの扉――使われなくなったあの扉――から入るようになっていて、しかも、とりわけほっそりした小さな女の子には動かせないかんぬきで閉ざされていた、という事実によるものだった。
parts: to the fact that it was properly entered from the second door of the house, the door that had been condemned, and that it was secured by bolts which a particularly slender little girl found it impossible to slide
point: 最後の関係詞節 which a particularly slender little girl found it impossible to slide は仮目的語の SVOC で、which は to slide の目的語。
explanation: owe A to B は「A は B のおかげだ」。owed の目的語は much of its mysterious melancholy で、to the fact ~ は修飾語。SVO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: Beth said nothing, but wiped away her tears with the blue army sock and began to knit with all her might, losing no time in doing the duty that lay nearest her, while she resolved in her quiet little soul to be all that Father hoped to find her when the year brought round the happy coming home.
translation: ベスは何も言わず、青い軍用靴下で涙をぬぐうと、一心に編み物を始めた。いちばん手近な務めに一刻も無駄にせず取りかかりながら、その物静かな小さな心のなかで、一年がめぐってお父さんがうれしい帰宅を果たすときには、お父さんが願っているとおりの自分になっていようと決心していた。
parts: losing no time in doing the duty that lay nearest her, while she resolved in her quiet little soul to be all that Father hoped to find her when the year brought round the happy coming home
point: while 節の all that Father hoped to find her は find her ~（SVOC）の C が関係代名詞 that になって前に出たもの。
explanation: said nothing、wiped away her tears、began to knit の三つの動詞はどれも目的語をとる。to knit は名詞的用法の不定詞で began の目的語。SVO。
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorJa: ルイーザ・メイ・オルコット

text: When I had cleared it all up I had an interview with him, and finding that he would not tell me the story, I told it to him, on which he had to confess that I was right and to add the very few details which were not yet quite clear to me.
translation: すべてを解き明かしてから、私は彼と面談した。彼が事情を話そうとしないとわかると、私のほうからそれを話してやった。すると彼は、私の言うとおりだと認め、私にまだはっきりしていなかったほんのわずかな点を補うしかなかった。
parts: When I had cleared it all up
and finding that he would not tell me the story
on which he had to confess that I was right and to add the very few details which were not yet quite clear to me
point: finding that he would not tell me the story の中の tell me the story は SVOO。すぐ後の I told it to him は「物 to 人」の形。
explanation: had の目的語は an interview、told の目的語は it。to him は修飾語。二つの主節はどちらも SVO。
note: tell A to B を SVOO（tell B A）の書きかえとみる説明もあるが、このアプリでは前置詞句を修飾語として SVO とする。
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorJa: アーサー・コナン・ドイル
workJa: シャーロック・ホームズの冒険

text: Induced to take particular notice of the housekeeper, both by her own striking appearance and by Wemmick’s preparation, I observed that whenever she was in the room she kept her eyes attentively on my guardian, and that she would remove her hands from any dish she put before him, hesitatingly, as if she dreaded his calling her back, and wanted him to speak when she was nigh, if he had anything to say.
translation: 家政婦その人の目を引く風貌と、ウェミックの前置きの両方から、彼女に特に注意を払う気になった私は、気づいた。彼女は部屋にいるときはいつも後見人にじっと目を注いでいること、そして彼の前に置いた皿から、呼び戻されるのを恐れるかのように、ためらいがちに手を離し、何か言うことがあるなら自分がそばにいるうちに言ってほしいと望んでいるようだということに。
parts: Induced to take particular notice of the housekeeper, both by her own striking appearance and by Wemmick’s preparation

that whenever she was in the room she kept her eyes attentively on my guardian, and that she would remove her hands from any dish she put before him, hesitatingly, as if she dreaded his calling her back, and wanted him to speak when she was nigh, if he had anything to say
point: 文頭の Induced ~ は受動の分詞構文。that 節の中に kept her eyes on ~ や wanted him to speak（SVOC）がある。
explanation: observed の目的語は that ~ and that ~ の二つの名詞節。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Wild as my inward hurry was, and wonderful the force of the pictures that rushed by me instead of thoughts, I could yet clearly understand that, unless he had resolved that I was within a few moments of surely perishing out of all human knowledge, he would never have told me what he had told.
translation: 心の中はめちゃくちゃに急き立てられ、考えのかわりに次々と目の前を駆けぬける光景の力はすさまじかったが、それでも私にははっきりわかった。私があと数分で、誰にも知られずに確実に死ぬのだと彼が決めこんでいなかったなら、彼が話したようなことを私に話すはずがない、と。
parts: Wild as my inward hurry was, and wonderful the force of the pictures that rushed by me instead of thoughts
that, unless he had resolved that I was within a few moments of surely perishing out of all human knowledge, he would never have told me what he had told
point: Wild as ~ was は「~だけれども」という譲歩の倒置（補語 Wild が前に出た形）。and wonderful the force ... は was の省略。that 節の中に told me what ~（SVOO）がある。
explanation: 主節は I could understand that ~。understand の目的語は that 節。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Seriously apprehending that his malady would increase, unless we put some innocent deception upon him and caused him to believe that he was useful, or unless we could put him in the way of being really useful (which would be better), I made up my mind to try if Traddles could help us.
translation: 何か罪のないごまかしで彼をあざむき、自分が役に立っていると思いこませるか、あるいは（そのほうがいいのだが）本当に役立てる道に彼をつけてやるかしないかぎり、彼の病はひどくなるだろうと本気で心配になって、私はトラドルズが手を貸してくれないか当たってみようと心を決めた。
parts: Seriously apprehending that his malady would increase, unless we put some innocent deception upon him and caused him to believe that he was useful, or unless we could put him in the way of being really useful (which would be better)
to try if Traddles could help us
point: 前置きの分詞構文の中に caused him to believe that ~（SVOC）がある。主語 I が出てくるまでが長い。
explanation: make up one's mind は「決心する」。made up の目的語は my mind で、to try ~ は「~しようと」という修飾語。SVO。
note: make up one's mind to do をまとめて「~することに決める」と考え、to try ~ を目的語とみる説明もあるが、いずれにしても SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: A day or two after one of them told me that they wandered about the greater part of the night, close by their own premises, and did not get home till toward morning, by which time, as there had been several heavy showers in the mean while, and the leaves were very wet, they were drenched to their skins.
translation: 一日か二日あとで、その中の一人が話してくれたところでは、彼らは夜の大半を自分の家のすぐ近くでさまよい歩き、明け方近くまで家に帰り着けなかった。その間に何度か激しいにわか雨があり、木の葉もひどく濡れていたので、そのころには骨までずぶ濡れになっていたという。
parts: that they wandered about the greater part of the night, close by their own premises, and did not get home till toward morning, by which time, as there had been several heavy showers in the mean while, and the leaves were very wet, they were drenched to their skins
point: A day or two after の after は「その後で」という副詞。after one of them ~ と前置詞や接続詞に読まないこと。that 節の中に by which time（その時までに）という関係詞もある。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Henry David Thoreau
authorJa: ヘンリー・デイヴィッド・ソロー
workJa: ウォールデン 森の生活

text: One evening, at this hour, he told me that he had found Martha waiting near his lodging on the preceding night when he came out, and that she had asked him not to leave London on any account, until he should have seen her again.
translation: ある晩、この時刻に、彼は私に話した。前の晩に宿を出ると、マーサが近くで待っていたこと、そして、もう一度自分に会うまでは何があってもロンドンを離れないでほしいと彼女に頼まれたことを。
parts: that he had found Martha waiting near his lodging on the preceding night when he came out, and that she had asked him not to leave London on any account, until he should have seen her again
point: that 節の中の found Martha waiting（SVOC）と asked him not to leave（SVOC）に引っぱられやすい。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~ and that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: He told her that the man was employed by himself and others who were working with him in that district, to paint these reminders that no means might be left untried which might move the hearts of a wicked generation.
translation: 彼が彼女に言うには、その男は、彼自身と、この地方で一緒に働いている人々に雇われて、この警句を書いて回っているのだという。邪悪な世代の心を動かすかもしれない手段を、一つも試さずに残しておかないためだと。
parts: that the man was employed by himself and others who were working with him in that district, to paint these reminders that no means might be left untried which might move the hearts of a wicked generation
point: that 節の中に was employed（受動態）、to paint（目的の不定詞）、reminders that ~（目的を表す節）、no means might be left untried（leave O C の受動態）と続く。which の先行詞は離れた no means。
explanation: told her（彼女に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: Some time after, asking a friend at court how they came to fix on that determinate number, he told me that his majesty’s mathematicians, having taken the height of my body by the help of a quadrant, and finding it to exceed theirs in the proportion of twelve to one, they concluded from the similarity of their bodies, that mine must contain at least 1724 of theirs, and consequently would require as much food as was necessary to support that number of Lilliputians.
translation: しばらくして、宮廷の友人に、どうしてあの決まった数にしたのかと尋ねると、彼はこう教えてくれた。陛下の数学者たちが四分儀を使って私の身長を測り、それが自分たちのものの十二倍あると知ると、体つきが似ていることから、私の体には少なくとも彼らの1724人分が入るはずで、したがってその数のリリパット人を養うのに必要なだけの食べ物が要るだろうと結論したのだ、と。
parts: asking a friend at court how they came to fix on that determinate number

that his majesty’s mathematicians, having taken the height of my body by the help of a quadrant, and finding it to exceed theirs in the proportion of twelve to one, they concluded from the similarity of their bodies, that mine must contain at least 1724 of theirs, and consequently would require as much food as was necessary to support that number of Lilliputians
point: asking a friend how ~ の主語は「私」なのに、主節の主語は he（その友人）という、ずれた分詞構文。asking a friend how ~ も SVOO の形、finding it to exceed ~ は SVOC の形。
explanation: 主節は he told me that ~。told me（私に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。that 節の中では his majesty’s mathematicians を they で言い直している。
author: Jonathan Swift
authorJa: ジョナサン・スウィフト

text: He told Stephen that his name was Athy and that his father kept a lot of racehorses that were spiffing jumpers and that his father would give a good tip to Brother Michael any time he wanted it because Brother Michael was very decent and always told him the news out of the paper they got every day up in the castle.
translation: その子はスティーヴンに話した。自分の名前はアサイで、父さんは障害を跳ぶのがすごくうまい競走馬をたくさん持っていて、ブラザー・マイケルが欲しいときはいつでもいい情報を教えてあげるんだ、だってブラザー・マイケルはとてもいい人で、上のお城で毎日とっている新聞のニュースをいつも父さんに話してくれるから、と。
parts: that his name was Athy and that his father kept a lot of racehorses that were spiffing jumpers and that his father would give a good tip to Brother Michael any time he wanted it because Brother Michael was very decent and always told him the news out of the paper they got every day up in the castle
point: that 節が and で三つ続く子どもらしい語り口。中の give a good tip to Brother Michael は「物 to 人」の SVO、told him the news は SVOO。
explanation: 主節は He told Stephen that ~。Stephen（人に）と that 節（内容を）の二つの目的語をとる SVOO。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス
work: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

text: I told him that if he owed this chance to any one especially, it was to an old Scot of whom he had never heard, who had died many years ago, of whom little was remembered besides a roaring voice and a rough sort of honesty.
translation: 私は彼に言った。この機会を特に誰かのおかげだと言うなら、それは名前も聞いたことのない一人の老スコットランド人のおかげだ、と。何年も前に死んだ男で、大きな声と荒っぽい正直さのほかには、ほとんど何も覚えられていない人物だった。
parts: that if he owed this chance to any one especially, it was to an old Scot of whom he had never heard, who had died many years ago, of whom little was remembered besides a roaring voice and a rough sort of honesty
point: that 節の中は if he owed this chance to any one（owe A to B）と、強調構文に似た it was to ~ の形。関係詞 of whom が二度出てくる。
explanation: told him（彼に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: She told him that there were many handsome English ladies in India who went out on speculation, and that there were some to be picked up with property, but that neither charms nor wealth would suffice for the descendant from such a line without birth, which must ever be the first consideration.
translation: 彼女は彼に話した。インドには一旗揚げようと渡っていった美しいイギリス女性が大勢いるし、財産つきで手に入る女性もいる。けれども、あれほどの家系の末裔には、魅力も富も、家柄がなければ足りない。家柄こそ常にまず考えるべきことなのだ、と。
parts: that there were many handsome English ladies in India who went out on speculation, and that there were some to be picked up with property, but that neither charms nor wealth would suffice for the descendant from such a line without birth, which must ever be the first consideration
point: that 節が三つ（and that、but that）続き、その中に there were ~（SV）、to be picked up（受動の不定詞）、suffice（自動詞）がある。
explanation: told him（彼に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Yet I tell you that upon one particular voyage which I made to the Pacific, among many others we spoke thirty different ships, every one of which had had a death by a whale, some of them more than one, and three that had each lost a boat’s crew.
translation: だが言っておくが、私が太平洋へ出かけたある航海では、ほかにもたくさん出会ったなかで、三十隻の船と言葉を交わしたが、そのどれもが鯨のために死者を出しており、なかには二人以上の船もあり、三隻はそれぞれボート一艘分の乗組員を失っていたのだ。
parts: that upon one particular voyage which I made to the Pacific, among many others we spoke thirty different ships, every one of which had had a death by a whale, some of them more than one, and three that had each lost a boat’s crew
point: that 節の中の spoke thirty different ships の speak は「（船と）交信する」の他動詞。every one of which ~ は「そのどれもが」という関係詞。
explanation: tell you（あなたに）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: I told him that he addressed my interest or what he supposed to be my interest quite as unsuccessfully as he addressed my inclination, and he would now understand that I requested him, if he pleased, to go away immediately.
translation: 私は彼に言った。あなたが私の利益――あるいはあなたが私の利益だと思っているもの――に訴えても、私の気持ちに訴えたのとまったく同じくうまくいかない。これで、すぐにお引き取りいただきたいという私の頼みがおわかりでしょう、と。
parts: that he addressed my interest or what he supposed to be my interest quite as unsuccessfully as he addressed my inclination, and he would now understand that I requested him, if he pleased, to go away immediately
point: what he supposed to be my interest は suppose O to be C の O が what になったもの。and 以下の he would now understand ~ も told の内容（時制の一致で would）で、その中に requested him to go away（SVOC）がある。
explanation: told him（彼に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。and he would ~ も that の後ろに続く伝達内容と読む。
note: and 以下を独立した主節（SVO）と読むこともできるが、would が時制の一致による形なので、言った内容の続きと考えるのが自然。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: The man who came with the barrow told us the mail had set him down the morning before at the Royal George, that he had inquired what inns there were along the coast, and hearing ours well spoken of, I suppose, and described as lonely, had chosen it from the others for his place of residence.
translation: 手押し車を押してきた男の話では、あの客は前の日の朝、郵便馬車でロイヤル・ジョージ亭に降ろされ、海岸沿いにどんな宿があるか尋ね、たぶん私たちの宿の評判がよく、さびしい場所だと聞いて、ほかの宿をさしおいてここを住まいに選んだのだということだった。
parts: the mail had set him down the morning before at the Royal George, that he had inquired what inns there were along the coast, and hearing ours well spoken of, I suppose, and described as lonely, had chosen it from the others for his place of residence
point: 一つ目の that が省略されて told us the mail had set him down ~ となっている（二つ目には that がある）。set him down は「降ろす」の SVO。
explanation: told us（私たちに）（that）~（~ということを）で SVOO。who came with the barrow は主語を説明する関係詞節。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン

text: With tears and prayers and tender hands, Mother and sisters made her ready for the long sleep that pain would never mar again, seeing with grateful eyes the beautiful serenity that soon replaced the pathetic patience that had wrung their hearts so long, and feeling with reverent joy that to their darling death was a benignant angel, not a phantom full of dread.
translation: 涙と祈りとやさしい手で、母と姉妹は、もう二度と苦痛にかき乱されることのない長い眠りのために彼女を整えた。長いあいだ皆の胸を締めつけてきた痛ましい忍耐が、ほどなく美しい安らぎに変わったのを感謝の目で見つめ、愛する彼女にとって死は恐ろしい幻ではなく慈悲深い天使だったのだと、敬虔な喜びとともに感じながら。
parts: With tears and prayers and tender hands
for the long sleep that pain would never mar again

seeing with grateful eyes the beautiful serenity that soon replaced the pathetic patience that had wrung their hearts so long, and feeling with reverent joy that to their darling death was a benignant angel, not a phantom full of dread
point: 後半の分詞構文 seeing ~ は目的語 the beautiful serenity が後ろに回った形。feeling ~ の that 節の中は to their darling death was ~（SVC）。
explanation: made her ready で「彼女を（長い眠りの）支度ができた状態にした」。her＝ready の関係なので SVOC。
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorJa: ルイーザ・メイ・オルコット

text: The fact that the remark was in distinctly bad taste did not make it any easier to answer, for Lily was vividly aware that it was not the moment for that drawing up of her slim figure and surprised lifting of the brows by which she usually quelled incipient signs of familiarity.
translation: その言葉がはっきり悪趣味だったからといって、答えやすくなるわけではなかった。ほっそりした体をすっと伸ばし、驚いたように眉を上げる――いつもならそれで、なれなれしさの兆しを芽のうちに抑えこんでいたあのしぐさをする場面ではないと、リリーにはよくわかっていたからである。
parts: that the remark was in distinctly bad taste
for Lily was vividly aware that it was not the moment for that drawing up of her slim figure and surprised lifting of the brows by which she usually quelled incipient signs of familiarity
point: 主語 The fact に同格の that 節がつく。for 以下は理由を表す節で、was aware that ~（SVC）や by which she quelled ~（SVO）がある。
explanation: make it easier で「それをより容易にする」。it（その言葉）＝easier の関係なので SVOC。to answer は easier を限定する不定詞。
note: it を仮目的語、to answer を真の目的語とみる読み方もあるが、どちらにしても SVOC。for 以下は理由を添える部分として修飾語扱いにした。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: So I thought it a good opportunity to hint to Richard that if he were sometimes a little careless of himself, I was very sure he never meant to be careless of Ada, and that it was a part of his affectionate consideration for her not to slight the importance of a step that might influence both their lives.
translation: そこで私は、リチャードにそれとなく伝えるいい機会だと思った。たとえ自分のことにはときどき少し無頓着でも、エイダのことをないがしろにするつもりなど決してないのはよくわかっている、そして二人の人生を左右しかねない一歩の重みを軽んじないことも、彼女への思いやりの一部なのだ、と。
parts: to hint to Richard that if he were sometimes a little careless of himself, I was very sure he never meant to be careless of Ada, and that it was a part of his affectionate consideration for her not to slight the importance of a step that might influence both their lives
point: to hint 以下の that 節の中に if 節や、仮主語の it was a part of ~ not to slight ~ がある。hint to Richard that ~ の to Richard は修飾語。
explanation: thought it a good opportunity で「それをいい機会だと思った」。it＝a good opportunity の関係なので SVOC。
note: it を仮目的語、to hint ~ を真の目的語とみることもできる。to hint を opportunity を説明する形容詞的用法とみても、文型は SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Yet this made me none the happier, for even if she had not taken that tone of our being disposed of by others, I should have felt that she held my heart in her hand because she wilfully chose to do it, and not because it would have wrung any tenderness in her to crush it and throw it away.
translation: それでも、これで私が少しでも幸せになるわけではなかった。たとえ彼女が、私たちの身の振り方は他人に決められているのだというあの口調をとらなかったとしても、私はきっと感じただろう。彼女が私の心を手中に握っているのは、わざとそうしようと選んだからであって、それを握りつぶして捨てるのが彼女の優しさを少しでも痛めるからではない、と。
parts: for even if she had not taken that tone of our being disposed of by others, I should have felt that she held my heart in her hand because she wilfully chose to do it, and not because it would have wrung any tenderness in her to crush it and throw it away
point: none the + 比較級 は「少しも~ない」。for 以下には仮定法過去完了 should have felt や、held my heart in her hand（SVO）、仮主語の it would have wrung ~ to crush it がある。
explanation: made me none the happier で「私を少しも幸せにしなかった」。me＝happier の関係なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: The battle reflection that shone for an instant in the faces on the mad current made the youth feel that forceful hands from heaven would not have been able to have held him in place if he could have got intelligent control of his legs.
translation: 狂ったような人の流れのなかの顔にほんの一瞬浮かんだ戦いの照り返しを見て、若者は、もし自分の脚を思いどおりに動かせていたら、天の力強い手でさえ自分をその場に押しとどめておけなかっただろうと感じた。
parts: that shone for an instant in the faces on the mad current
feel that forceful hands from heaven would not have been able to have held him in place if he could have got intelligent control of his legs
point: 使役動詞 make の後ろは to のない原形不定詞 feel。feel の後ろの that 節には仮定法過去完了 would not have been able to have held ~ if he could have got ~ がある。
explanation: made the youth feel で「若者に感じさせた」。the youth が feel の主体なので SVOC。主語は無生物の reflection。
author: Stephen Crane
authorJa: スティーヴン・クレイン

text: In the afternoon the farmer made it known that the rick was to be finished that night, since there was a moon by which they could see to work, and the man with the engine was engaged for another farm on the morrow.
translation: 午後になって、農場主は、麦わら積みを今夜のうちに仕上げると知らせた。月が出ていて仕事ができるだけの明るさがあったし、機械を扱う男は翌日には別の農場に雇われていたからである。
parts: that the rick was to be finished that night
since there was a moon by which they could see to work, and the man with the engine was engaged for another farm on the morrow
point: it は仮目的語で、本当の目的語は that the rick was to be finished that night。since 以下は理由を表すので、that 節の中身と区別する。
explanation: make it known that ~ で「~ということを知らせる」。it（＝that 節）＝known の関係なので SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: This caused me to feel that I ought to tell her, and Caddy too, that I was going to be the mistress of Bleak House and that if I avoided that disclosure any longer I might become less worthy in my own eyes of its master’s love.
translation: そのことで私は、彼女にも、そしてキャディにも話さなければと感じた。私が荒涼館の女主人になること、そしてこれ以上打ち明けるのを先延ばしにしたら、自分の目から見ても、その主人の愛にふさわしくない人間になってしまうかもしれないということを。
parts: to feel that I ought to tell her, and Caddy too, that I was going to be the mistress of Bleak House and that if I avoided that disclosure any longer I might become less worthy in my own eyes of its master’s love
point: C の中に tell her, and Caddy too, that ~（SVOO）や become less worthy（SVC）がある。
explanation: cause O to do で「O に~させる」。me が feel の主体なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I saw him once, early on the morning of her birthday, when she came to sit in the window while we were at work (which she had always done, but now began to do with a timid and uncertain air that I thought very touching), take her forehead between his hands, kiss it, and go hurriedly away, too much moved to remain.
translation: 一度、彼女の誕生日の朝早く、私たちが仕事をしているあいだに彼女が窓辺に座りに来たとき（それはいつものことだったが、このごろはおずおずとためらいがちな様子でそうするようになっていて、それが私にはとても胸を打つものに思えた）、彼が彼女の額を両手で包み、そこに口づけして、胸がいっぱいでその場にいられずに急いで立ち去るのを、私は見た。
parts: early on the morning of her birthday, when she came to sit in the window while we were at work (which she had always done, but now began to do with a timid and uncertain air that I thought very touching)
take her forehead between his hands, kiss it, and go hurriedly away
point: 知覚動詞 saw him と、C の原形不定詞 take ~, kiss ~, go ~ のあいだに、when 節と括弧の挿入がまるごと入っている。括弧の中の that I thought very touching は think O C の O が関係代名詞になった形。
explanation: saw him take ~ で「彼が~するのを見た」。him が take / kiss / go の主体なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: I thought it my duty to give the speediest intelligence of this to my cousin, that she and her noble admirer may be aware of what they are about, and not run hastily into a marriage which has not been properly sanctioned.
translation: このことを一刻も早くいとこに知らせるのが私の務めだと考えました。彼女とその高貴な崇拝者が自分たちのしようとしていることをよくわきまえ、正式に認められていない結婚に軽はずみに飛びこんだりしないようにするためです。
parts: to give the speediest intelligence of this to my cousin
that she and her noble admirer may be aware of what they are about, and not run hastily into a marriage which has not been properly sanctioned
point: it は仮目的語で、真の目的語は to give ~。that 以下は「~するように」という目的を表す節（so that の so の省略）。
explanation: thought it my duty で「それを自分の務めだと考えた」。it（＝to give ~）＝my duty の関係なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: The shops thought it very natural that a man who, by importing direct from the producer, had daringly set aside the first great principle of provincial existence, namely that God made country villages to supply customers to county towns, should have confused ideas about the Decalogue.
translation: 商店主たちは、生産者からじかに仕入れることで、田舎暮らしの第一の大原則――つまり、神が村をつくったのは州都の町に客を供給するためだという原則――を大胆にも踏みにじった男が、十戒について混乱した考えを持っているのは、しごく当然のことだと思った。
parts: that a man who, by importing direct from the producer, had daringly set aside the first great principle of provincial existence, namely that God made country villages to supply customers to county towns, should have confused ideas about the Decalogue
point: it は仮目的語で、真の目的語は that 節。that 節の主語 a man と動詞 should have のあいだに who 節が割りこみ、その中にさらに namely that ~ という同格の節がある。
explanation: thought it very natural で「それをとても当然だと思った」。it（＝that 節）＝natural の関係なので SVOC。should は「~するとは」という感情・判断の should。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: He thought of his own father, of how he sang songs while his mother played and of how he always gave him a shilling when he asked for sixpence and he felt sorry for him that he was not a magistrate like the other boys’ fathers.
target: He thought of his own father, of how he sang songs while his mother played and of how he always gave him a shilling when he asked for sixpence
translation: 彼は自分の父親のことを考えた。母がピアノを弾くあいだ父が歌を歌ったこと、六ペンスねだるといつも一シリングくれたことを。そして、ほかの子の父親たちのように治安判事でないことを、父のために気の毒に思った。
parts: of his own father, of how he sang songs while his mother played and of how he always gave him a shilling when he asked for sixpence
point: of how ~ の中の gave him a shilling（SVOO）に引っぱられやすい。
explanation: think of ~（~のことを考える）の think は自動詞。of 以下は前置詞句の修飾語なので SV。
note: think of を一つの他動詞（群動詞）とみて SVO とする説明もある。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス
work: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

text: By this time, however, the ladies had pressed forward, curious to know what could have brought the solitary linen-weaver there under such strange circumstances, and interested in the pretty child, who, half alarmed and half attracted by the brightness and the numerous company, now frowned and hid her face, now lifted up her head again and looked round placably, until a touch or a coaxing word brought back the frown, and made her bury her face with new determination.
target: By this time, however, the ladies had pressed forward, curious to know what could have brought the solitary linen-weaver there under such strange circumstances
translation: このころにはもう婦人たちが前へ押し寄せていた。孤独な亜麻布織りがこんな妙な事情でここへ来たのはなぜなのか知りたくてたまらず、また、かわいい子どもにも興味をそそられていたのだ。子どもは、明るさと大勢の人に半ばおびえ半ば引きつけられて、顔をしかめて隠したかと思えば、また顔を上げて穏やかにあたりを見回し、そのうち誰かが触れたりあやす言葉をかけたりするとまたしかめ面に戻り、いっそう頑なに顔をうずめるのだった。
parts: curious to know what could have brought the solitary linen-weaver there under such strange circumstances
point: curious to know ~ は主語の様子を補う形容詞句（分詞構文に近い）。what could have brought ~ there の brought ~ there（SVO）に引っぱられないこと。
explanation: press forward は「前へ押し寄せる」で press は自動詞。SV。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: This was eaten on the plateless system, which is performed by placing a slice of bread upon the table, the meat flat upon the bread, a mustard plaster upon the meat, and a pinch of salt upon the whole, then cutting them vertically downwards with a large pocket-knife till wood is reached, when the severed lump is impaled on the knife, elevated, and sent the proper way of food.
target: This was eaten on the plateless system
translation: これは皿なしの流儀で食べられた。つまり、パンを一切れテーブルに置き、肉をパンの上に平らにのせ、からしをその上に塗り、全体にひとつまみの塩をふって、大きなポケットナイフで木の台に届くまでまっすぐ切り下ろす。すると切り分けられた塊はナイフに突き刺され、持ち上げられて、食べ物の行くべき道へと送られるのである。
point: 後半の is performed、is impaled、sent the proper way of food などの受動態に目を奪われやすいが、判定するのは冒頭の主節。
explanation: eat（他動詞）の受動態 was eaten。SVO の受動態は SV と判定する。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: The scene had a greatness that made it a different affair from my own scant home, and there immediately appeared at the door, with a little girl in her hand, a civil person who dropped me as decent a curtsy as if I had been the mistress or a distinguished visitor.
target: there immediately appeared at the door, with a little girl in her hand, a civil person
translation: その眺めには、私のつつましい実家とはまるで別物にしてしまうほどの壮大さがあった。そしてすぐに戸口に、小さな女の子の手を引いた礼儀正しい人が現れ、私がまるで女主人か大切な客であるかのように、うやうやしくお辞儀をした。
parts: with a little girl in her hand
point: there + appear の倒置で、主語 a civil person が最後に来る。前半の made it a different affair（SVOC）や後の dropped me a curtsy（SVOO）に引っぱられやすい。
explanation: appear（現れる）は自動詞。there は形式的に前に出ているだけで、主語は a civil person。SV。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: Anne thought she left great happiness behind her when they quitted the house; and Louisa, by whom she found herself walking, burst forth into raptures of admiration and delight on the character of the navy; their friendliness, their brotherliness, their openness, their uprightness; protesting that she was convinced of sailors having more worth and warmth than any other set of men in England; that they only knew how to live, and they only deserved to be respected and loved.
target: Louisa, by whom she found herself walking, burst forth into raptures of admiration and delight on the character of the navy
translation: その家を出るとき、アンは大きな幸せをあとに残してきたように思った。気づけば並んで歩いていたルイーザは、海軍の気風をほめたたえ、うっとりと喜びを爆発させた。その友情、兄弟のような絆、率直さ、高潔さ。船乗りはイングランドのほかのどんな人たちよりも値打ちと温かみがあると信じている、生き方を知っているのは船乗りだけで、尊敬され愛されるにふさわしいのも船乗りだけだ、と言い張って。
parts: by whom she found herself walking
into raptures of admiration and delight
on the character of the navy
point: 関係詞節 by whom she found herself walking の found herself walking は SVOC。
explanation: burst forth（ほとばしり出る）は自動詞。into ~、on ~ は修飾語。SV。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: His dog waited for his meals in a way so like that in which Oak waited for the girl’s presence, that the farmer was quite struck with the resemblance, felt it lowering, and would not look at the dog.
target: His dog waited for his meals in a way so like that in which Oak waited for the girl’s presence
translation: その犬が食事を待つ様子は、オークが娘の来るのを待つ様子にあまりにそっくりだったので、農場主はその類似にすっかり驚き、それを屈辱的に感じて、犬のほうを見ようとしなかった。
parts: in a way so like that in which Oak waited for the girl’s presence
point: 後半の felt it lowering は SVOC。that in which ~ の that は a way のくり返しを避ける代名詞。
explanation: wait for ~ の wait は自動詞。SV。
note: wait for を一つの他動詞とみて SVO とする説明もある。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
