text: Nor did my hate long confine itself to useless wishes; I began to reflect on the best means of securing him; and for this purpose, about a month after my release, I repaired to a criminal judge in the town and told him that I had an accusation to make, that I knew the destroyer of my family, and that I required him to exert his whole authority for the apprehension of the murderer.
target: for this purpose, about a month after my release, I repaired to a criminal judge in the town
translation: 私の憎しみは、むなしい願望にとどまってはいなかった。私は彼を捕らえる最善の手段を考えはじめた。そしてそのために、釈放されてひと月ほどたったころ、町の刑事裁判官のもとへ出向いて、訴えたいことがある、家族を殺した者を知っている、その殺人者を捕らえるために全権限を行使してほしい、と告げた。
parts: about a month after my release
to a criminal judge in the town
point: 後に続く told him that ~（SVOO）や required him to exert ~（SVOC）に引っぱられやすい。
explanation: repair to ~ は「~へ赴く」で repair は自動詞（修理する、ではない）。SV。
author: Mary Shelley
authorJa: メアリー・シェリー
workJa: フランケンシュタイン

text: An elderly dame, too, dwells in my neighborhood, invisible to most persons, in whose odorous herb garden I love to stroll sometimes, gathering simples and listening to her fables; for she has a genius of unequalled fertility, and her memory runs back farther than mythology, and she can tell me the original of every fable, and on what fact every one is founded, for the incidents occurred when she was young.
target: An elderly dame, too, dwells in my neighborhood, invisible to most persons, in whose odorous herb garden I love to stroll sometimes
translation: 近所には年老いた婦人も住んでいる。たいていの人の目には見えないが、香りのよいその薬草園を、私はときどき散歩するのが好きだ。薬草を摘み、彼女の作り話に耳を傾けながら。彼女は比類のない豊かな才を持ち、その記憶は神話よりも昔にさかのぼるので、どの作り話もその元の形を、そしてそれぞれがどんな事実にもとづいているかを、私に教えてくれる。その出来事は彼女が若いころに起きたのだから。
parts: in whose odorous herb garden I love to stroll sometimes
point: 後半の she can tell me the original of every fable は SVOO。
explanation: dwell（住む）は自動詞。in my neighborhood は場所の修飾語。SV。
author: Henry David Thoreau
authorJa: ヘンリー・デイヴィッド・ソロー
workJa: ウォールデン 森の生活

text: Simultaneously came from every part of the tumbling sky what may be called a shout; since, though no shout ever came near it, it was more of the nature of a shout than of anything else earthly.
target: Simultaneously came from every part of the tumbling sky what may be called a shout
translation: 同時に、崩れ落ちるような空のあらゆる方角から、叫びとでも呼べるものが聞こえてきた。叫びなどとうてい及ばないものではあったが、地上のほかの何よりも叫びに近い性質のものだったからである。
parts: from every part of the tumbling sky
what may be called a shout
point: 動詞 came が主語より先に来る倒置。主語は最後の what may be called a shout（関係代名詞 what の名詞節）。
explanation: 元の語順は What may be called a shout came from ~。come は自動詞なので SV。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: He stood by the bed in silence for some time, with his eyes turned on the dying man, but with that subdued activity of expression which showed that he was carrying on an inward debate.
target: He stood by the bed in silence for some time, with his eyes turned on the dying man
translation: 彼はしばらく黙ってベッドのそばに立ち、死にかけている男に目を向けていた。だがその表情には抑えられた動きがあり、心の中で議論を戦わせていることがうかがえた。
parts: with his eyes turned on the dying man
point: with his eyes turned ~ は「目を~に向けて」という付帯状況の with。his eyes と turned の関係は O と C に似ているが、全体で修飾語。
explanation: stand（立つ）は自動詞。SV。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: She stood talking with her cousin and Miss Van Osburgh, till a slight cloud on the latter’s brow advised her that even cousinly amenities were subject to suspicion, and Miss Bart, mindful of the necessity of not exciting enmities at this crucial point of her career, dropped aside while the happy couple proceeded toward the tea-table.
target: Miss Bart, mindful of the necessity of not exciting enmities at this crucial point of her career, dropped aside while the happy couple proceeded toward the tea-table
translation: 彼女はいとこやヴァン・オズバーグ嬢と立ち話をしていたが、やがてヴァン・オズバーグ嬢の額にかすかな曇りが見え、いとこ同士の親しさでさえ疑いの的になるのだと悟った。そこでバート嬢は、人生のこの大事な時期に敵をつくってはならないと心して、幸せな二人がお茶のテーブルへ向かうあいだ、そっと脇へ退いた。
parts: mindful of the necessity of not exciting enmities at this crucial point of her career
while the happy couple proceeded toward the tea-table
point: 前半の advised her that ~ は SVOO。主語と動詞のあいだに mindful of ~ という長い形容詞句が割りこんでいる。
explanation: drop aside（脇へ退く）の drop は自動詞。SV。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: I went to hide little Hareton, and to take the shot out of the master’s fowling-piece, which he was fond of playing with in his insane excitement, to the hazard of the lives of any who provoked, or even attracted his notice too much; and I had hit upon the plan of removing it, that he might do less mischief if he did go the length of firing the gun.
target: I went to hide little Hareton, and to take the shot out of the master’s fowling-piece
translation: 私は小さなヘアトンを隠しに行き、主人の猟銃から弾を抜きに行った。主人は正気を失った興奮の中でその銃をもてあそぶのが好きで、怒らせた者、いや、気を引きすぎた者でさえ命が危うかったのだ。それで、もし本当に引き金を引くところまでいっても害が少なくて済むように、弾を抜いておくことを思いついたのだった。
parts: to hide little Hareton, and to take the shot out of the master’s fowling-piece
point: to hide ~、to take ~ を went の目的語と取り違えやすい。これは「~するために」という目的を表す副詞的用法。
explanation: go は自動詞。SV。
author: Emily Brontë
authorJa: エミリー・ブロンテ

text: I waited till the last deep and full vibration had expired—till the tide of talk, checked an instant, had resumed its flow; I then quitted my sheltered corner and made my exit by the side-door, which was fortunately near.
target: I waited till the last deep and full vibration had expired
translation: 私は、最後の深く豊かな響きが消えるまで待った。一瞬とだえた話し声の流れがまた戻ってくるまで。それから、身を隠していた隅を離れ、運よく近くにあった横の扉から出ていった。
parts: till the last deep and full vibration had expired
point: 後半の made my exit（SVO）や quitted my sheltered corner（SVO）と混同しないこと。
explanation: wait（待つ）は自動詞。till ~ は時を表す修飾語。SV。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: When we came to the court, there was the Lord Chancellor—the same whom I had seen in his private room in Lincoln’s Inn—sitting in great state and gravity on the bench, with the mace and seals on a red table below him and an immense flat nosegay, like a little garden, which scented the whole court.
target: there was the Lord Chancellor—the same whom I had seen in his private room in Lincoln’s Inn—sitting in great state and gravity on the bench
translation: 法廷に着くと、大法官がいた。リンカーンズ・インの私室で会ったあの人が、威儀を正して重々しく判事席に座っていた。その下の赤いテーブルには職杖と印章、それに小さな庭のような大きな平たい花束が置かれ、法廷じゅうに香りを漂わせていた。
parts: the same whom I had seen in his private room in Lincoln’s Inn
sitting in great state and gravity on the bench
point: ダッシュではさまれた同格の語句と、sitting ~ の分詞が主語の後ろに続く。
explanation: there + be は「~がいる」で SV。主語は the Lord Chancellor。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: She went stealthily as a cat through this profusion of growth, gathering cuckoo-spittle on her skirts, cracking snails that were underfoot, staining her hands with thistle-milk and slug-slime, and rubbing off upon her naked arms sticky blights which, though snow-white on the apple-tree trunks, made madder stains on her skin; thus she drew quite near to Clare, still unobserved of him.
target: She went stealthily as a cat through this profusion of growth
translation: 彼女は猫のように忍び足で、このおい茂った草木の中を進んでいった。スカートにアワフキムシの泡をつけ、足もとのカタツムリを踏みつぶし、アザミの汁とナメクジのぬめりで手を汚し、むき出しの腕にべたつく虫を払いつけながら。それはリンゴの幹の上では雪のように白いのに、肌には赤黒いしみを残した。こうして彼女は、気づかれないままクレアのすぐ近くまで来た。
point: 後に続く gathering ~, cracking ~, staining ~ の分詞構文の中に目的語があるが、主節の go は目的語をとらない。made madder stains（SVO）も関係詞節の中。
explanation: go は自動詞。SV。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: They turned into the wine-shop, which was closed (for it was midnight), and where Madame Defarge immediately took her post at her desk, counted the small moneys that had been taken during her absence, examined the stock, went through the entries in the book, made other entries of her own, checked the serving man in every possible way, and finally dismissed him to bed.
target: They turned into the wine-shop, which was closed (for it was midnight)
translation: 二人は酒場に入った。店は閉まっていた（真夜中だったから）。そこでドファルジュ夫人はすぐに帳場の自分の席に着き、留守中に入った小銭を数え、在庫を調べ、帳簿の記入に目を通し、自分でも書きこみをし、給仕をあらゆる手で問いただしたうえで、最後に寝床へ下がらせた。
parts: which was closed (for it was midnight)
point: 後半の where 節に took her post、counted ~、dismissed him to bed など目的語をとる動詞が並ぶ。
explanation: turn into ~（~に入る）の turn は自動詞。SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I went back with him to the Admiral Benbow, and you cannot imagine a house in such a state of smash; the very clock had been thrown down by these fellows in their furious hunt after my mother and myself; and though nothing had actually been taken away except the captain’s money-bag and a little silver from the till, I could see at once that we were ruined.
target: I went back with him to the Admiral Benbow
translation: 私は彼と一緒にアドミラル・ベンボウ亭へ戻った。あれほどめちゃくちゃになった家は想像もつかないだろう。母と私を血まなこで探しまわった連中に、時計まで投げ倒されていたのだ。船長の金袋と帳場の銀貨が少し取られたほかは、実際には何も持ち去られていなかったが、私たちが破産したことはひと目でわかった。
point: 後の had been thrown down（受動態）や could see that ~（SVO）と区別する。
explanation: go back は自動詞。SV。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン

text: He listened eagerly to what Lydgate had to say in dissipation of his fears, though this too was only repetition; and this moment in which Bulstrode was receiving a medical opinion with a sense of comfort, seemed to make the communication of a personal need to him easier than it had been in Lydgate’s contemplation beforehand.
target: He listened eagerly to what Lydgate had to say in dissipation of his fears
translation: 彼は、自分の不安を払いのけてくれるリドゲイトの言葉に熱心に耳を傾けた。もっともそれも同じことのくり返しにすぎなかったが。そして、バルストロードが安心して医師の意見を聞いているこのときこそ、個人的な頼みごとを打ち明けるのが、リドゲイトが前もって考えていたより楽になったように思えた。
parts: to what Lydgate had to say in dissipation of his fears
point: what Lydgate had to say（リドゲイトが言わねばならないこと）は前置詞 to の目的語で、文の目的語ではない。
explanation: listen to ~ の listen は自動詞。SV。
note: listen to を一つの他動詞とみて SVO とする説明もある。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: When we turned out of the town, round a corner, and Richard told us that the post-boy, who had for a long time sympathized with our heightened expectation, was looking back and nodding, we both stood up in the carriage (Richard holding Ada lest she should be jolted down) and gazed round upon the open country and the starlight night for our destination.
target: we both stood up in the carriage (Richard holding Ada lest she should be jolted down) and gazed round upon the open country and the starlight night for our destination
translation: 町を出て角を曲がったとき、リチャードが、さっきから私たちの高まる期待に共感していた御者が振り返ってうなずいていると教えてくれたので、私たちは二人とも馬車の中で立ち上がり（リチャードはエイダが揺れて転ばないように支えていた）、行き先を探して、ひらけた野と星明かりの夜を見回した。
parts: (Richard holding Ada lest she should be jolted down)
round upon the open country and the starlight night
point: When 節の中の Richard told us that ~ は SVOO。括弧の中は独立分詞構文。
explanation: stand up と gaze はどちらも自動詞。SV。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: She looked forward to our union with placid contentment, not unmingled with a little fear, which past misfortunes had impressed, that what now appeared certain and tangible happiness might soon dissipate into an airy dream and leave no trace but deep and everlasting regret.
target: She looked forward to our union with placid contentment
translation: 彼女は穏やかな満足をもって私たちの結婚を心待ちにしていた。ただ、過去の不幸が刻みつけた小さな恐れもまじっていた。今は確かで手に取れるように見える幸福も、すぐにはかない夢と消え、深い永遠の悔いのほかには何も残さないのではないか、と。
point: 後半の leave no trace but ~ は SVO だが、that 節の中。
explanation: look forward to ~（~を楽しみに待つ）の look は自動詞。SV。
note: look forward to をひとまとまりの他動詞とみて SVO とする説明もある。
author: Mary Shelley
authorJa: メアリー・シェリー
workJa: フランケンシュタイン

text: Why, neighbours, when every one of my taties were frosted, our Parson Thirdly were the man who gave me a sack for seed, though he hardly had one for his own use, and no money to buy ’em.
target: our Parson Thirdly were the man who gave me a sack for seed
translation: だってさ、みんな、わしのジャガイモがひとつ残らず霜にやられたとき、種用にひと袋くれたのはサードリー牧師だったんだ。自分の使う分さえろくになく、それを買う金もなかったってのに。
parts: who gave me a sack for seed
point: 関係詞節 who gave me a sack for seed は SVOO。were は方言で、標準英語なら was。
explanation: the man は主語 Parson Thirdly とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: He spoke so gently to me one dear night when I was going to bed, that I was not afraid to ask him once more if you might come home; and he said Yes, you should; and sent me in a coach to bring you.
target: I was not afraid to ask him once more if you might come home
translation: ある幸せな夜、私が寝に行くときに、お父さんがとてもやさしく話しかけてくれたので、私は怖がらずにもう一度、お兄ちゃんが家に帰ってきてもいいかって聞けたの。そうしたらお父さんは、うん、いいよって言って、お兄ちゃんを迎えに私を馬車で行かせてくれたのよ。
parts: to ask him once more if you might come home
point: to ask him if ~ は SVOO の形だが、afraid を説明する不定詞句の中。
explanation: afraid は主語 I の状態を表す補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: クリスマス・キャロル

text: So tardily stole the time in this lonely place, and so eager was the spy to penetrate the motives of an interview so different from what he had been led to expect, that he more than once gave the matter up for lost, and persuaded himself, either that they had stopped far above, or had resorted to some entirely different spot to hold their mysterious conversation.
target: so eager was the spy to penetrate the motives of an interview so different from what he had been led to expect
translation: このさびしい場所では時間がのろのろと過ぎ、しかもスパイは、予想していたのとまるで違うこの会見の動機を見抜きたくてたまらなかったので、何度もあきらめかけ、二人はずっと上流で止まったのか、それとも秘密の話をするためにまったく別の場所へ行ったのだと思いこもうとした。
parts: to penetrate the motives of an interview so different from what he had been led to expect
point: 補語 so eager が文頭に出た倒置。had been led to expect は lead O to do（SVOC）の受動態。
explanation: 元の語順は The spy was so eager to penetrate ~。eager は主語の状態を表す補語なので SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: Though it would cost him a hard pang to leave her, and though he could think of no similar place in which his condemnation would not pursue him, perhaps it was almost a relief to be forced away from the endurance of the last four days, even to unknown difficulties and distresses.
target: perhaps it was almost a relief to be forced away from the endurance of the last four days
translation: 彼女と別れるのはひどくつらいだろうし、自分への非難がついて回らないような同じような場所も思いつかなかったけれど、たとえ見知らぬ苦労や悩みが待っていようと、この四日間の忍耐から無理にでも引き離されるのは、ほとんど救いだったのかもしれない。
parts: to be forced away from the endurance of the last four days
point: 前の Though 節の cost him a hard pang to leave her は SVOO（仮主語 it）。
explanation: it は仮主語で、真主語は to be forced away ~。a relief が補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I also furbished up one of the great cutlasses that I had out of the ship, and made me a belt to hang it on also; so that I was now a most formidable fellow to look at when I went abroad, if you add to the former description of myself the particular of two pistols, and a broadsword hanging at my side in a belt, but without a scabbard.
target: I was now a most formidable fellow to look at when I went abroad
translation: 私はまた、船から持ってきた大きな短剣の一本を磨き上げ、それを下げるベルトも作った。だから外へ出かけるときの私は、見るからにものすごい男になっていた。前に書いた私の姿に、ピストル二丁と、鞘はないがベルトで脇に下げた幅広の剣を加えてみてほしい。
point: 前の made me a belt to hang it on は SVOO（私のためにベルトを作った）。
explanation: a most formidable fellow は主語 I とイコールの補語。to look at は「見たところ」。SVC。
author: Daniel Defoe
authorJa: ダニエル・デフォー
workJa: ロビンソン・クルーソー

text: She was a clever young woman, who understood the art of pleasing—the art of pleasing, at least, at Kellynch Hall; and who had made herself so acceptable to Miss Elliot, as to have been already staying there more than once, in spite of all that Lady Russell, who thought it a friendship quite out of place, could hint of caution and reserve.
target: She was a clever young woman, who understood the art of pleasing
translation: 彼女は人を喜ばせるこつを心得た利口な若い女性だった。少なくともケリンチ・ホールで人を喜ばせるこつを。そしてミス・エリオットにすっかり気に入られ、すでに何度もそこに泊まっていた。この交際をまったく場違いだと考えていたレディ・ラッセルが、どれほど用心と遠慮をほのめかしてもである。
parts: who understood the art of pleasing
point: 後半の made herself so acceptable（SVOC）、thought it a friendship（SVOC）に引っぱられやすい。
explanation: a clever young woman は主語 She とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: My mind is a blank, from some time--I cannot even say what time--when I employed myself, in my captivity, in making shoes, to the time when I found myself living in London with my dear daughter here.
target: My mind is a blank
translation: ある時から――それがいつかも言えないのですが、牢獄で靴を作っていたころから――ロンドンでここにいる愛する娘と暮らしている自分に気づいた時まで、私の記憶は空白なのです。
point: 後の found myself living in London（SVOC）に目を奪われやすい。
explanation: a blank（空白）は主語 My mind とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Though he looked the phantom through and through, and saw it standing before him; though he felt the chilling influence of its death-cold eyes; and marked the very texture of the folded kerchief bound about its head and chin, which wrapper he had not observed before; he was still incredulous, and fought against his senses.
target: he was still incredulous
translation: 幽霊を隅から隅まで見つめ、それが目の前に立っているのを見、その死人のように冷たい目のぞっとする力を感じ、頭とあごに巻いた折りたたんだ布の織り目まで――前には気づかなかった布だ――はっきり見てとったのに、彼はまだ信じようとせず、自分の感覚に逆らった。
point: 長い though 節の中の saw it standing before him は SVOC。
explanation: incredulous（信じない）は主語の状態を表す補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: クリスマス・キャロル

text: The worst features of this arrangement were that, if he thought she ridiculed him, an apology would increase the offence by being disbelieved; and if he thought she wanted him to woo her, it would read like additional evidence of her forwardness.
target: The worst features of this arrangement were that, if he thought she ridiculed him, an apology would increase the offence by being disbelieved
translation: この成り行きの最悪な点は、もし彼女にばかにされたと彼が思っているなら、謝っても信じてもらえずに怒りを増すだけだろうし、もし彼女に言い寄ってほしがっていると思われているなら、それは彼女の厚かましさのさらなる証拠のように受け取られるだろう、ということだった。
parts: The worst features of this arrangement
that, if he thought she ridiculed him, an apology would increase the offence by being disbelieved
point: that 節の中の if he thought ~、would increase the offence（SVO）に引っぱられやすい。後半の wanted him to woo her は SVOC。
explanation: that 節は主語の内容を表す補語。SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Perhaps that faculty of unawareness was what gave her eyes their transparency, and her face the look of representing a type rather than a person; as if she might have been chosen to pose for a Civic Virtue or a Greek goddess.
target: Perhaps that faculty of unawareness was what gave her eyes their transparency, and her face the look of representing a type rather than a person
translation: おそらく、その無自覚という才能こそが、彼女の目に透明さを与え、顔に、一人の人間というより一つの型を表しているような趣を与えているのだった。まるで「市民の美徳」かギリシアの女神のモデルに選ばれたかのように。
parts: what gave her eyes their transparency, and her face the look of representing a type rather than a person
point: 補語の what 節の中が gave her eyes their transparency（SVOO）で、さらに her face the look ~ と O₁ O₂ がもう一組続く。
explanation: what ~ は「~するもの」という名詞節で、主語とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン
workJa: エイジ・オブ・イノセンス

text: Lydgate sat paralyzed by opposing impulses: since no reasoning he could apply to Rosamond seemed likely to conquer her assent, he wanted to smash and grind some object on which he could at least produce an impression, or else to tell her brutally that he was master, and she must obey.
target: Lydgate sat paralyzed by opposing impulses
translation: リドゲイトは相反する衝動に身動きできず座っていた。どんな理屈もロザモンドを納得させられそうにないので、せめて手ごたえの感じられる何かを叩きつぶし粉々にしたかった。さもなければ、自分が主人で、彼女は従わねばならないのだと乱暴に言い渡してやりたかった。
point: 後半の tell her brutally that ~ は SVOO。
explanation: sit + 過去分詞で「~の状態で座っている」。paralyzed は主語の状態を表す補語。SVC。
note: paralyzed を様子を表す修飾語とみて SV とする説明もある。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: She was alive to anything that gave her an opportunity for active sympathy, and at this moment it seemed as if the visit had come to shake her out of her self-absorbed discontent—to remind her of her husband’s goodness, and make her feel that she had now the right to be his helpmate in all kind deeds.
target: She was alive to anything that gave her an opportunity for active sympathy
translation: 彼女は、積極的に思いやりを示す機会を与えてくれるものには何にでも敏感だった。そしてこのときは、その訪問が、自分にかまけた不満から彼女をゆさぶり出し、夫の善良さを思い出させ、自分にはいまや夫のあらゆる善行の手助けをする権利があるのだと感じさせるために来たかのように思えた。
parts: to anything that gave her an opportunity for active sympathy
point: 関係詞節 that gave her an opportunity は SVOO、後半の make her feel that ~ は SVOC。
explanation: alive to ~ は「~に敏感な」。alive は主語の状態を表す補語。SVC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: If he had suddenly asked her what she thought of the Countess Gemini, that was doubtless a proof that he was interested in her; it could scarcely be as a help to knowledge of his own sister.
target: that was doubtless a proof that he was interested in her
translation: もし彼が突然ジェミニ伯爵夫人をどう思うかと彼女に尋ねたのなら、それはきっと彼が彼女に関心を持っている証拠だった。自分の妹のことを知る手がかりとしてでは、とうていありえなかった。
parts: that he was interested in her
point: If 節の asked her what she thought ~ は SVOO。a proof のあとの that 節は proof の内容を表す同格節。
explanation: a proof は主語 that とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: She remained fruitlessly blowing and blowing, wondering how she could have so grown out of the art which had come by nature, till she became aware of a movement among the ivy-boughs which cloaked the garden-wall no less then the cottage.
target: She remained fruitlessly blowing and blowing
translation: 彼女はむなしく何度も何度も口笛を吹きつづけた。生まれつき身についていた技を、どうしてこんなに忘れてしまったのだろうと思いながら。やがて、家ばかりでなく庭の塀まで覆っているツタの枝のあいだで、何かが動く気配に気づいた。
point: 後の became aware of ~ も SVC だが、判定するのは冒頭の主節。
explanation: remain + 現在分詞は「~しつづける」。blowing は主語の状態を表す補語。SVC。
note: remain ~ing の ~ing を主語の様子を表す修飾語とみて SV とする説明もある。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: Difficult as it is in a large city to avoid the suspicion of being watched, when the mind is conscious of danger in that regard, I could not persuade myself that any of the people within sight cared about my movements.
target: Difficult as it is in a large city to avoid the suspicion of being watched
translation: 大都会では、その点で危険を意識しているとき、見張られているのではという疑いを避けるのは難しいものだが、それでも私には、目に入る人々の誰かが私の動きを気にしているとは思えなかった。
parts: to avoid the suspicion of being watched
point: 形容詞 + as + S + V は「~だけれども」という譲歩の倒置。主節は I could not persuade myself that ~（SVO）だが、判定するのは色のついた部分。
explanation: 元の形は It is difficult in a large city to avoid ~。it は仮主語、真主語は to avoid ~、difficult が補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: But, all I had endured up to this time was nothing in comparison with the awful feelings that took possession of me when the pause was broken which ensued upon my sister’s recital, and in which pause everybody had looked at me (as I felt painfully conscious) with indignation and abhorrence.
target: all I had endured up to this time was nothing in comparison with the awful feelings that took possession of me
translation: だが、それまでに耐えてきたことはすべて、姉の話のあとに続いた沈黙が破られたときに私を襲った恐ろしい気持ちに比べれば、何でもなかった。その沈黙のあいだ、皆が（痛いほど感じたのだが）憤りと嫌悪をこめて私を見ていたのだ。
parts: all I had endured up to this time
in comparison with the awful feelings that took possession of me
point: 主語は all（that）I had endured で、関係代名詞が省略されている。took possession of me は関係詞節の中。
explanation: nothing は主語とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: This was the shocking thing; that the slime of the pit seemed to utter cries and voices; that the amorphous dust gesticulated and sinned; that what was dead, and had no shape, should usurp the offices of life.
target: This was the shocking thing
translation: ぞっとするのはこういうことだった。地獄の泥が叫びや声を発するように思えること。形のない塵が身ぶりをし、罪を犯すこと。死んで形のないものが、生命の役目を奪い取ろうとすること。
point: 後に that 節が並んで This の内容を説明する。その中の usurp the offices of life は SVO。
explanation: the shocking thing は主語 This とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
work: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
workJa: ジキル博士とハイド氏

text: What his subsequent conduct and proposals were is a matter of pure conjecture; but when an event transpired which rendered inquiry after the governess necessary, it was discovered she was gone—no one could tell when, where, or how.
target: What his subsequent conduct and proposals were is a matter of pure conjecture
translation: その後の彼のふるまいや申し出がどんなものだったかは、まったくの推測にすぎない。だが、家庭教師の行方を問いただす必要が生じるような出来事が起きたとき、彼女はいなくなっていることがわかった。いつ、どこへ、どうやってかは、誰にもわからなかった。
parts: What his subsequent conduct and proposals were
point: 主語が What ~ were という名詞節で、were の直後に is が来るので動詞を見失いやすい。後半の rendered inquiry necessary は SVOC。
explanation: a matter of pure conjecture は主語の名詞節とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: It was pleasant in the summer forenoons—when the fervent heat, that almost liquefied the rest of the human family, merely communicated a genial warmth to their half torpid systems—it was pleasant to hear them chatting in the back entry, a row of them all tipped against the wall, as usual; while the frozen witticisms of past generations were thawed out, and came bubbling with laughter from their lips.
target: it was pleasant to hear them chatting in the back entry
translation: 夏の午前中は楽しかった。人類のほかの者たちを溶かしてしまいそうな猛暑も、彼らの半ば眠ったような体にはほどよいぬくもりを伝えるだけで、その季節には、裏口の通路で、いつものように壁に椅子を傾けて一列に並んだ彼らがおしゃべりするのを聞くのは楽しかった。過ぎ去った世代の凍りついた冗談が溶け出して、笑いとともに口から湧き出てくるのだった。
parts: to hear them chatting in the back entry
point: 真主語の中の hear them chatting は知覚動詞の SVOC の形。
explanation: it は仮主語で真主語は to hear ~。pleasant が補語。SVC。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン

text: It was not a bright or splendid summer evening, though fair and soft: the haymakers were at work all along the road; and the sky, though far from cloudless, was such as promised well for the future: its blue—where blue was visible—was mild and settled, and its cloud strata high and thin.
target: the sky, though far from cloudless, was such as promised well for the future
translation: 明るくまばゆい夏の夕べではなかったが、穏やかでおだやかだった。干し草作りの人たちが道沿いに働いていた。空は、雲ひとつないとはとても言えないものの、先行きのよさを約束するような空だった。青の見えるところは、その青が穏やかで落ち着き、雲の層は高く薄かった。
parts: such as promised well for the future
point: such as ~ の as は関係代名詞のはたらきをし、promised well は「先行きがよさそうだ」。
explanation: such（そのようなもの）が主語 the sky とイコールの補語。SVC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: To the sellers in the market, to the barmen and barmaids, to the beggars who importuned him for a lob Mr Dedalus told the same tale, that he was an old Corkonian, that he had been trying for thirty years to get rid of his Cork accent up in Dublin and that Peter Pickackafax beside him was his eldest son but that he was only a Dublin jackeen.
target: To the sellers in the market, to the barmen and barmaids, to the beggars who importuned him for a lob Mr Dedalus told the same tale
translation: 市場の売り子にも、酒場の男女の給仕にも、金をせびる物乞いにも、ディーダラス氏は同じ話をした。自分は生粋のコーク人で、三十年もダブリンでコーク訛りを抜こうとしてきた、隣にいるピーター・ピカッカファックスは長男だが、こいつはただのダブリンっ子だ、と。
parts: To the sellers in the market, to the barmen and barmaids, to the beggars who importuned him for a lob
point: told を見て SVOO と思いやすいが、「人」は文頭の to ~ で示されていて、told の直後には「話」しかない。
explanation: told の目的語は the same tale。to ~ は修飾語。SVO。
note: tell A to B を tell B A（SVOO）の書きかえとみる説明もあるが、このアプリでは前置詞句を修飾語として SVO とする。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス
work: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

text: He cast only one glance at the dead face on the pillow, which Dolly had smoothed with decent care; but he remembered that last look at his unhappy hated wife so well, that at the end of sixteen years every line in the worn face was present to him when he told the full story of this night.
target: he remembered that last look at his unhappy hated wife so well, that at the end of sixteen years every line in the worn face was present to him when he told the full story of this night
translation: 彼は、ドリーがきちんと整えた枕の上の死に顔を一度ちらりと見ただけだった。だが、不幸で憎い妻を見たその最後の一瞥をあまりによく覚えていたので、十六年たってこの夜のことをすっかり話したときにも、やつれた顔のしわの一本一本が目の前に浮かんだ。
parts: that last look at his unhappy hated wife
that at the end of sixteen years every line in the worn face was present to him when he told the full story of this night
point: that last look の that は「あの」という指示語で、that 節ではない。後ろの that は so ~ that の that。
explanation: remembered の目的語は that last look at ~。SVO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Scrooge asked the question, because he didn't know whether a ghost so transparent might find himself in a condition to take a chair; and felt that in the event of its being impossible, it might involve the necessity of an embarrassing explanation.
target: Scrooge asked the question, because he didn't know whether a ghost so transparent might find himself in a condition to take a chair
translation: スクルージがその質問をしたのは、こんなに透きとおった幽霊が椅子に座れる状態にあるのかどうかわからなかったからだ。もし座れないとなると、気まずい説明をしなければならなくなるかもしれないと思ったのである。
parts: because he didn't know whether a ghost so transparent might find himself in a condition to take a chair
point: because 節の中の find himself in a condition ~ に引っぱられやすい。asked の後に人はなく、the question だけ。
explanation: asked の目的語は the question。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: クリスマス・キャロル

text: A secret sense of having failed and been ridiculous—a dread of what other fellows who went in for similar sorts of things, would say at his expense if they knew it—so oppressed him, that what was about the very best passage in his life was the one of all others he would not have owned to on any account, and the only one that made him ashamed of himself.
target: A secret sense of having failed and been ridiculous—a dread of what other fellows who went in for similar sorts of things, would say at his expense if they knew it—so oppressed him
translation: 失敗して笑い者になったというひそかな思い――同じようなことに手を出す仲間が知ったら自分をどう笑うだろうという恐れ――が彼をひどく苦しめたので、人生でおそらく最上の一節が、何があっても認めたくないただ一つのもの、自分を恥じ入らせるただ一つのものになってしまった。
parts: A secret sense of having failed and been ridiculous
a dread of what other fellows who went in for similar sorts of things, would say at his expense if they knew it
point: 主語の後にダッシュではさまれた同格の語句が入り、動詞 oppressed が遠い。後半の made him ashamed of himself は SVOC。
explanation: oppress（苦しめる）は他動詞で、目的語は him。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Everybody knows the story of another experimental philosopher who had a great theory about a horse being able to live without eating, and who demonstrated it so well, that he had got his own horse down to a straw a day, and would unquestionably have rendered him a very spirited and rampacious animal on nothing at all, if he had not died, four-and-twenty hours before he was to have had his first comfortable bait of air.
target: Everybody knows the story of another experimental philosopher who had a great theory about a horse being able to live without eating
translation: 誰もが知っている話だが、ある実験哲学者が、馬は食べなくても生きていけるという大理論を持っていて、それを見事に実証してみせ、自分の馬を一日わら一本にまで減らした。そして、初めて空気だけのごちそうにありつくはずだった二十四時間前に馬が死ななかったら、きっと何も食べずに元気いっぱいの暴れ馬にしてみせたことだろう。
parts: the story of another experimental philosopher who had a great theory about a horse being able to live without eating
point: 後半の would have rendered him a very spirited animal は SVOC。
explanation: knows の目的語は the story of ~。who 以下は philosopher を説明する関係詞節で、目的語の一部。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: They had a long talk that night, and Meg learned to love her husband better for his poverty, because it seemed to have made a man of him, given him the strength and courage to fight his own way, and taught him a tender patience with which to bear and comfort the natural longings and failures of those he loved.
target: Meg learned to love her husband better for his poverty
translation: その夜二人は長いあいだ話しあった。そしてメグは、夫が貧しいからこそ、いっそう夫を愛するようになった。貧しさが夫を一人前の男にし、自分の道を切り開く強さと勇気を与え、愛する者たちのもっともな望みや失敗を受けとめ慰めるやさしい忍耐を教えてくれたように思えたからだ。
parts: to love her husband better for his poverty
point: because 節の中に made a man of him、given him the strength（SVOO）、taught him a tender patience（SVOO）が並ぶ。
explanation: learn to do（~するようになる）の to love ~ は learned の目的語（名詞的用法）。SVO。
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorJa: ルイーザ・メイ・オルコット

text: When he offered her his arm, she took it with a look that filled him with delight, but when he asked if she missed him, she gave such a chilly, formal reply that despair fell upon him.
target: she gave such a chilly, formal reply that despair fell upon him
translation: 彼が腕を差し出すと、彼女はその腕を取り、彼をうっとりさせるような目つきをした。けれども、ぼくがいなくて寂しかったかいと彼が尋ねると、彼女はひどく冷たいよそよそしい返事をしたので、彼は絶望に襲われた。
point: gave を見て SVOO と思いやすいが、gave の後に「人」がなく、目的語は reply だけ。前半の offered her his arm は SVOO。
explanation: such ~ that …（とても~なので…）の構文。gave の目的語は such a chilly, formal reply。SVO。
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorJa: ルイーザ・メイ・オルコット

text: So when our walk brought us round to the village again, and I went home to breakfast, I prepared Ada for the account I was going to give her and told her exactly what reason we had to dread that Richard was losing himself and scattering his whole life to the winds.
target: I prepared Ada for the account I was going to give her
translation: それで、散歩をして村へ戻ってきて家で朝食をとると、私はこれから話すことに備えてエイダに心の準備をさせ、リチャードが自分を見失い、人生をまるごと風に散らしてしまうのではないかと私たちが恐れる理由を、ありのままに話した。
parts: for the account I was going to give her
point: the account（that）I was going to give her は関係代名詞の省略で、give her the account（SVOO）が元の形。
explanation: prepare A for B は「A に B の心構えをさせる」。目的語は Ada で、for ~ は修飾語。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: He then told her of that time of his life to which allusion has been made when, tossed about by doubts and difficulties in London, like a cork on the waves, he plunged into eight-and-forty hours’ dissipation with a stranger.
target: He then told her of that time of his life to which allusion has been made
translation: それから彼は、前にも触れた、人生のあの時期のことを彼女に話した。ロンドンで疑いと苦しみに、波間のコルクのように翻弄され、見知らぬ女と四十八時間の放蕩に身を投じたときのことを。
parts: of that time of his life to which allusion has been made
point: told her と続くので SVOO と思いやすいが、話の中身は of ~ という前置詞句で示されている。
explanation: tell 人 of ~ は「人に~のことを話す」。目的語は her だけで、of ~ は修飾語。SVO。
note: tell her of ~ を SVOO に準じて扱う説明もある。このアプリでは前置詞句を修飾語として SVO とする。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: She found, on reaching home, that she had, as she intended, escaped seeing Mr Elliot; that he had called and paid them a long morning visit; but hardly had she congratulated herself, and felt safe, when she heard that he was coming again in the evening.
target: She found, on reaching home, that she had, as she intended, escaped seeing Mr Elliot
translation: 家に帰ってみると、思惑どおりエリオット氏に会わずに済んだことがわかった。彼は訪ねてきて、午前中ずっと長居をしていったという。ところが、ほっとして胸をなでおろしたとたん、彼が夕方また来るという話が耳に入った。
parts: that she had, as she intended, escaped seeing Mr Elliot
point: 後の paid them a long morning visit は SVOO。found の後に that 節が来ているので SVOC ではない。
explanation: found の目的語は that 節。on reaching home は「帰るとすぐ」。SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: I passed an hour in this state of mind, when suddenly I reflected how fearful the combat which I momentarily expected would be to my wife, and I earnestly entreated her to retire, resolving not to join her until I had obtained some knowledge as to the situation of my enemy.
target: I passed an hour in this state of mind
translation: 私はこんな心持ちで一時間を過ごしたが、ふと、刻一刻と待ち受けている戦いが妻にとってどれほど恐ろしいものかに思い至り、部屋へ下がっていてくれと熱心に頼んだ。敵の居場所が少しでもわかるまでは、妻のところへは行くまいと決めて。
point: 後半の entreated her to retire は SVOC。
explanation: pass（時を過ごす）は他動詞で、目的語は an hour。SVO。
author: Mary Shelley
authorJa: メアリー・シェリー
workJa: フランケンシュタイン

text: Knightley remained with them, Emma’s fever continued; but when he was gone, she began to be a little tranquillised and subdued—and in the course of the sleepless night, which was the tax for such an evening, she found one or two such very serious points to consider, as made her feel, that even her happiness must have some alloy.
target: she found one or two such very serious points to consider, as made her feel, that even her happiness must have some alloy
translation: ナイトリー氏が一緒にいるあいだは、エマの興奮は続いた。だが彼が帰ると、少し落ち着き静まりはじめた。そして、こんな晩の代償である眠れない夜のあいだに、自分の幸福にさえいくらかの混じり物があるにちがいないと感じさせるような、ひどく重大な点を一つ二つ考えることになった。
parts: one or two such very serious points
as made her feel, that even her happiness must have some alloy
point: such ~ as … の as は関係代名詞のはたらきで、as made her feel ~ は SVOC。found の後が SVOC に見えるが、points は名詞で to consider はそれを説明している。
explanation: found の目的語は points。to consider は points を説明する形容詞的用法。SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: As she walked beside him, shrinking in every nerve from the way in which his look and tone made free of her, yet telling herself that this momentary endurance of his mood was the price she must pay for her ultimate power over him, she tried to calculate the exact point at which concession must turn to resistance, and the price HE would have to pay be made equally clear to him.
target: she tried to calculate the exact point at which concession must turn to resistance
translation: 彼と並んで歩きながら、彼の目つきや口調がなれなれしく踏みこんでくるのに全身の神経が縮みあがる思いだったが、それでも、彼の気まぐれにいま耐えるのは、いずれ彼を支配するための代価なのだと自分に言い聞かせて、彼女は、譲歩が抵抗に変わらねばならない正確な一点と、彼が払うことになる代価もまた同じくはっきり示される一点とを、見きわめようとした。
parts: to calculate the exact point at which concession must turn to resistance
point: 前置きの分詞構文の中に made free of her や telling herself that ~（SVOO）がある。
explanation: try to do の to calculate ~ は tried の目的語（名詞的用法）。SVO。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: When we came home we found that a young man had called three times in the course of that one day to see me and that having been told on the occasion of his third call that I was not expected to return before ten o’clock at night, he had left word that he would call about then.
target: When we came home we found that a young man had called three times in the course of that one day to see me
translation: 家に帰ると、ある若い男がその一日のうちに三度も私に会いに来たことがわかった。三度目に来たとき、私は夜十時より前には戻らないと聞かされ、そのころまた来ると言い置いていったという。
parts: that a young man had called three times in the course of that one day to see me
point: 後半の having been told ~ that I was not expected ~ は tell O that の受動態。
explanation: found の目的語は that 節。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: When they arrived at the gateway where he had paused in the dark not many hours before, to picture to himself on which of the rough stones of the street her feet had trodden, he lifted her again, and carried her up the staircase to their rooms.
target: he lifted her again, and carried her up the staircase to their rooms
translation: 数時間前、暗がりの中で足を止め、通りのどの粗い石を彼女の足が踏んだのだろうと思い描いたあの門口に着くと、彼はまた彼女を抱き上げ、階段を上って部屋まで運んだ。
point: When 節の中の to picture to himself ~ は目的の不定詞で、その中に on which of the rough stones ~ という間接疑問がある。
explanation: lift、carry はどちらも目的語 her をとる。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: It struck those who knew him well that he might do greater things than carry on a cotton-factory; there was nothing cottony about Caspar Goodwood, and his friends took for granted that he would somehow and somewhere write himself in bigger letters.
target: It struck those who knew him well that he might do greater things than carry on a cotton-factory
translation: 彼をよく知る人たちには、彼は綿工場を経営するよりもっと大きなことができるのではないかと思えた。カスパー・グッドウッドには綿くさいところなどまるでなく、友人たちは、彼がいつかどこかで、もっと大きな文字で自分の名を書きこむだろうと当然のように思っていた。
parts: that he might do greater things than carry on a cotton-factory
point: it は仮主語で、真主語は that 節。その間に目的語 those who knew him well がはさまっている。
explanation: It strikes 人 that ~ は「人に~と思われる」。strike は他動詞で、目的語は those who knew him well。SVO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: The officer looked at Daisy while she was speaking, in a way that every young girl wants to be looked at sometime, and because it seemed romantic to me I have remembered the incident ever since.
target: because it seemed romantic to me I have remembered the incident ever since
translation: その将校は、彼女が話しているあいだずっとデイジーを見つめていた。若い娘なら誰でもいつかはそんなふうに見つめられたいと思うような見つめ方で。私にはそれがロマンチックに思えたので、そのとき以来この出来事を覚えている。
parts: because it seemed romantic to me
point: because 節の it seemed romantic は SVC だが、従属節の中。
explanation: have remembered の目的語は the incident。SVO。
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
authorJa: F・スコット・フィッツジェラルド
workJa: グレート・ギャツビー

text: It had, indeed, a very cheery aspect, the walls being overspread with a kind of stucco, in which fragments of broken glass were plentifully intermixed; so that, when the sunshine fell aslant-wise over the front of the edifice, it glittered and sparkled as if diamonds had been flung against it by the double handful.
target: It had, indeed, a very cheery aspect
translation: それは実にうきうきするような外観をしていた。壁一面に一種のスタッコが塗られ、その中に割れたガラスのかけらがたっぷり練りこまれていたので、日の光が建物の正面に斜めにさすと、まるでダイヤモンドを両手でつかんで投げつけたかのように、きらきらと輝いたのだ。
point: 後半の the walls being overspread ~ は独立分詞構文、had been flung は受動態。
explanation: had の目的語は a very cheery aspect。SVO。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン

text: I knew that I had come face to face with some one whose mere personality was so fascinating that, if I allowed it to do so, it would absorb my whole nature, my whole soul, my very art itself.
target: I knew that I had come face to face with some one whose mere personality was so fascinating that, if I allowed it to do so, it would absorb my whole nature, my whole soul, my very art itself
translation: 私にはわかっていた。その人柄だけであまりに魅惑的で、もしそうさせてしまえば、私の本性のすべて、魂のすべて、芸術そのものまでも吸いつくしてしまうような人物と、自分は向きあってしまったのだと。
parts: that I had come face to face with some one whose mere personality was so fascinating that, if I allowed it to do so, it would absorb my whole nature, my whole soul, my very art itself
point: that 節の中に whose 節、so ~ that 構文、if I allowed it to do so（SVOC）と入れ子が続く。
explanation: knew の目的語は that 以下の名詞節全体。SVO。
author: Oscar Wilde
authorJa: オスカー・ワイルド
workJa: ドリアン・グレイの肖像

text: The way by which we approached it took us past the Three Jolly Bargemen, which we were surprised to find—it being eleven o’clock—in a state of commotion, with the door wide open, and unwonted lights that had been hastily caught up and put down scattered about.
target: The way by which we approached it took us past the Three Jolly Bargemen
translation: そこへ近づく道は「三人の陽気な船頭」亭の前を通っていた。驚いたことに――十一時だというのに――その店は大騒ぎで、扉は開け放たれ、慌ただしく持ち出しては置かれたいつにない明かりがあちこちに散らばっていた。
point: 後半の which we were surprised to find ~ in a state of commotion は find O C の O が関係代名詞になった形。
explanation: took の目的語は us で、past ~ は「~を通り過ぎて」という修飾語。SVO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: During all those years he had never heard from any of his masters a flippant word: it was they who had taught him christian doctrine and urged him to live a good life and, when he had fallen into grievous sin, it was they who had led him back to grace.
target: it was they who had taught him christian doctrine
translation: その間ずっと、彼は先生たちの誰からも軽はずみな言葉を一つも聞いたことがなかった。キリスト教の教えを彼に教え、善い生活を送るよう励ましてくれたのは彼らであり、彼が重い罪に落ちたとき、恵みへと連れ戻してくれたのも彼らだった。
point: It was ~ who … の強調構文。it was と who を取りのぞくと元の文が現れる。
explanation: 元の文は They had taught him christian doctrine.「彼に（O₁）キリスト教の教えを（O₂）」で SVOO。
note: 強調構文は元の文に戻して判定する。it was と who は強調のための枠なので M とした。
author: James Joyce
authorJa: ジェイムズ・ジョイス
work: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

text: At first, he was pleased with the discovery: hoping that it might be the forerunner of his release; but such thoughts were quickly dispelled, on his sitting down to breakfast along with the Jew, who told him, in a tone and manner which increased his alarm, that he was to be taken to the residence of Bill Sikes that night.
target: who told him, in a tone and manner which increased his alarm, that he was to be taken to the residence of Bill Sikes that night
translation: 初めのうち、彼はその発見を喜んだ。釈放の前触れかもしれないと思ったのだ。だが、ユダヤ人と一緒に朝食の席に着くと、そんな考えはたちまち吹き飛んだ。ユダヤ人は、彼の不安をいっそうつのらせる口調と態度で、今夜ビル・サイクスの家へ連れていかれるのだと告げたのである。
parts: in a tone and manner which increased his alarm
that he was to be taken to the residence of Bill Sikes that night
point: 関係詞節の中を判定する問題。who が主語。told him と that 節のあいだに長い修飾語がはさまっている。
explanation: told him（彼に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: オリヴァー・ツイスト

text: This had been Silas’s testimony, though he clutched strongly at the idea of the pedlar’s being the culprit, if only because it gave him a definite image of a whereabout for his gold after it had been taken away from its hiding-place: he could see it now in the pedlar’s box.
target: it gave him a definite image of a whereabout for his gold after it had been taken away from its hiding-place
translation: これがサイラスの証言だった。もっとも彼は行商人が犯人だという考えに強くしがみついていた。それは、金貨が隠し場所から持ち去られたあとの行方について、はっきりした像を与えてくれたからにほかならなかった。今では行商人の箱の中にあるのが目に見えるようだった。
parts: a definite image of a whereabout for his gold
after it had been taken away from its hiding-place
point: after 節の had been taken away は受動態（SV）。
explanation: gave him（彼に）a definite image（はっきりした像を）で SVOO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Knightley had once told her it was because she saw in her the really accomplished young woman, which she wanted to be thought herself; and though the accusation had been eagerly refuted at the time, there were moments of self-examination in which her conscience could not quite acquit her.
target: Knightley had once told her it was because she saw in her the really accomplished young woman, which she wanted to be thought herself
translation: ナイトリー氏はかつて彼女に、それは、自分もそう思われたいと願っている本当に教養ある若い女性をその人の中に見ているからだ、と言ったことがあった。その非難はそのときむきになって打ち消したものの、自省の折には、良心が彼女をすっかり無罪にはできない瞬間もあった。
parts: it was because she saw in her the really accomplished young woman, which she wanted to be thought herself
point: told her の後の that が省略されている。which she wanted to be thought herself は want O to be thought の関係詞化。
explanation: told her（彼女に）（that）~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: When I had done this, I began to work my way into the rock, and bringing all the earth and stones that I dug down out through my tent, I laid them up within my fence, in the nature of a terrace, so that it raised the ground within about a foot and a half; and thus I made me a cave, just behind my tent, which served me like a cellar to my house.
target: thus I made me a cave, just behind my tent, which served me like a cellar to my house
translation: これが済むと、私は岩を掘り進めはじめた。掘り出した土や石をすべてテントの中を通して運び出し、囲いの内側に段のように積み上げたので、内側の地面が一フィート半ほど高くなった。こうして私はテントのすぐ裏に洞穴をこしらえ、それが家の地下室のように役立った。
parts: which served me like a cellar to my house
point: made me a cave は「私を洞穴にした」（SVOC）ではなく「自分のために洞穴を作った」。me と a cave はイコールではない。
explanation: made me（自分に）a cave（洞穴を）で SVOO。me は古い英語で myself の代わり。
author: Daniel Defoe
authorJa: ダニエル・デフォー
workJa: ロビンソン・クルーソー

text: As to what sensations he experienced when he got ashore and heard the unforeseen conclusion of the tale in which he had taken such a pitiful part, he told me nothing of them, and it is difficult to imagine.
target: he told me nothing of them
translation: 上陸して、自分があれほど情けない役を演じた物語の思いがけない結末を聞いたとき、彼がどんな気持ちを味わったかについては、彼は何ひとつ話してくれなかったし、想像するのも難しい。
point: 文頭の As to what sensations ~ は「~については」という長い修飾語で、them はその sensations を指す。
explanation: told me（私に）nothing（何も~ない）で SVOO。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: Frequently when they came to a gate or stile they found painted thereon in red or blue letters some text of Scripture, and she asked him if he knew who had been at the pains to blazon these announcements.
target: she asked him if he knew who had been at the pains to blazon these announcements
translation: 門や踏み越し段に来ると、そこに赤や青の文字で聖書の一節が書かれていることがよくあった。彼女は彼に、わざわざこんな文句を書きつけて回っているのが誰か知っているかと尋ねた。
parts: if he knew who had been at the pains to blazon these announcements
point: 前半の they found painted thereon ~ some text は find O C の O と C が入れかわった形（SVOC）。
explanation: asked him（彼に）if ~（~かどうかを）で SVOO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: ダーバヴィル家のテス

text: My poor little visitor made me a present of the account, and when as the evening began to close in she rose to take her leave, lest she should miss the coach by which she was to return, she was still full of the shipwreck, which I had not yet sufficiently composed myself to understand in all its details.
target: My poor little visitor made me a present of the account
translation: かわいそうな小さな客人は、その話を私に聞かせてくれた。そして夕方暗くなりはじめ、帰りの馬車に乗り遅れないよう暇を告げて立ち上がったときにも、彼女はまだ難破の話で頭がいっぱいだった。私のほうは、まだ細かいところまで理解できるほど落ち着いてはいなかったのだが。
point: made me a present を「私を贈り物にした」（SVOC）と読まないこと。me と a present はイコールではない。
explanation: make 人 a present of ~ は「人に~を贈る」。made me（私に）a present（贈り物を）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: Lestrade showed us the exact spot at which the body had been found, and, indeed, so moist was the ground, that I could plainly see the traces which had been left by the fall of the stricken man.
target: Lestrade showed us the exact spot at which the body had been found
translation: レストレードは死体が見つかった正確な場所を私たちに示した。実際、地面はとても湿っていたので、撃たれた男が倒れたときの跡がはっきり見てとれた。
parts: the exact spot at which the body had been found
point: 後半の so moist was the ground は補語が前に出た倒置（SVC）。
explanation: showed us（私たちに）the exact spot（場所を）で SVOO。
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorJa: アーサー・コナン・ドイル
workJa: シャーロック・ホームズの冒険

text: The Bugis owner of the prau, whom I saw on Stein’s verandah, and who was amongst them, told me that the boat, shaving the low point close, seemed for a moment to grow big and hang over it like a mountain.
target: The Bugis owner of the prau, whom I saw on Stein’s verandah, and who was amongst them, told me that the boat, shaving the low point close, seemed for a moment to grow big and hang over it like a mountain
translation: スタインのベランダで会った、その場に居合わせたブギス人の小舟の持ち主が私に話してくれたところでは、低い岬をすれすれにかすめていった舟は、一瞬大きくふくらみ、山のように岬の上にのしかかったように見えたという。
parts: The Bugis owner of the prau
whom I saw on Stein’s verandah, and who was amongst them
that the boat, shaving the low point close, seemed for a moment to grow big and hang over it like a mountain
point: 主語の後に関係詞節が二つ続き、動詞 told が遠い。that 節の中の seemed to grow big は SVC。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: I told them that you were of all human creatures the one over whom habit had most power and novelty least; and that the very circumstance of the novelty of Crawford’s addresses was against him.
target: I told them that you were of all human creatures the one over whom habit had most power and novelty least
translation: 私はあの人たちに言ったのよ。あなたはあらゆる人間の中で、習慣にいちばん強く、目新しさにいちばん弱く左右される人なのだと。そしてクロフォードの求愛が目新しいということ自体が、彼には不利なのだと。
parts: that you were of all human creatures the one over whom habit had most power and novelty least
point: that 節の中の over whom habit had most power and novelty least は、後半で had が省略されている。
explanation: told them（あの人たちに）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: A placard near by announced that they had been reduced in price from two dollars and fifty cents to one dollar and ninety-eight cents; and a young girl who stood behind the counter asked her if she wished to examine their line of silk hosiery.
target: a young girl who stood behind the counter asked her if she wished to examine their line of silk hosiery
translation: 近くの札には、二ドル五十セントから一ドル九十八セントに値下げしたと書かれていた。そしてカウンターの後ろに立っていた若い娘が、絹の靴下の品ぞろえをご覧になりますかと彼女に尋ねた。
parts: if she wished to examine their line of silk hosiery
point: 前半の had been reduced は受動態。主語 a young girl の後に関係詞節がはさまる。
explanation: asked her（彼女に）if ~（~かどうかを）で SVOO。
author: Kate Chopin
authorJa: ケイト・ショパン

text: His reason told him how the affair might have been magnified into ruin by a slight change of scenery—if it had been a gambling-house that he had turned into, where chance could be clutched with both hands instead of being picked up with thumb and fore-finger.
target: His reason told him how the affair might have been magnified into ruin by a slight change of scenery
translation: 理性は彼に告げていた。場面がほんの少し違っていたら、この件はどれほど破滅にまでふくれあがっていたかもしれないかを。もし彼がふらりと入ったのが賭博場で、運を親指と人さし指でつまみ上げるのではなく、両手でわしづかみにできる場所だったなら。
parts: how the affair might have been magnified into ruin by a slight change of scenery
point: 主語が人ではなく His reason（彼の理性）という無生物主語。if 節の中の it had been a gambling-house は SVC。
explanation: told him（彼に）how ~（どのように~かを）で SVOO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Something especially reckless in his demeanour, not only gave him a disreputable look, but so diminished the strong resemblance he undoubtedly bore to the prisoner (which his momentary earnestness, when they were compared together, had strengthened), that many of the lookers-on, taking note of him now, said to one another they would hardly have thought the two were so alike.
target: Something especially reckless in his demeanour, not only gave him a disreputable look
translation: その態度にどこかひどく投げやりなところがあって、彼をいかがわしく見せていただけでなく、被告と彼とが確かに似ているという印象も――比べられたとき彼が一瞬見せた真剣さがそれを強めていたのだが――ずいぶん薄れさせたので、今になって彼に目をとめた傍聴人の多くは、二人がそんなに似ているとはとても思わなかっただろうと言いあった。
parts: Something especially reckless in his demeanour
point: not only ~ but so diminished … that ~ の構文。後半の so diminished the strong resemblance は SVO。
explanation: gave him（彼に）a disreputable look（いかがわしい様子を）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: One morning, being left alone with him a few minutes in the parlour, I ventured to approach the window-recess—which his table, chair, and desk consecrated as a kind of study—and I was going to speak, though not very well knowing in what words to frame my inquiry—for it is at all times difficult to break the ice of reserve glassing over such natures as his—when he saved me the trouble by being the first to commence a dialogue.
target: he saved me the trouble by being the first to commence a dialogue
translation: ある朝、居間で数分間彼と二人きりになったとき、私は思いきって窓のくぼみに近づいた。そこは彼のテーブルと椅子と机が置かれて書斎のようになっていた。何と言って尋ねればいいかよくわからないまま話しかけようとしたのだが――彼のような人の心を覆う遠慮の氷を割るのはいつだって難しいのだ――そのとき彼のほうから先に話を始めて、その手間を省いてくれた。
parts: by being the first to commence a dialogue
point: save は「救う」ではなく「（人の）手間を省く」の意味で二つの目的語をとる。
explanation: saved me（私に）the trouble（手間を）省いてくれた、で SVOO。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: The worthy Obed tells us, that in the early times of the whale fishery, ere ships were regularly launched in pursuit of the game, the people of that island erected lofty spars along the sea-coast, to which the look-outs ascended by means of nailed cleats, something as fowls go upstairs in a hen-house.
target: The worthy Obed tells us, that in the early times of the whale fishery, ere ships were regularly launched in pursuit of the game, the people of that island erected lofty spars along the sea-coast
translation: 立派なオーベッドが私たちに語るところでは、捕鯨の初期、まだ獲物を追って船が定期的に出されるようになる前、あの島の人々は海岸沿いに高い円材を立て、見張りは打ちつけた横木をつたって、ちょうど鶏が鶏小屋のはしごを上るような具合に、そこへ登ったという。
parts: that in the early times of the whale fishery, ere ships were regularly launched in pursuit of the game, the people of that island erected lofty spars along the sea-coast
point: that 節の中に ere ~ were launched（受動態）や erected lofty spars（SVO）がある。
explanation: tells us（私たちに）that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Herman Melville
authorJa: ハーマン・メルヴィル

text: Creakle, who was very severe with me; but whenever I had been treated worse than usual, he always told me that I wanted a little of his pluck, and that he wouldn’t have stood it himself; which I felt he intended for encouragement, and considered to be very kind of him.
target: he always told me that I wanted a little of his pluck, and that he wouldn’t have stood it himself
translation: クリークル氏は私にとても厳しかった。だが、私がいつもよりひどい目にあわされると、彼はいつも私に、きみにはぼくの度胸が少し足りない、ぼくだったら我慢しなかったね、と言った。それは励ましのつもりなのだと私は感じ、とても親切なことだと思った。
parts: that I wanted a little of his pluck, and that he wouldn’t have stood it himself
point: 後の considered to be very kind of him は consider O to be C の O が which になった形（SVOC）。
explanation: told me（私に）that ~ and that ~（~ということを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: While he was so engaged, he asked me what I would take with it; and on my replying ‘Half a pint of sherry,’ thought it a favourable opportunity, I am afraid, to extract that measure of wine from the stale leavings at the bottoms of several small decanters.
target: he asked me what I would take with it
translation: そうしながら、彼はそれと一緒に何を飲むかと私に尋ねた。そして私が「シェリーを半パイント」と答えると、どうやらこれ幸いと、小さなデカンターいくつかの底に残った気の抜けた残り物から、その量のワインをかき集めようと考えたらしい。
parts: what I would take with it
point: 後の thought it a favourable opportunity to ~ は仮目的語の SVOC。
explanation: asked me（私に）what ~（何を~かを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: A rebuke might possibly have been irritating, though it is much more probable that Isabel would have taken it in good part; but, strange to say, the words that Madame Merle actually used caused her the first feeling of displeasure she had known this ally to excite.
target: the words that Madame Merle actually used caused her the first feeling of displeasure she had known this ally to excite
translation: とがめられたら腹が立ったかもしれないが、イザベルならむしろ素直に受けとめた見込みのほうがずっと大きかった。ところが奇妙なことに、マール夫人が実際に口にした言葉は、この味方がかき立てるのを彼女が初めて知った不快感を彼女に抱かせたのだった。
parts: the first feeling of displeasure she had known this ally to excite
point: cause を見て cause O to do（SVOC）と思いやすいが、ここでは her の後に名詞 feeling が続く。she had known this ally to excite は know O to do の関係詞化。
explanation: cause 人 物 は「人に物（感情など）を引き起こす」。caused her（彼女に）the first feeling（感情を）で SVOO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: I asked him what her disposition was: whether it was at all mischievous, and if her sympathies were generally on the right side of things: but, not succeeding in attracting his attention to these questions after two or three attempts, I forbore or forgot to repeat them.
target: I asked him what her disposition was
translation: 私は彼に、彼女の気性はどんなふうかと尋ねた。いたずら好きなところがあるのかどうか、彼女の共感はたいてい物事の正しい側に向いているのかどうか、と。だが二、三度試みても彼の注意をこうした質問に向けられなかったので、くり返して尋ねるのはやめにした、というより忘れてしまった。
point: 後半の not succeeding in attracting his attention ~ は分詞構文。
explanation: asked him（彼に）what ~（どんなものかを）で SVOO。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: It kind of made him drunk, as you may say, and he didn’t know nothing at all the rest of the day, and preached a prayer-meeting sermon that night that gave him a rattling ruputation, because the oldest man in the world couldn’t a understood it.
target: It kind of made him drunk, as you may say
translation: それで彼はいわば酔っぱらったみたいになって、その日はあとずっと何が何だかわからなくなり、その晩、祈祷会の説教をしたら、これがすごい評判になったんだ。世界一の年寄りだってわかりっこない説教だったからさ。
point: 後の gave him a rattling ruputation は SVOO（ruputation は reputation の方言つづり）。kind of は「なんだか」という口語の副詞。
explanation: made him drunk で「彼を酔ったようにした」。him＝drunk の関係なので SVOC。
author: Mark Twain
authorJa: マーク・トウェイン
workJa: ハックルベリー・フィンの冒険

text: It seemed to him that the weaver was very selfish (a judgment readily passed by those who have never tested their own power of sacrifice) to oppose what was undoubtedly for Eppie’s welfare; and he felt himself called upon, for her sake, to assert his authority.
target: he felt himself called upon, for her sake, to assert his authority
translation: 彼には、あの織工がエピーのためになるに決まっていることに反対するのは、ひどく身勝手に思えた（自分の犠牲の力を試したことのない者ほど、こういう判断をすぐ下すものだ）。そして、彼女のために、自分の権威をはっきり示さねばならないと感じた。
point: 前半の It seemed to him that ~ は SV（seem は自動詞）。
explanation: felt himself called upon で「自分が求められていると感じた」。himself＝called upon の関係なので SVOC。to assert ~ は called upon の内容。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: It was because he grew so scared and trembling, and because he felt himself to be a poor, weak, ignorant, helpless man (those used to be his words), that he wanted me so much to know a great deal, and be different from him.
target: It was because he grew so scared and trembling, and because he felt himself to be a poor, weak, ignorant, helpless man (those used to be his words), that he wanted me so much to know a great deal, and be different from him
translation: 父が私にいろいろなことを知ってほしい、自分とは違う人間になってほしいとあれほど願ったのは、父がすっかりおびえて震えるようになったからであり、自分を貧しく弱く無知で頼りない男だと感じていたからでした（それが父の口ぐせでした）。
parts: because he grew so scared and trembling, and because he felt himself to be a poor, weak, ignorant, helpless man (those used to be his words)
to know a great deal, and be different from him
point: It was because ~ that … は because 節を強調した強調構文。because 節の中の felt himself to be ~ も SVOC だが、強調されている部分にすぎない。
explanation: 元の文は He wanted me so much to know a great deal ~ because ~。want O to do で SVOC。
note: 強調構文は元の文に戻して判定する。It was と that は強調のための枠なので M とした。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: She felt herself a most fortunate woman; and she had lived long enough to know how fortunate she might well be thought, where the only regret was for a partial separation from friends whose friendship for her had never cooled, and who could ill bear to part with her.
target: She felt herself a most fortunate woman
translation: 彼女は自分をこのうえなく幸運な女だと感じていた。そして、友情が一度も冷めたことがなく、別れるのをつらがってくれる友人たちと少し離れて暮らすことだけが心残りだというのなら、自分がどれほど幸運だと思われてもおかしくないかがわかるくらいには、長く生きてきたのだった。
point: 後の how fortunate she might well be thought は think O C の受動態の形。
explanation: felt herself a most fortunate woman で「自分をとても幸運な女だと感じた」。herself＝woman の関係なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: The idea of wanting gratitude and consideration for Miss Woodhouse, whom she really loved extremely, made her wretched for a while, and when the violence of grief was comforted away, still remained powerful enough to prompt to what was right and support her in it very tolerably.
target: The idea of wanting gratitude and consideration for Miss Woodhouse, whom she really loved extremely, made her wretched for a while
translation: 心から大好きなウッドハウス嬢への感謝と思いやりに欠けていると思うと、彼女はしばらくみじめな気持ちになった。そして悲しみの激しさがなぐさめられて消えたあとも、その思いは、正しいことをするよう促し、それをかなりうまくやり通す支えになるほどの力を持ちつづけた。
parts: The idea of wanting gratitude and consideration for Miss Woodhouse
point: wanting は「欠いている」の意味。主語が長く、関係詞節もはさまって動詞 made が遠い。後半の support her in it は SVO。
explanation: made her wretched で「彼女をみじめにした」。her＝wretched の関係なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: This little wandering journey, without settled place of abode, had been so unpleasant to me, that my own house, as I called it to myself, was a perfect settlement to me compared to that; and it rendered everything about me so comfortable, that I resolved I would never go a great way from it again while it should be my lot to stay on the island.
target: it rendered everything about me so comfortable, that I resolved I would never go a great way from it again while it should be my lot to stay on the island
translation: この落ち着き先のない小さな放浪の旅はひどく不快だったので、自分で「わが家」と呼んでいた住まいが、それに比べれば完璧な落ち着き場所に思えた。そしてそれが身のまわりのすべてをとても快適に感じさせたので、この島にとどまる運命にあるあいだは、二度とそこから遠くへは行くまいと決心した。
parts: that I resolved I would never go a great way from it again while it should be my lot to stay on the island
point: 前半の had been so unpleasant to me（SVC）、as I called it to myself（call O C）と続く。
explanation: render O C は「O を C にする」。everything＝comfortable の関係なので SVOC。
author: Daniel Defoe
authorJa: ダニエル・デフォー
workJa: ロビンソン・クルーソー

text: It was partly to this vague fear that Marner was indebted for protecting him from the persecution that his singularities might have drawn upon him, but still more to the fact that, the old linen-weaver in the neighbouring parish of Tarley being dead, his handicraft made him a highly welcome settler to the richer housewives of the district, and even to the more provident cottagers, who had their little stock of yarn at the year’s end.
target: his handicraft made him a highly welcome settler to the richer housewives of the district
translation: マーナーが、その風変わりなところのせいで受けたかもしれない迫害を免れたのは、ひとつにはこの漠然とした恐れのおかげだった。だがそれ以上に、隣の教区のタープリーにいた年寄りの亜麻布織りが死んでしまっていたので、彼の手仕事のおかげで、地区の裕福な主婦たちや、年末に少しばかり糸を蓄えておくような用意のよい小作人たちにとって、彼がたいへん歓迎される住人になっていたからだった。
parts: to the richer housewives of the district
point: made him a ~ を SVOO（彼に~を作った）と読まないこと。ここでは him＝settler。文頭の It was partly to ~ that … は強調構文。
explanation: made him a highly welcome settler で「彼をたいへん歓迎される住人にした」。him＝settler の関係なので SVOC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: As I turned my eyes to the elder brother, I saw him looking down at this handsome boy whose life was ebbing out, as if he were a wounded bird, or hare, or rabbit; not at all as if he were a fellow-creature.
target: I saw him looking down at this handsome boy whose life was ebbing out
translation: 兄のほうに目を向けると、彼は、命が尽きかけているこの美しい少年を、まるで傷ついた鳥か野ウサギかウサギでも見るように見下ろしていた。同じ人間を見るようにでは、まったくなかった。
parts: looking down at this handsome boy whose life was ebbing out
point: 後の as if he were a wounded bird は仮定法。
explanation: 知覚動詞 see O ~ing で「O が~しているのを見る」。him が looking の主体なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ

text: I showed them with what indefatigable pains I had hewed a large tree into single planks, and I caused them to do the like, till they made about a dozen large planks, of good oak, near two feet broad, thirty-five feet long, and from two inches to four inches thick: what prodigious labour it took up any one may imagine.
target: I caused them to do the like
translation: 私は、どれほど根気よく苦労して大きな木を一枚一枚の板に切り分けたかを彼らに見せ、同じようにさせた。こうして彼らは、上等なオーク材の大きな板を十二枚ほど作った。幅二フィート近く、長さ三十五フィート、厚さ二インチから四インチの板である。それがどれほどの重労働だったかは誰でも想像がつくだろう。
point: 前の I showed them with what ~ は SVOO（彼らに、どんなに~かを見せた）。
explanation: cause O to do で「O に~させる」。them が do の主体なので SVOC。
author: Daniel Defoe
authorJa: ダニエル・デフォー
workJa: ロビンソン・クルーソー

text: A few minutes, though as few as possible, were inevitably consumed; and when her own mistress again, when able to turn and look as she had done before, she found herself accosted by Captain Wentworth, in a reserved yet hurried sort of farewell.
target: she found herself accosted by Captain Wentworth, in a reserved yet hurried sort of farewell
translation: できるだけ短くとはいえ、どうしても数分はかかった。そして、ふたたび自分を取り戻し、前のように振り向いて見られるようになったとき、彼女は、ウェントワース大佐が控えめな、それでいて急いだ別れの言葉をかけてくるのに気づいた。
parts: in a reserved yet hurried sort of farewell
point: 前の when her own mistress again は when she was her own mistress again の省略。were consumed は受動態。
explanation: found herself accosted で「自分が話しかけられているのに気づいた」。herself＝accosted の関係なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: I was ready to burst with holding my breath, when, as I felt myself rising up, so, to my immediate relief, I found my head and hands shoot out above the surface of the water; and though it was not two seconds of time that I could keep myself so, yet it relieved me greatly, gave me breath, and new courage.
target: I found my head and hands shoot out above the surface of the water
translation: 息を止めているせいで今にも破裂しそうだったが、体が浮き上がるのを感じたかと思うと、ほっとしたことに、頭と両手が水面の上に飛び出した。そのままでいられたのは二秒もなかったが、それでも大いに楽になり、息がつけて、新たな勇気がわいた。
parts: shoot out above the surface of the water
point: 後半の gave me breath, and new courage は SVOO。as I felt myself rising up も SVOC。
explanation: find O do で「O が~するのに気づく」。my head and hands が shoot out の主体なので SVOC。
author: Daniel Defoe
authorJa: ダニエル・デフォー
workJa: ロビンソン・クルーソー

text: She saw her less shy, and less serious, which was all to the good, and the violent leaps and the interminable mazes which had led to that result were usually not even guessed at by her.
target: She saw her less shy, and less serious
translation: 彼女は、その子が前ほど内気でなく、前ほど深刻でもなくなったのを見てとった。それはまったくよいことだった。そして、その結果にたどり着くまでの激しい跳躍や果てしない迷路は、たいてい彼女には思いもよらなかった。
point: 後半の were usually not even guessed at by her は受動態。
explanation: saw her less shy で「彼女が前ほど内気でないのを見た」。her＝less shy の関係なので SVOC。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: He desired me to give him some account of my travels; and, to let me see that I should be treated without ceremony, he dismissed all his attendants with a turn of his finger; at which, to my great astonishment, they vanished in an instant, like visions in a dream when we awake on a sudden.
target: He desired me to give him some account of my travels
translation: 彼は私に旅の話を少し聞かせてほしいと言った。そして、堅苦しい扱いはしないことを私にわからせるため、指をひと振りして家来を全員下がらせた。すると、私がひどく驚いたことに、彼らは、夢から急に覚めたときの幻のように、一瞬にして消えてしまった。
parts: to give him some account of my travels
point: C の中の give him some account は SVOO だが、判定するのは desired の文型。
explanation: desire O to do で「O に~してほしいと望む」。me が give の主体なので SVOC。
author: Jonathan Swift
authorJa: ジョナサン・スウィフト

text: Wickham was the happy man towards whom almost every female eye was turned, and Elizabeth was the happy woman by whom he finally seated himself; and the agreeable manner in which he immediately fell into conversation, though it was only on its being a wet night, and on the probability of a rainy season, made her feel that the commonest, dullest, most threadbare topic might be rendered interesting by the skill of the speaker.
target: the agreeable manner in which he immediately fell into conversation, though it was only on its being a wet night, and on the probability of a rainy season, made her feel that the commonest, dullest, most threadbare topic might be rendered interesting by the skill of the speaker
translation: ウィッカムは女性たちのほとんどの視線が向けられる幸せな男で、エリザベスは彼が最後にそばに腰を下ろした幸せな女だった。彼がすぐに会話を始めたその感じのよさは、話題が雨の夜のことや、雨の季節になりそうだということにすぎなかったにもかかわらず、どんなにありふれた、退屈な、陳腐な話題でも、話し手の腕しだいでおもしろくなりうるのだと彼女に感じさせた。
parts: in which he immediately fell into conversation
though it was only on its being a wet night, and on the probability of a rainy season
feel that the commonest, dullest, most threadbare topic might be rendered interesting by the skill of the speaker
point: 主語と動詞 made のあいだに関係詞節と though 節がはさまる。C の that 節の中の might be rendered interesting は render O C の受動態。
explanation: 使役の make O do で「O に~させる」。her が feel の主体なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Archer had made her understand this, as he was bound to do; he had also made her understand that simple-hearted kindly New York, on whose larger charity she had apparently counted, was precisely the place where she could least hope for indulgence.
target: Archer had made her understand this, as he was bound to do
translation: アーチャーは、そうする義務があったので、彼女にこのことをわからせていた。また、彼女があてにしていたらしい、もっと大きな慈悲を持つはずの素朴で親切なニューヨークこそ、彼女が寛大な扱いを最も期待できない場所なのだということも、わからせていた。
parts: as he was bound to do
point: 後半にも made her understand that ~ がくり返され、その that 節の中に on whose larger charity ~ という関係詞がある。
explanation: 使役の make O do で「O に~させる」。her が understand の主体なので SVOC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン
workJa: エイジ・オブ・イノセンス

text: She had not seen him before since his engagement became public, and therefore not since his knowing her to be acquainted with it; which, with the consciousness of what she had been thinking of, and what she had to tell him, made her feel particularly uncomfortable for some minutes.
target: which, with the consciousness of what she had been thinking of, and what she had to tell him, made her feel particularly uncomfortable for some minutes
translation: 婚約が公になってから彼に会うのは初めてで、したがって、彼女がそのことを知っていると彼が知ってからも初めてだった。そのことが、自分が何を考えていたか、彼に何を伝えねばならないかという意識とあいまって、彼女をしばらくひどく落ち着かない気持ちにさせた。
parts: with the consciousness of what she had been thinking of, and what she had to tell him
point: 関係詞節の中を判定する問題。主語は which（前の内容全体）。前の his knowing her to be acquainted with it は know O to be C の動名詞形。
explanation: make O do で「O に~させる」。her が feel の主体なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: Norris felt herself defrauded of an office on which she had always depended, whether his arrival or his death were to be the thing unfolded; and was now trying to be in a bustle without having anything to bustle about, and labouring to be important where nothing was wanted but tranquillity and silence.
target: Norris felt herself defrauded of an office on which she had always depended
translation: ノリス夫人は、いつもあてにしていた役目をだまし取られたと感じていた。明かされるのが彼の到着であれ死であれ、である。そして今は、騒ぐことなど何もないのに騒いでいようとし、静けさと沈黙のほかは何も求められていないところで、偉そうにしようと骨を折っていた。
parts: defrauded of an office on which she had always depended
point: 後半の was trying to be in a bustle は SVO（try to do）。
explanation: felt herself defrauded で「自分がだまし取られたと感じた」。herself＝defrauded の関係なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: マンスフィールド・パーク

text: It was late in the morning before they returned home; and no sooner had they entered the house than Marianne flew eagerly up stairs, and when Elinor followed, she found her turning from the table with a sorrowful countenance, which declared that no Willoughby had been there.
target: she found her turning from the table with a sorrowful countenance
translation: 二人が家に戻ったのは朝も遅くなってからだった。家に入るやいなや、マリアンヌは二階へ駆け上がっていった。エリナーがあとを追うと、マリアンヌは悲しげな顔でテーブルから振り向くところだった。その顔は、ウィロビーは来なかったと告げていた。
parts: turning from the table with a sorrowful countenance
point: 前半の no sooner had they entered ~ than … は否定語が前に出た倒置。
explanation: find O ~ing で「O が~しているのに気づく」。her が turning の主体なので SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン

text: She took me in both her arms, and squeezed me to her stays until the pressure on my nose was extremely painful, though I never thought of that till afterwards when I found it very tender.
target: I found it very tender
translation: 彼女は両腕で私を抱きかかえ、コルセットに押しつけるようにぎゅっと抱きしめたので、鼻が押されてひどく痛かった。もっともそのことに気づいたのはあとになってからで、鼻がひどくひりひりするのに気づいたときだった。
point: 主節の took me（SVO）、squeezed me（SVO）と区別する。tender は「やさしい」ではなく「（触ると）痛い」。
explanation: found it very tender で「それ（鼻）がひどく痛いと気づいた」。it＝tender の関係なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
workJa: デイヴィッド・コパフィールド

text: I thought it a little too much that he should complain of being cut short in his flower after all, as if he had not been running to seed, leaf after leaf, ever since his course began.
target: I thought it a little too much that he should complain of being cut short in his flower after all
translation: 結局のところ花の盛りに断ち切られたと彼が嘆くのは、少し大げさすぎると私は思った。まるで、生まれてからずっと、葉を一枚また一枚と散らしながら種になりかけていたわけではないかのように。
parts: that he should complain of being cut short in his flower after all
point: it は仮目的語で、本当の目的語は that 節。being cut short は受動の動名詞。
explanation: thought it too much で「それを度を越していると思った」。it（＝that 節）＝too much の関係なので SVOC。
author: Charles Dickens
authorJa: チャールズ・ディケンズ
